# Changelog

All shipped features live here so the README can stay focused on what
Senkani *is*. Entries are grouped by the server version reported by
`senkani_version` (see `VersionTool.serverVersion`).

## v0.4.0 — unreleased

### May 31 — cleanup: hardened the schedule edit-in-place launchd lifecycle in `PresetInstaller.install` (3 gaps from the 2026-05-31 schedule-lifecycle PASS_WITH_GAPS re-audit). (1) **Transactional plist write** — the edit path now writes the new plist (`atomically: true`, temp-write-then-rename) BEFORE unloading the prior launchd job, so a thrown write leaves the live job armed; the old unload→write ordering disarmed the job with no rollback if the write threw (inconsistent JSON=new / plist=old / job=DOWN triple). Fresh-install (load-only) and cron→cron (unload-then-load) re-arm sequences are unchanged. (2) `ScheduleStore.removePlist` now derives its label via `plistLabel(for:)` instead of the duplicated `"com.senkani.schedule.\(name)"` literal (single source of truth). (3) NEW `ScheduledTask.isLaunchdBacked` (`eventCounterCadence == nil`) replaces the `eventCounterCadence?.isEmpty ?? true` test in `ScheduleView`'s mode-switch teardown — a malformed empty-string counter cadence (`""` vs a number) is now classified as a counter row (NOT launchd-backed), so a counter→counter edit no longer triggers a spurious `removePlist`. THREE new behavioral tests in `ScheduleLifecycleLaunchdTests` (write-failure-keeps-job-loaded via a directory-at-plist-path forcing the write to throw + asserting no `unload` recorded; `removePlist` label-path parity; `isLaunchdBacked` nil/`""`/`"5"` edge); `swift test --filter ScheduleLifecycleLaunchdTests` 13/13 green. The one remaining (pre-existing, unchanged) disarm path — `launchctl load` failing after a successful `unload`, stderr-only with no rollback/retry — is outside this item's scope and filed as a follow-up. (`schedule-install-transactional-edit-hardening-2026-05-31`)

Rather than delete it, relabeled it as a non-pane panel and moved its sidebar link into a new "Panels & overlays" group across the detail-page nav (so Settings is no longer presented as a `PaneType`); no broken links remain. (`orphan-panes-settings-html-cleanup-2026-05-31`)

### May 31 — docs: tightened the cancellation-flake test comment in `SubprocessMLXProseCadenceCompilerTests` — it now states that the timing-independent `outcome == "cancelled"` `#expect` is the PRIMARY regression detector and `elapsed < 30` is a SECONDARY sanity bound against the ~20s no-cancel sleep fallback, dropping the unproven "routinely exceeds 30s under saturation" claim. Comment-only; `swift test --filter SubprocessMLXProseCadenceCompilerTests` green. (`subprocess-mlx-cancellation-comment-precision-2026-05-31`)

The gallery parity test was named `allEntriesCoversAll18Panes` and `PaneGalleryBuilder`'s doc-comment said "17/18 pane types" — both stale against the shipped 20. Renamed + made the count enum-derived (no hardcoded literal to re-stale on the next pane). NEW `Tests/SenkaniTests/PanesReferenceDriftTests.swift` — the root-cause CI guard: parses card slugs out of `docs/reference/panes.html` and cases out of `PaneType` (read off disk via `#filePath`, the `DocsTruthGuardTests` trick, since the `SenkaniApp` target isn't test-importable), applies the two documented slug↔rawValue overrides (`schedules`↔`scheduleManager`, `served-requests`↔`openAIServedRequests`), and **fails the build** the moment the sets diverge or the on-page count stops matching the card count. The manual-audit drift that produced `website-panes-reference-out-of-sync-with-panetype-enum` can no longer recur silently. `swift test --filter "PaneGallery|PanesReferenceDrift"` green. (`panes-gallery-parity-test-stale-18-count-2026-05-31`, `panes-html-vs-panetype-ci-drift-check-2026-05-31`)

### May 31 — fix: Schedules pane edit-in-place now **re-arms the live launchd job** + tears down stale plists on mode-switch (closes the two P1s filed by the a-2 round). Editing a cron/prose schedule's cadence previously updated the JSON + plist but left the running launchd job firing the OLD cadence (`PresetInstaller.install` ran `launchctl load`, a no-op on an already-loaded label). `install` now detects a pre-existing plist and **unloads-then-(re)loads** so an edited cadence fires without a relaunch; a fresh create (no prior plist) loads only, so the create/CLI path is unchanged. launchctl is routed through a new recordable `ScheduleStore.runLaunchctl` seam, and `PresetInstaller.reload(task:)` is added as an explicit edit verb. Editing a cron/prose schedule **down to counter mode** now calls `ScheduleStore.removePlist(name)` (unload + delete plist, retain JSON) so no ghost cron job double-fires. Drag-reorder now persists order via a new optional `ScheduledTask.sortIndex` (Codable `decodeIfPresent`; `ScheduleStore.list()` sorts sortIndex-then-createdAt-then-name, legacy rows migrate gracefully) instead of overwriting `createdAt`. NEW `Tests/SenkaniTests/ScheduleLifecycleLaunchdTests.swift` — 10 **behavioral** tests (recorded launchctl verbs `[load, unload, load]` on edit vs `[load]` on create, plist removal on mode-switch, sortIndex/createdAt preservation + legacy migration). `swift build --target SenkaniApp` clean; `swift test --filter "Schedule|PresetInstaller"` 113/113 green. Re-audit (Allspaw / Kleppmann / Norman): unanimous PASS, PASS_WITH_GAPS — one accepted-risk P1 (non-transactional window if the plist write throws mid-edit; visible error, recoverable, strictly safer than before) + 2 cleanups filed as `schedule-install-transactional-edit-hardening-2026-05-31`. (`schedule-edit-in-place-launchd-rearm-2026-05-31`, `schedule-edit-mode-switch-stale-plist-2026-05-31`, `schedule-movetasks-overloads-createdat-2026-05-31`)

### May 31 — feature: Schedules pane a-2 — **edit-in-place + drag-reorder + validation tooltips**. Selecting an existing schedule reopens a-1's compose surface prefilled with its current cadence (the mode is inferred from prose/counter/cron and the prose/counter/preset/custom-cron fields are re-hydrated); saving reuses a-1's compile + `AmplificationGuard` + gating path and preserves the original `enabled`/`createdAt`/run-history so a cadence edit doesn't re-enable or wipe history. The schedule list now supports drag-to-reorder (persisted via `ScheduleStore`), and each compose field carries an inline validation tooltip surfacing the `AmplificationGuard` rationale and any compile/parse error. NEW `Tests/SenkaniTests/ScheduleViewEditReorderTests.swift` — 4 `#filePath` source-scan guards (edit-in-place, drag-reorder, validation tooltips, a-1 + list/toggle/delete regression); `swift build --target SenkaniApp` clean, `swift test --filter ScheduleView` 8/8 green (no a-1 regression). Re-audit (Sutherland / Allspaw / Norman): **PASS_WITH_GAPS** — **two P1 launchd-lifecycle defects filed, NOT yet fixed**: cron/prose edit-in-place persists the new cadence but does not unload-then-reload the live launchd job, so the running job keeps firing the OLD schedule until relaunch (`schedule-edit-in-place-launchd-rearm-2026-05-31`), and editing a cron/prose schedule down to counter mode leaves the prior plist loaded → ghost double-fire (`schedule-edit-mode-switch-stale-plist-2026-05-31`). The new tests are source-scan guards only (no behavioral launchd coverage); the drag-reorder also overloads `createdAt` for ordering (`schedule-movetasks-overloads-createdat-2026-05-31`). The groomable Cowork real-machine walk is queued separately. Branch-integrity pre-flight passed (on `main`). (`schedule-senkaniapp-pane-2026-05-21-a-2`)

### May 31 — fix: `SubprocessMLXProseCadenceCompiler` cancellation test no longer flakes under full-suite parallel load. The test "Cancellation terminates the subprocess and surfaces .cancelled (not the would-be success payload)" passes in 0.28s in isolation but blew past its `#expect(elapsed < 10.0)` ceiling to 27.9s under the 3243-test parallel load (the box is saturated; SIGTERM round-trips late, but the cancellation itself is still correct). **Fix (option i):** raised the elapsed ceiling to `30.0s` with a load-aware heuristic comment that references the finding id and names the timing-independent `outcome == "cancelled"` `#expect` as the real regression detector — the elapsed bound is only a secondary sanity check against the ~20s no-cancel sleep fallback, so 30s still distinguishes prompt-cancel from no-cancel. Test-only change to `Tests/SenkaniTests/SubprocessMLXProseCadenceCompilerTests.swift`; the other 8 SubprocessMLXProseCadenceCompiler tests unchanged. `swift test --filter SubprocessMLXProseCadenceCompilerTests` 9/9 green (cancellation test 0.275s). Re-audit (Grace / Kleppmann): PASS_CLEAN — no production/state/security surface; both agree the outcome assertion fails first if cancellation breaks. Comment-precision nit filed as `subprocess-mlx-cancellation-comment-precision-2026-05-31`. Branch-integrity pre-flight passed (on `main`). (`subprocess-mlx-cancellation-timing-flake-2026-05-30`)

### May 31 — fix: Schedules pane "New Schedule" form now writes + loads a launchd plist for cron and prose schedules — GUI-created cron/prose schedules actually fire. Closes `schedule-pane-create-form-cron-prose-no-launchd-load-2026-05-31` (the P2 follow-up filed by the a-1 round below). The bug: `ScheduleView.createSchedule()` persisted every new schedule via `ScheduleStore.save(task)`, which writes ONLY the JSON config to `~/.senkani/schedules/<name>.json` — it never wrote or loaded a launchd plist, so a cron/prose schedule created from the GUI was recorded but never fired. The CLI's `runCron` / `runProse` (`Sources/CLI/ScheduleCommand.swift`) instead route through `PresetInstaller.install(task:)`, which writes the JSON **and** renders + writes the plist to `~/Library/LaunchAgents/` and loads it with `launchctl`. The gap was pre-existing for cron; a-1 widened it to prose mode (prose also compiles to a launchd cron). **Fix:** the create-form's final persistence now branches on compose mode — cron + prose route through `PresetInstaller.install(task:)` (matching the CLI verbatim, `loadWithLaunchctl: true`); counter cadences keep `ScheduleStore.save` (they fire from `HookRouter` post-tool reactions, not launchd — the `COUNTER:` sentinel cron carries no plist, matching `ScheduleCommand.runCounterCadence`). `PresetInstaller.InstallError` (`.invalidCronPattern` / `.writeFailed`) is now caught and surfaced inline in the form's `createError` message instead of silently dropping the schedule. The a-1 `AmplificationGuard` form-side gate stays the authority (install does not re-run the guard, so no double-gating). NEW `Tests/SenkaniTests/ScheduleViewCreatePersistenceTests.swift` — 2 `@Test`: a `#filePath` source guard asserting cron/prose route through `PresetInstaller.install` and counter through `ScheduleStore.save` (anchored on the install call so it cannot match the view's other `composeMode` switches), plus a behavioral `PresetInstaller.install` round-trip (under a `ScheduleStore.withTestDirs`-isolated temp dir, `loadWithLaunchctl: false`) confirming a cron task yields BOTH a JSON config and a launchd plist on disk. Suite 3268 → 3270 (+2). `swift build --target SenkaniApp` clean (2.1s); `swift test --filter ScheduleViewCreatePersistenceTests` 2/2 green; full `swift test` 3270/3270 green (the prior-round `subprocess-mlx-cancellation-timing-flake-2026-05-30` passed under load this run). No copy change to `README.md` / `index.html` / `docs/reference/panes/schedules.html` — all already describe the Schedules pane as managing tasks "via launchd" and the form as "mirroring the `senkani schedule create` CLI flags"; this fix makes those existing claims true rather than aspirational. Re-audit (Allspaw / Sutherland): PASS — Allspaw confirms the silent-no-fire gap is closed and the `launchctl` load matches the CLI (a non-zero load only warns, but the JSON+plist now exist so it fires on next login); Sutherland confirms the persistence routing mirrors the validated task-construction switch and the `InstallError` catch precedes the generic catch with readable messages. Branch-integrity pre-flight (Step 4.5) passed — on `main`, `close.merge_target: main` matches. (`schedule-pane-create-form-cron-prose-no-launchd-load-2026-05-31`)

### May 31 — feat: the Schedules pane "New Schedule" form composes prose / counter / cron cadences with a live amplification verdict + next-fires preview + confirm-gating. Closes `schedule-senkaniapp-pane-2026-05-21-a-1` (child 1 of 2 of the Schedules-pane decomposition). The create-form was cron/preset-only; it now matches the `senkani schedule create` CLI's three cadence flags. **New:** a segmented compose-mode toggle (Prose / Counter / Cron) in `SenkaniApp/Views/ScheduleView.swift`. Prose mode compiles live as you type via an app-side `CompositeProseCadenceCompiler(rule: RuleBasedProseCadenceCompiler(), mlx: NullProseCadenceCompiler())` — common phrases resolve in-process with no model; a phrase that would need the MLX fallback shows an inline error (the app does not link the CLI's subprocess MLX arm). Counter mode parses `every N event_name` via `CounterCadence.parse` and persists the `COUNTER:` sentinel cron (HookRouter-driven, no launchd plist). Cron mode keeps the existing preset/custom picker. A live `AmplificationGuard.validate` **verdict banner** renders green (✓, fires above the 60 s floor) or red (⚠ with the reason) across all three modes; a `CronPreview.nextFires` **next-fires preview** shows the upcoming five fire times for cron + prose. The **Create** button is gated on an OK verdict via a new `canCreate` derivation — an amplifying schedule cannot submit unless the operator ticks an explicit "Override and create anyway" checkbox — and the async prose-compile/gating race is closed (Create stays disabled until `compiledProseCron` resolves; submit re-runs the guard, matching the CLI). Existing list / toggle / delete behavior unchanged. 1 new source-guard test suite `ScheduleViewComposeModeTests` (2 tests: compose-mode/banner/preview/gating declarations + list/toggle/delete regression), `#filePath`-rooted per the `ScheduleCommandListRenderTests` pattern. Suite 3266 → 3268 (+2). `swift build --target SenkaniApp` clean (10.6 s); `swift test --filter ScheduleViewComposeModeTests` 2/2 green; full `swift test` 3267/3268 — the single failure is the **already-filed** load-induced flake `subprocess-mlx-cancellation-timing-flake-2026-05-30` (`SubprocessMLXProseCadenceCompilerTests` cancellation test, 13.5 s > 10 s ceiling under parallel load; passes 0.28 s in isolation — confirmed re-run green), unrelated to this change. Re-audit (Sutherland / Allspaw / Norman): PASS — Sutherland confirms the verdict + preview recompute live from `@State`-derived computed properties; Allspaw confirms the compile/gating race is closed and every compiler error surfaces inline; Norman confirms icon+text+color banner (not color alone) and an explicit override affordance. **Follow-up filed** (`schedule-pane-create-form-cron-prose-no-launchd-load-2026-05-31`, P2): the create-form persists via `ScheduleStore.save` (JSON only) — GUI-created cron/prose schedules never write/load a launchd plist (the CLI uses `PresetInstaller.install`), a pre-existing gap a-1 widened to prose mode; outside a-1's acceptance. Branch-integrity pre-flight (Step 4.5) passed — on `main`, `close.merge_target: main` matches. (`schedule-senkaniapp-pane-2026-05-21-a-1`)

### May 30 — fix: ⌘K-launched panes now get the gallery's clean `defaultTitle`, not `typeId.capitalized`. Closes `command-palette-addpanebytypeid-ugly-titles-2026-05-30` (the follow-up filed by the dead-click round below). The bug: `ContentView.addPaneByTypeId` titled a new pane with `typeId.capitalized`, which uppercases the first letter and **lowercases the rest of each word**, so a camelCase gallery id collapsed to one mangled word — `artifactGallery` → "Artifactgallery", `openAIServedRequests` → "Openaiservedrequests", `skillLibrary` → "Skilllibrary". The **same pane** launched from the Add-Pane sheet got the clean `defaultTitle` ("Artifacts") because `AddPaneSheet` passes `entry.defaultTitle` directly — one pane, two names, depending on launch path. `defaultTitle` already exists on every `PaneGalleryEntry` for exactly this purpose. **Fix:** NEW `PaneGalleryBuilder.defaultTitle(forLaunchID:)` Core resolver (`Sources/Core/PaneGalleryBuilder.swift`) — `allEntries().first(where:{ $0.id == id })?.defaultTitle`. `ContentView.addPaneByTypeId` now titles via `PaneGalleryBuilder.defaultTitle(forLaunchID: typeId) ?? typeId.capitalized`, so both launch surfaces resolve the SAME title; the `.capitalized` fallback survives only as a never-reached safety net (the `launchMapMatchesGallery` parity test guarantees every `launchMap` key has a gallery entry). The `terminal` special-case branch is dropped — its `defaultTitle` is already "Terminal". Title resolution lifted to Core so it is unit-testable (the title path lives in the non-importable `SenkaniApp` target). 3 new `PaneGalleryTests`: `everyLaunchIDResolvesToNonEmptyDefaultTitle` (every `launchMap` key → non-nil, non-empty title), `camelCaseLaunchIDsResolveToCleanTitles` (regression pin: the six camelCase ids resolve to their clean titles, not `.capitalized`), `unknownLaunchIDResolvesToNil` (fallback contract). `PaneGalleryTests` 14 → 17 (+3, total suite 3263 → 3266). `swift test --filter 'PaneGallery|CommandPalette'` → 26/26 green; `swift build --target SenkaniApp` clean (2.0s); `swift test --filter LaunchCoordinatorRoutingTests` 6/6 (ContentView source-guards intact); full `swift test` 3266/3266 green. No copy change to `index.html` / `docs/reference/panes.html` / `README.md` — a cosmetic title-resolution fix on one launch path changes no documented surface (the landing-page "what's listed is what launches" claim is launch-parity, not titles). Re-audit (Norman / Lauret): PASS — Norman confirms the dual-name consistency violation is structurally closed (same pane, same title, any launch path); Lauret confirms the Core resolver mirrors the `launchMap` single-source-of-truth pattern and avoids a third hand-mirror. Branch-integrity pre-flight (Step 4.5) passed — on `main`, `close.merge_target: main` matches. (`command-palette-addpanebytypeid-ugly-titles-2026-05-30`)

### May 30 — fix: ⌘K "New Artifact Gallery" no longer a dead click + gallery↔launch parity is now CI-enforced. Closes `command-palette-artifact-gallery-dead-click-2026-05-30` (filed by the a-3 round below). The bug: `artifactGallery` shipped in `PaneGalleryBuilder.allEntries()` (so the ⌘K palette advertised "New Artifact Gallery") but was **missing** from `ContentView.addPaneByTypeId`'s hand-maintained `typeMap`, so selecting it hit `guard … else { return }` and silently no-op'd — violating the palette's own "never display a row that does nothing" honesty contract. Root cause class: the string→`PaneType` launch map was hand-mirrored across two app-target surfaces (`ContentView.addPaneByTypeId`, `AddPaneSheet.idToType`) with **no parity test**, because both live in the non-importable `SenkaniApp` executable target. **Fix:** lifted the canonical launch binding into Core as `PaneGalleryBuilder.launchMap` (`[galleryId: PaneTypeRawValue]`, `Sources/Core/PaneGalleryBuilder.swift`) — single source of truth. Both app launchers now DERIVE their `[String: PaneType]` from it (`ContentView.addPaneByTypeId` resolves `launchMap[id]` → `PaneType(rawValue:)`; `AddPaneSheet.idToType` is `launchMap.compactMapValues(PaneType.init(rawValue:))` with a DEBUG `assert` catching any raw value that doesn't resolve — the one invariant Core can't see since it can't import `PaneType`), so the two surfaces can no longer drift from each other or from the gallery. NEW `PaneGalleryTests.launchMapMatchesGallery` asserts `Set(allEntries().map(\.id)) == Set(launchMap.keys)` both directions — fails CI the instant a gallery id has no launch path (or vice-versa). `PaneGalleryTests` 13 → 14 (+1, total suite 3262 → 3263). `swift test --filter 'PaneGallery|CommandPalette'` → 23/23 green; `swift build --target SenkaniApp` clean (2.1s); full `swift test` green modulo the pre-existing `subprocess-mlx-cancellation-timing-flake-2026-05-30` flake (P2 load-induced timing, passes 0.28s isolated — not a regression). The landing-page claim (`index.html`: "what's listed is what launches") and `docs/reference/panes.html` ⌘K copy are now honest and test-backed (no copy change needed). Re-audit (Lauret / Norman): PASS — Lauret confirms one tested Core source eliminates the two-map drift class; Norman confirms the dead-click honesty violation is structurally closed. Branch-integrity pre-flight (Step 4.5) passed — on `main`, `close.merge_target: main` matches. Follow-up filed: `command-palette-addpanebytypeid-ugly-titles-2026-05-30` — the ⌘K launch path titles panes via `typeId.capitalized` ("Artifactgallery", "Openaiservedrequests") instead of the gallery's `defaultTitle`, surfaced by this round's audit outside its acceptance. (`command-palette-artifact-gallery-dead-click-2026-05-30`)

### May 30 — feature: V.13 GUI a-2 — `OpenAIServedRequestsPane` now live-refreshes on a 500ms poll (no reactive SQLite seam). Second child of the 3-way decomposition of `phase-v13-gui-agent-timeline-consumer-2026-05-28`. a-1 rendered an appear-time snapshot only; a-2 wraps that read in a 500ms poll lifecycle — the pane refreshes every 500ms while visible (`onAppear` start, `onDisappear` stop), matching `AgentTimelinePane`'s pattern verbatim. There is deliberately NO reactive SQLite-change-notification seam (operator decompose decision 2026-05-30, Q3 — a 500ms poll is sufficient and adds no producer/write path). **Architecture:** the store read + poll loop are extracted into a new importable `Core.OpenAIServedRequestsPoller` (`@Observable @MainActor`) for the same reason a-1's presentation logic lives in `Core.OpenAIServedRequestsPresenter` — the SwiftUI view is an executable-target type that `SenkaniTests` cannot `@testable import`, so the poll lifecycle (cadence, cancellation, no-drop wholesale read) is exercised against the Core poller. The view becomes a thin shell that owns an `@State` poller, binds `poller.rows`, and drives `start()`/`stop()`. The poll loop is generic over a `Clock` so tests inject an advance-time clock instead of waiting 500ms of wall time; production passes `ContinuousClock`. Each tick re-reads `recentOpenAIRequests(limit: 100)` wholesale — the persisted store is the single truth source, so a 100-request burst renders in full with no row dropped. Cancellation (from `onDisappear`) throws out of the in-flight `sleep` so the poll task unwinds rather than leaking a parked task. 3 new `@Test` added to `Tests/SenkaniTests/OpenAIServedRequestsPaneTests.swift` (a new persisted row appears after exactly one 500ms interval, driven by a manual advance-time `ManualClock`; `onDisappear` cancels the poll task with no leak — `await`-ing the task's unwind returns promptly, `isCancelled` holds, no sleeper continuation stays parked; a 100-row burst renders without dropping a single id); the a-1 `viewSourceGuard` test updated — the `Task.sleep`-absence guard moved into Core, and the guard now asserts the view wires the poll lifecycle (`OpenAIServedRequestsPoller`, `poller.start()`/`.onAppear`, `poller.stop()`/`.onDisappear`). `OpenAIServedRequestsPaneTests` 7 → 10 (+3). `swift test --filter OpenAIServedRequestsPaneTests` → 10/10; full `swift test` green modulo the pre-existing `subprocess-mlx-cancellation-timing-flake-2026-05-30` flake (P2, load-induced timing, not a regression from this round). a-3 (pane-catalog registration + accessibility) remains.

### May 30 — feature: V.13 (sub-item 2) — `StreamingChatEngine` seam + MCP-side MLX streaming chat adapter + `ServeCommand` SSE delta rewire. Real token-by-token Gemma 4 SSE deltas now back `senkani serve --openai`'s streaming chat path when the MCP target is active; absent that, the streamHandler falls through to v13b's collected-then-chunk path. NEW `public protocol StreamingChatEngine: Sendable` at `Sources/Core/OpenAIEndpoint/StreamingChatEngine.swift` (one method returning `AsyncThrowingStream<OpenAIChatHandler.TokenDelta, Error>` — first async-stream shape in the OpenAIEndpoint surface); NEW `OpenAIChatHandler.TokenDelta` (Core-side `Sendable` struct: `content: String` + optional forward-compat `finishReason: String?`); NEW `OpenAIChatHandler.StreamingEngine` injectable wrapper mirroring the existing `OpenAIChatHandler.Engine` shape; NEW `OpenAIChatHandler.renderStreamingEvents(id:created:model:source:) -> AsyncThrowingStream<Data, Error>` — translates `TokenDelta` deltas into SSE-framed chunks (leading role chunk + one content chunk per non-empty delta + terminal `finish_reason: "stop"`; empty-content deltas elided so a bursty MLX run can't emit empty SSE events); NEW `ModelManager.registerStreamingChatHandler(_:)` + `resolvedStreamingChatHandler() -> (any StreamingChatEngine)?` slot at `Sources/Core/ModelManager.swift` mirroring `registerChatHandler` (lock-protected, idempotent). `OpenAIChatStream.Plan` gains an alternate `init(head:streamingEvents:done:onFinish:)` carrying a `(@Sendable () -> AsyncThrowingStream<Data, Error>)?` source; `OpenAIChatStream.run(plan:, sink:)` dispatches on plan shape (pre-baked `events: [Data]` v13b path vs. new `streamingEvents` v13 sub-item 2 path). NEW private `OpenAIChatStream.driveStreaming(...)` bridges the async event source to the listener's synchronous `Sink` contract: a producer Task pulls deltas from the upstream source and pushes them to a bounded NSLock+DispatchSemaphore channel; the drive loop drains the channel and writes each event through the sink, with bidirectional cancellation (peer disconnect → sink-write throw → producer Task cancel via `onTermination`; producer error → channel `.error` → drive returns `.clientCancel`; sink-`isCancelled` check before every wait). NEW `MLXStreamingChatEngineAdapter: StreamingChatEngine` + `MLXChatEngine.stream(prompt:) -> AsyncThrowingStream<String, Error>` in `Sources/MCP/ChatHandlerRegistration.swift` running real on-device Gemma 4 token-stream inference (mirrors `MLXChatEngine.complete(prompt:)` byte-for-byte except yields each `Generation.chunk` to the continuation instead of accumulating, and skips the end-of-stream `trimmingCharacters` since the streaming path can't unwrite earlier deltas — clients accumulate `delta.content` verbatim as MLX produces it, documented trade-off). Shared `MLXChatPrompt.assemble(messages:)` extracted so non-streaming + streaming adapters can't drift on prompt shape. `ChatHandlerRegistration.register()` now registers both `MLXChatEngineAdapter` + `MLXStreamingChatEngineAdapter` at MCP startup. `Sources/CLI/ServeCommand.swift`'s `streamHandler` rewires the non-tool-use content-stream path through the registered `StreamingChatEngine` when present: an NSLock-protected accumulator tees each delta so the `chatStream` audit entry's `completionTokenCount` reflects what actually streamed (vs v13b's pre-computed `result.auditFields.completionTokenCount`); tool-use streams (`OpenAIChatHandler.requestUsesTools(request) == true`) + unregistered-handler runs keep the v13b collected-then-chunk path verbatim — preserves the v13d-1 tool-call delta contract + the unit-test stability the legacy fallback gives test environments that don't start MCP. `Sources/Core/` MLX-import-free invariant preserved (`grep -rE '^import MLX' Sources/Core/` returns empty). `OpenAIChatHandler.requestSummary` promoted internal → public so the streaming audit-body capture can reuse the same documented sanitizer the non-streaming path uses. NEW `Tests/SenkaniTests/OpenAIChatStreamingEngineTests.swift` ships 5 `@Test` functions covering the seam in isolation (no MLX runtime required): (1) `testSseShapeFromStubSource` — feeds a deterministic stub `["Hello", " from", " the", " stream"]` source through `renderStreamingEvents` and asserts role chunk + 4 content chunks + terminal `finish_reason: "stop"` (byte-prefix `data: ` + suffix `\n\n` checks per chunk); (2) `testEmptyStreamEmitsRoleAndTerminal` — an empty source still emits role + terminal only; (3) `testEmptyContentDeltaSkipped` — TokenDeltas with empty content are skipped, not rendered as empty `data: {}` events; (4) `testStreamingPlanMatchesPreBakedPlan` — feeds `OpenAIChatStream.splitForStreaming(content)` slices through the new streaming Plan path and asserts the byte sequence delivered to a `Buffer` sink is identical to `Plan(events:)` on the same content — proves the new path is a drop-in for the v13b shape; (5) `testStreamingDriveCancelsOnSinkCancel` — a sink that cancels after the first write returns `.clientCancel`, the onFinish status captures `.clientCancel`, `close()` is called exactly once, and only the head was written. NEW `testStreamingDeltasArriveOverTime` `@Test` added to the existing `OpenAIChatRealEngineTests` suite — best-effort real-model probe with deterministic prompt (`"Name three primary colors."`), records inter-delta wall-clock gaps during a real Gemma 4 stream and logs `[v13-chat-finding]` to stderr when fewer than 3 distinct delta timestamps are captured OR the inter-delta max gap exceeds 5s; composite skip on no-Gemma-tier-downloaded + no-StreamingChatEngine-registered (the test target links Core only — MCP isn't started during `swift test`; the @Test exists to detect "deltas bunched at the end" regressions on operator integration walks). All 16 `OpenAIChatStreamTests` (v13b stream + v13d-1 tool-call deltas) continue green (no tool-call streaming regression). `swift build` clean; `swift test --filter "OpenAI"` 116/116 green; `swift test --filter "OpenAIChatStreamingEngineTests"` 5/5 green; full `swift test` 3237 → 3243 (+6 new: 5 stub + 1 real-engine; one pre-existing unrelated `SubprocessMLXProseCadenceCompiler` cancellation timing flake under heavy parallel-test load filed as a follow-up — see below). Re-audit (Lauret / Karpathy / Schneier): PASS — Lauret confirms the streaming seam mirrors the v13a-1 `ChatEngine` pattern + `OpenAIChatStream.Plan`'s dual-init carrier is clearly documented; Karpathy confirms MLX `container.generate` natively yields `Generation.chunk` so plumbing through to `AsyncThrowingStream` is a natural fit, the no-trim-on-streaming trade-off is the right call (clients reconstruct full content from deltas, sampler whitespace at edges is acceptable), and tool-call streams correctly route to the v13b path; Schneier confirms `onFinish` still fires exactly once per stream via `OpenAIChatStream.run`'s close discipline, audit-chain shape unchanged (`surface: "chat"` chained row), accumulator-based completion-token-count reflects actual streamed bytes (no token-count drift), and `requestSummary` raised to public is a no-scope-expansion change (the helper was already a documented sanitizer for the audit `request_body` column). Out of scope (covered by V.13 sub-items 3-4): non-local-tier 503s + readiness 503 + tokenizer-accurate usage (a-3), full v13a-3 audit-chain regression sweep + real-engine SLO smoke test + durable `CoreModuleBoundaryTests.testCoreContainsNoMLXImports` + V-operator-surface row flip (a-4). The adapter bridges to a new `EmbedEngine.embedStrings(_:)` method that runs the SAME MLX tokenize → pad → pool path `EmbedEngine.indexProject` uses (same `MLXInferenceLock.shared` serialization, same memory-pressure unload registration), so the `senkani_embed` MCP tool and the OpenAI `/v1/embeddings` surface share a single embedding stack rooted at `ModelManager.embeddingModelID = "minilm-l6"` — no parallel implementation. `ServeCommand` resolves the registered handler at startup and prints `openai-serve embeddings_backend=mcp_handler|placeholder` so operators can verify which path serves: when registered, request flow checks `ModelManager.shared.isReady(minilm-l6)` and returns a framed `HTTP 503` with `error.type: "model_not_available"` pointing at the Models pane / `senkani doctor` if not downloaded (Q2 scope-groom 2026-05-28 — no auto-pull on the hot request path); when unregistered (e.g. listener started without the MCP startup hook, or in unit tests), falls back to v13c's `Serve.placeholderEmbeddingsEngine()` and logs the unregistered state once at startup so test environments stay self-contained without an MCP wiring. The bridge is sync (`OpenAIEmbeddingsServeBridge.syncEngine(for:)`) so the existing listener closure signature stays unchanged — a `DispatchSemaphore` waits on the listener thread while a `Task` runs MLX inference under the shared lock; cleaner than refactoring the listener to async, and the listener thread's brief block is already implicit in the global Metal serialization. `usage.prompt_tokens` now reflects the REAL `Tokenizer.encode(...)` count (summed across batched inputs), not v13c's `OpenAIChatHandler.estimateTokens` ~4-chars/token heuristic — matches the chat-engine arc's tokenizer-accuracy posture. Vector dimensionality stays at 384 (MiniLM-L6 native; the placeholder already returned 384-dim so well-behaved clients see no shape change). Audit-chain shape is unchanged: exactly one entry per request, `surface: "embeddings"`, `completion_token_count: 0`, input text NEVER in audit fields. Process model is in-process (~90 MB resident MiniLM next to any chat-tier work, gated by the global lock; memory-pressure unload reuses `EmbedEngine`'s existing handler registration). Install-size posture preserved: `grep -r "^import MLX" Sources/Core/` returns zero hits — the new protocol is pure-Swift String/struct passing, the bridge is `Foundation` only, the registration adapter lives in `Sources/MCP/` (MCP target already linked MLX), so the CLI binary's MLX-symbol count is unchanged from the u8b-mlx-prose-subprocess-delegation baseline (~51.88 MiB unstripped; the 50 MiB SLO breach remains owned by `slo-install-size-unstripped-exceeds-50mb-threshold-2026-05-27`'s strip-vs-revise scope-groom, not widened by this round). `Tests/SenkaniTests/EmbeddingEngineRegistrationTests.swift` ships 6 `@Test` functions covering the seam in isolation (no MLX model required in CI): (1) registration round-trip through a custom `ModelManager` instance; (2) sync-bridge vector + real-tokenizer-count pass-through against a recorded 384-dim fixture; (3) sync-bridge error path returns an empty embedding when the underlying handler throws (production path is gated by `isReady` upstream so this is defense-in-depth); (4) readiness gate returns framed 503 with `error.type: "model_not_available"` + Models pane / `senkani doctor` hint when not ready; (5) readiness gate returns nil when ready (caller dispatches normally); (6) end-to-end registered-handler path → `OpenAIEmbeddingsHandler.handle` produces valid OpenAI list response + audit entry with the bridge's tokenizer count flowing through to `usage.prompt_tokens` / `usage.total_tokens`. Real on-device fidelity (cosine similarity to a fixture vector against the actual downloaded MiniLM, plus `curl POST /v1/embeddings` round-trip end-to-end including the 503 path with a partial-state `ModelManager`) is covered by the manual-log walk fired via the item's `manual_validation_needed` `affects:` tag — CI can verify the seam shape; only a real-machine pass with the model downloaded can verify the inference fidelity. v13c's `OpenAIEmbeddingsTests` (8 tests) continue passing unchanged against the registered-handler path — the audit-chain regression bullet holds: same surface name, same body shape, same chain count per request. `swift build` clean; `swift test --filter "OpenAIEmbeddings|EmbeddingEngine"` 14/14 green. ### May 28 — feature: U.8b follow-up — `MLX prose path moves off the senkani CLI binary` — subprocess-delegation closes the install-size SLO breach u8b-5 (2026-05-28) filed: the `senkani` binary no longer links `MLXLMCommon` + `MLXVLM`. Production `CompositeProseCadenceCompiler`'s MLX arm swaps from in-process `MLXProseCadenceCompiler` to a new `SubprocessMLXProseCadenceCompiler` (in the CLI target, no MLX import) that shells out to a new `senkani-mcp prose` argv-mode handler (`Sources/MCPMain/ProseSubprocessHandler.swift`) over stdin/stdout JSON. Wire contract: request `{"protocol_version": 1, "prose": "...", "locale": "..."}` on stdin; response `{"cron": "..."}` (exit 0) or `{"error": {"kind": "...", "detail": "..."}}` (exit 1) on stdout. Error `kind` discriminator (`unavailable` / `invalidJSON` / `invalidCron` / `cancelled` / `unrecognizedPhrase` / `unsupportedLocale` / `version` / `spawn`) translates to the closed `ProseCadenceCompilerError` taxonomy on the CLI side; unknown kinds fold to `.unavailable` for forward-compat. Wire-protocol versioned at v1 so mixed-install scenarios (a v0.4.0 `senkani` against a v0.5.0 `senkani-mcp`) get a clean rejection instead of silent drift. Cancellation wired via `withTaskCancellationHandler { … } onCancel: { process.terminate() }` — a cancelled Task SIGTERMs the subprocess and surfaces `.cancelled` (cancellation test confirms <1s settle vs the fake-binary's 20s sleep, critical because a Gemma cold-load can be 5–15 s). Subprocess stderr is piped + discarded so the helper's `senkani.prose: Gemma VLM loaded` log line doesn't leak to the CLI's stderr stream. `Sources/CLI/ScheduleCommand.swift` drops `import MLXProseCompiler`; `Package.swift` removes `"MLXProseCompiler"` from the CLI executable target's deps and adds it to `SenkaniMCP` (net-zero on senkani-mcp's install size — that binary already linked MLX via MCPServer's embed + vision tools). Binary discovery reuses `MLEval.discoverMCPBinary()` (same-dir / .build/release / .build/debug / PATH lookup) — no new discovery surface. The rule arm of `CompositeProseCadenceCompiler` continues to handle common cadences in sub-ms and never reaches the subprocess; only irregular prose like `every other Tuesday at 6pm` pays the ~10–50 ms subprocess launch overhead, on top of the 0.5–2 s Gemma inference cost — so subprocess overhead is under 5% of total `--prose` latency. **Install-size measurement post-swap**: `stat -f%z .build/release/senkani` reports 54,402,936 bytes ≈ 51.88 MiB unstripped, **a 40 MiB reduction from u8b-5's 92 MiB baseline**; `nm` confirms **0** MLX framework symbols (`MLXLMCommon` / `MLXVLM` / `MLXEmbedders` / `VLMModelFactory` / `MLXNN` / `MLXFast` / `MLXRandom`) in the CLI binary — the MLX-link-into-CLI delta is fully closed, which was this round's explicit scope per the parent's `## Install-size note`. The remaining ~2 MiB of unstripped overhead vs the strict 50 MiB SLO line is non-MLX (tree-sitter parsers, Foundation / ArgumentParser, Bench / Bundle / Indexer); `strip -x` resolves it (stripped: 47.27 MB / 45.08 MiB < 50 MB threshold). The stripping decision continues to live under the open `slo-install-size-unstripped-exceeds-50mb-threshold-2026-05-27` (strip-vs-revise — operator scope-groom not yet completed). NEW `Tests/SenkaniTests/SubprocessMLXProseCadenceCompilerTests.swift` ships 9 `@Test` functions: 4 decoder unit tests (`decodeCron` returns cron on exit 0, 9-case wire-`kind` translation matrix, malformed-stdout → `.unavailable` fallback, exit-0-without-`cron`-field → `.invalidJSON`, exit-143 SIGTERM → `.cancelled`); 4 subprocess integration tests using `#!/bin/sh` fake binaries mirroring the `MLEvalCommandTests` harness (success returns `ProseCadence` with caller's prose + locale + helper's cron, error envelope translates end-to-end, missing binary → `.unavailable`); 1 cancellation test (Task.cancel() while subprocess sleeps 20s — outcome `.cancelled` in <1s). `Tests/SenkaniTests/ScheduleCommandProseTests.swift` `proseNonEnglishLocaleRefusesNoDiskTrace` updated to inject a deterministic Composite(rule, MockMLX) so the test no longer depends on `.build/debug/senkani-mcp` being built (which `swift test` does not do); doc-comment on `compositeConstructionDoesNotLoadGemma` updated to clarify probe-2 (the `MLXProseCadenceCompiler` actor's `ensureModelCallCountForTesting == 0` assertion) is now independent MLXProseCompiler-module coverage, not a direct test of the production factory's MLX arm. `swift build` clean in 12.1 s; `swift build -c release` clean in 13.2 s; `./tools/test-safe.sh` 8/8 chunks green (`other` chunk 1634 → 1643, +9). MLX-side errors propagate unchanged so the operator sees clear messages (`"no MLX model installed; pass --cron"` / `"model output unparseable"` / `"model emitted invalid cron"`). ### May 27 — feature: V.13e gate-refusal → persisted request-log recording — closes the `429-rate` gap the listener-wiring round left open. The listener-wiring round below made `requests (24h)` reflect real *successful* traffic, but the rate-limited (`429`) and auth-refused (`401` / `403`) responses are emitted by `OpenAIAuthGate` **before** any surface handler runs — they short-circuit at the gate, so they reached NEITHER the in-memory `OpenAIAuditChain` NOR the persisted `openai_request_log`. Consequence: `OpenAIRequestLogStore.trailing24hStats` computes `429-rate = count429 / count24h`, but no live producer ever wrote a `status: 429` row, so the v13e-2 doctor line's `429-rate` was structurally `0.0%` regardless of real rejected traffic. NEW `OpenAIServedRequestSink.recordRefusal(decision:path:authorizationHeader:records:db:now:)` (`Sources/Core/OpenAIEndpoint/OpenAIServedRequestSink.swift`) records one **metadata-only** persisted row per refusal at the single point the gate decides: `401` → `keyLabel: nil` (missing / unknown / expired / malformed — no label leak), `403` → the matched key's label (scope miss, not identity), `429` → the matched key's label (per-key limit). Surface is path-derived via `OpenAIAuthGate.surface(forPath:)` (`/v1/chat*` → `.chat`, `/v1/embeddings` → `.embeddings`; a surface-less `/v1/*` path falls back to `.chat`, and since `429-rate` counts `status = 429` across all rows it is surface-agnostic). `Sources/CLI/ServeCommand.swift`'s authenticator closure (which calls `decide` exactly once per `/v1/*` request) now calls the recorder right after the decision, so exactly one row lands per refused request with no double-count. **Deliberate asymmetry:** refusals are NOT appended to the in-memory chain (they never were — that chain is the per-served-request log; the persisted store is the cross-process observability log), so the v13e-5 burst-integrity test's chain semantics are unaffected. **Privacy:** the raw key is never recorded — only the matched record's `label`, re-derived via the gate's constant-time `matchRecord`. 1 new test (`OpenAIRequestLogStoreTests.gateRefusalsRecordPersistedRowsAndDrive429Rate`) drives all three refusal kinds (the `429` through a real `decide` over an exhausted rate window) plus an `.ok` no-op, and asserts one row per refusal, the right status / path-derived surface / key-label policy, no raw key on disk, and a then-non-zero `count429` / `rate429`. `./tools/test-safe.sh` 8/8 chunks green (chunk[other] 1614 → 1615, +1). `docs/reference/cli/senkani-doctor.html` updated — the "`429-rate` still reads `0.0%` until … a tracked follow-up" sentence is replaced with the landed recording description. Re-audit (Lauret / Karpathy / Schneier): PASS clean; one quality observation filed (`openai-refusal-surface-attribution-surfaceless-path-2026-05-27` — surface-less `/v1/*` refusals attribute to `.chat`). Branch-integrity pre-flight (Step 4.5) passed — on `main`. (`openai-429-path-not-recorded-to-request-log-2026-05-27`)

### May 27 — fix: `install.size` release-commitment SLO now measures the shipped artifact, not the `.build/release` symlink (reported `0.0`). `tools/measure-slos.sh` measured `install.size` with `du -sk .build/release`, but SwiftPM leaves `.build/release` as a **symlink** to `.build/<triple>/release` — and `du -sk` of a symlink reports the ~0 KB link, not its target. Every captured row recorded `install_size_mb: 0.0`, which read as a false `ok` against the 50 MB gate (the SLO was effectively unmeasured). Worse, `du -sk -L` of the resolved target is ~1.8 GB of build intermediates (`*.build`, object files, ModuleCache), not the artifact. The measurement is now extracted into a single-source-of-truth helper `tools/measure-install-size.sh` (called by `measure-slos.sh`) that resolves the release dir through its symlink and **sums the shipped executable products** (`senkani`, `senkani-mcp`, `senkani-hook`, `senkani-mig-helper`) — excluding both the build intermediates and the SenkaniApp GUI bundle (which ships as a separate `.app` via DMG, not a CLI product). A measurement miss prints `null`, not an error, so the script's "never abort a run" contract holds. A clean release build now yields `install_size_mb: 151.7` (was `0.0`). 1 new `@Test` (`ReleaseSLOInstallSizeMeasurementTests`: shells out to the helper against a fixture symlink tree, asserts the link is followed → non-zero and that intermediates/non-products are excluded → < 1 MB for ~0.4 MB of fixture products; missing dir → `null`); ReleaseSLO suite 8 → 9, green. `spec/slos.md` recipe + table updated; `docs/reference/cli/senkani-doctor.html` install.size description corrected from "`du -sk` of the release directory". Re-audit (Lauret / Karpathy / Schneier): PASS. **Finding (outside criteria, filed):** the honest unstripped product-binary sum (~150 MB) exceeds the published `< 50 MB` threshold — the gate is now correctly red against an unmet commitment instead of falsely green at 0.0; reconciling strip-vs-threshold is filed as `slo-install-size-unstripped-exceeds-50mb-threshold-2026-05-27`. Branch-integrity pre-flight (Step 4.5) passed — on `main`. (`measure-slos-install-size-symlink-du-2026-05-27`, `phase-v13e-3-slo-cold-start` build-round Finding)

### May 27 — feature: `openai.cold.start` release-commitment SLO — `senkani serve --openai` spawn → listener-ready p95 (V.13e-3). `tools/measure-slos.sh` gains a fifth release-commitment measurement: it launches `senkani serve --openai --port 0` (ephemeral loopback port, no keys, no network bind), times from process spawn until the listener **accepts a TCP connection**, SIGKILLs it, and repeats N=10 (one discarded warm-up cycle first) for a p95 — same linear-interpolation recipe as the CLI `cold.start`. **Readiness is detected by polling the port with `connect()`, not by reading the "listening on" startup log**, because Swift's `print()` block-buffers stdout when it is a pipe (the line never flushes until exit, so a live stdout read hangs) — the connect-poll measures the true bind-ready edge and the SIGKILL teardown needs no graceful drain. The new field `openai_cold_start_ms_p95` is appended to each `~/.senkani/slo-history.jsonl` row; `ReleaseSLORow` decodes it (pre-V.13e-3 rows backfill to `nil` — backward compatible) and `ReleaseSLOName.openaiColdStart` (threshold < 1500 ms p95) makes it a gated, doctor-surfaced SLO. `spec/slos.md` gains the row + measurement recipe; a real baseline row (`openai_cold_start_ms_p95: 7.3` on this machine) is committed at `tools/slo-baseline.jsonl`. New flags `--openai-runs N` / `--skip-openai`. 1 new `@Test` (`ReleaseSLOTests.openaiColdStartRowAppendedAndEvaluated`: field decodes, pre-V.13e-3 row backfills nil, under-threshold → ok, over-threshold → overBudget); ReleaseSLO suite 7 → 8. Full `./tools/test-safe.sh` 8/8 chunks green (no regression, 1606 in the largest chunk). Re-audit (Lauret / Karpathy / Schneier): PASS — measurement is graceful (null field, never aborts the run) when the binary is absent or the endpoint never binds; loopback-only, short-lived, zero requests land on the socket. **Finding (outside criteria, filed):** `install.size` measures `du -sk` of the `.build/release` **symlink** (reports 0) instead of its target — filed as `measure-slos-install-size-symlink-du-2026-05-27`. ### May 27 — hardening: live OpenAI-endpoint key reload + sealed disk store (V.13a-2 follow-up). Two findings from the v13a-2 build round, both outside its acceptance, now closed. **(1) Live key reload.** `senkani serve --openai` read a START-TIME key snapshot, so a key provisioned (or revoked) with `senkani vault add/remove openai-key` while the server was already running silently `401`'d (or stayed valid) until a restart. The serve authenticator + chat/embeddings/stream handlers now read a LIVE `OpenAIKeyRecordSnapshot` per request — mid-serve provisioning takes effect, and revocation de-authorizes, without a restart. Cost is bounded: the on-disk `~/.senkani/openai-keys.json` is re-read only when its `(mtime, size)` advances (one `stat` per request in steady state). **(2) Sealed disk store.** `JSONFileKeychainStore` persists base64 (NOT encrypted) to a 0600 JSON file; as a general `KeychainStore` a future caller could have wired it for a scope holding actual SECRETS and silently leaked plaintext. It is now SEALED to a single non-secret scope (`openai-endpoint` by default) — `read`/`write`/`delete`/`list` throw `JSONFileKeychainStore.ScopeViolation` for any other scope, so misuse is loud, not silent (secrets still belong in the macOS Keychain store, T.4c). The v13a-2 0600 + hash-only-on-disk invariants are regression-guarded, and `loadAllSync` (the snapshot's synchronous reader) is asserted equivalent to the async `loadAll`. 4 new `@Test` functions (`OpenAIKeyVaultHardeningTests`); full `./tools/test-safe.sh` green (8/8 chunks, 1595 tests). Re-audit (Lauret / Karpathy / Schneier): PASS — torn-read ruled out (the store persists via temp-file + atomic rename, so a concurrent snapshot read sees the old or new complete file, never a partial write). Branch-integrity pre-flight (Step 4.5) passed — on `main`. (`process-gap-v13a-2-openai-key-vault-persistence-hardening-2026-05-27`, V.13a-2 build-round follow-up)

### May 27 — feature: streaming `tool_calls` deltas (SSE) for tool-use requests (V.13d-1, follow-up to V.13d). V.13d shipped tool-use on the non-streaming chat path and deferred "streaming-of-tool-calls deltas"; a `stream: true` + tools request rode v13b's content-chunk path, and because a tool-call completion's content is empty, **the tool call was dropped from the SSE stream** — a streaming client that declared tools saw only an empty `[DONE]`. This closes the gap: a valid, in-scope `stream: true` tool-use request now emits OpenAI-shaped `choices[].delta.tool_calls[]` fragments. NEW `OpenAIChatStream.toolCallEvents(…)` emits a leading `{role: "assistant"}` chunk, then per tool call a **header fragment** carrying `{index, id, type: "function", function: {name, arguments: ""}}` followed by one `function.arguments` string fragment per `splitForStreaming` piece (the fragments concatenate byte-for-byte back to the full JSON-encoded arguments string, mirroring the content-delta invariant), and a terminal chunk with `finish_reason: "tool_calls"` before `data: [DONE]`. NEW `OpenAIChatStream.Chunk.Delta.ToolCallFragment` (sparse-encoded — `index` ALWAYS present so a client keys fragments by array index; `id`/`type`/`function.name` only on the first fragment for an index). **No parallel streaming stack:** the tool-call path reuses the same `Chunk` model, `run(…)` drive loop, `Sink` contract, and `splitForStreaming` splitter as v13b's content path; `ServeCommand`'s `streamHandler` branches on `message.toolCalls` to pick `toolCallEvents` vs `events`. **Scope-gate parity preserved (Schneier):** an out-of-scope or malformed `stream: true` tool-use request still funnels through `toolsPreflightError` → returns a nil plan → the listener renders the framed `403 insufficient_scope` (or `400`) BEFORE any `text/event-stream` byte (no half-open SSE). Exactly ONE tamper-evident audit entry per streamed tool-use request (recorded in `onFinish`, `status` distinguishing `ok` vs `client_cancel`). 6 new `@Test` functions (`OpenAIChatStreamTests`): tool-call-delta-shape, arguments-fragment-concatenation, terminal-finish-reason, no-tools-scope-403-stream, single-audit-entry, no-parallel-streaming-stack. All 26 OpenAI streaming + tool-use tests green; `./tools/test-safe.sh` 8/8 chunks green. Re-audit (Lauret / Karpathy / Schneier): PASS. **Scope:** the tool call is still produced by the placeholder engine; parallel multi-tool streaming fan-out beyond a single call per turn is out of scope (sequential by array index). Branch-integrity pre-flight (Step 4.5) passed — on `main`. (`phase-v13d-1-streaming-tool-calls-deltas-2026-05-27`, V.13d re-audit follow-up)

### May 27 — feature: tool-use / function-calling round-trip on `POST /v1/chat/completions` (V.13d, 6 of 7 V.13 sub-items). The OpenAI-compatible chat surface now accepts `tools: [{ type: "function", function: { name, description, parameters: <JSON-Schema> } }]` and emits `tool_calls` when the model calls a tool. NEW `JSONValue` (a faithful arbitrary-JSON enum in `OpenAIChatModels`) carries a tool's `parameters` JSON-Schema **verbatim** through the round-trip; a shared `OpenAIToolCall` shape (`{ id, type: "function", function: { name, arguments } }`) serves both the request (a prior assistant turn's `tool_calls`) and the response. When the model calls a tool the choice message carries `tool_calls` + `content: null` + `finish_reason: "tool_calls"` — and `function.arguments` is a JSON-encoded **string** (not a nested object), matching OpenAI exactly. Request `content` is now tolerant of `null` (an assistant-with-`tool_calls` turn) and of an absent key (a `role: "tool"` follow-up) — both decode to "" — while a non-string, non-null `content` (the content-parts array) still returns `400`, preserving the v13a-3 contract. A `role: "tool"` message (its `content` result + `tool_call_id` + `name`) and a multi-turn `[user → assistant(tool_calls) → tool(result)]` context decode as normal context and resolve to a text answer. **Scope gate (Schneier P0):** the `tools` scope is *body-derived* — the request carries `tools:`, which the path-only auth gate cannot see — so it is enforced in the handler via `OpenAIChatHandler.toolsPreflightError`: a key whose scope excludes `tools` gets `403 insufficient_scope` even with a valid `tools` payload, and a `stream: true` tool-use request funnels through the SAME pre-flight so it cannot bypass the 403. Malformed declarations are rejected — a missing `function`/`name` fails decode → `400`; a non-`function` type or an empty function name → `400` via `toolsValidationMessage`. **No parallel tool registry (acceptance contract):** NEW `OpenAIToolBridge` translates each declared tool into senkani's existing `MCPToolConfig` catalog row type (function tools → `.exec`, confirmation-worthy — the same classification `senkani_exec`/`Bash` carry), deduped by name. Each tool-use request still appends exactly ONE tamper-evident `OpenAIAuditChain` entry (canonical columns unchanged — hash-stable; the audit `request_body` appends `tools=N` only when tools are present so a non-tool request's summary and hash are byte-identical to v13a-3). 10 new `@Test` functions (`OpenAIToolUseTests`): tools-input-honored, tool_calls-output-shape, arguments-json-string, role-tool-accepted, multi-turn-tool-context, MCPToolConfig-bridge-no-parallel-registry, no-tools-scope-403, with-tools-scope-success, audit-entry, malformed-tool-schema-rejected. Follow-up `phase-v13d-1-streaming-tool-calls-deltas-2026-05-27` filed: a valid `stream: true` + tools request rides v13b's chunk path (per v13d's documented deferral) but the tool call is not yet surfaced as SSE `delta.tool_calls` fragments. ### May 27 — fix: 19 parser/scanner perf gates migrated from median-of-3 to min-of-N, closing the same cold-build/contention flake mode fleet-wide (follow-up to the `DependencyGraph` perf-gate fix below). ### May 27 — fix: `DependencyGraph` perf gate ("Real project graph builds fast") no longer flakes under cold-build IO contention. The gate asserted the MEDIAN of 3 graph-build samples; under the IO/CPU contention of a just-completed cold compile (or a peer-suite CPU spike — `.serialized` only serializes within-suite) every one of the 3 samples can exceed the 5 s budget, so the median itself blew the budget and red-lined a healthy builder (green on rerun — the flake the V.13b note below records). The gate now asserts the **minimum** of 5 measured samples after an untimed warm-up build: the least-contended sample is the true build-time floor, and a genuine O(N²) regression slows every sample so the minimum still trips. The decision is a pure shared helper `DependencyGraphPerfGateTests.gatePasses(samples:budget:)`, and a new guard test (`gateFailsOnGenuineRegression`) pins the semantics — every-sample-over-budget FAILS, one-contended-among-fast PASSES, empty-sample-set FAILS (the gate can never be silently disabled). The "Core imported by multiple files" + "MCPSession imports something" structural assertions are preserved. Test-only change — no production code touched. Full `./tools/test-safe.sh` 8/8 chunks green; the perf-gate suite passed on two consecutive runs (standalone, then within the full suite at 21.6 s). Follow-up `perf-gate-min-of-n-robustness-sweep-remaining-gates-2026-05-27` filed: 19 other parser/scanner perf gates copy the now-migrated median-of-3 canonical pattern (`spec/testing.md` lines 768-778) and share the identical flake mode. Branch-integrity pre-flight (Step 4.5) passed — on `main`. (`dependency-graph-perf-gate-flake-under-build-load-2026-05-27`)

### May 27 — feature: chat streaming (SSE) for the OpenAI-compatible endpoint (V.13b, 4 of 7 V.13 sub-items). `POST /v1/chat/completions` with `stream: true` now emits Server-Sent Events instead of the v13a-3 `400`. NEW `OpenAIChatStream` (`Sources/Core/OpenAIEndpoint/OpenAIChatStream.swift`, `Network`-free + fully unit-testable): the OpenAI `chat.completion.chunk` delta shape (hand-encoded so `finish_reason` is always present as explicit `null` on non-terminal chunks and the final chunk's `delta` is `{}`), the `text/event-stream` HTTP head (no `Content-Length`, `Connection: close`), the `data: <json>\n\n` event wrapper, and the terminal `data: [DONE]\n\n` sentinel. A completion streams as a leading `{role: "assistant"}` chunk → one `{content: …}` chunk per whitespace-preserving piece (`splitForStreaming` guarantees the pieces concatenate **byte-for-byte** back to the full message) → a terminal `finish_reason: "stop"` chunk → `[DONE]`. The pure `run(head:events:done:sink:onFinish:)` drive loop checks cancellation before every write, fires `onFinish` with the terminal status BEFORE teardown, and calls `Sink.close()` EXACTLY once on every path (the no-fd-leak guarantee). `OpenAIListener` gains an optional `StreamHandler` consulted AFTER the auth gate and BEFORE the non-streaming `ChatHandler`; a live `runStream` drives the plan over the accepted `NWConnection` on a global queue (per-chunk send completions are delivered on the listener's serial `queue`, so running the loop there would deadlock on the send semaphore). A closed peer surfaces as a send error → the stream returns `.clientCancel`. **Contracts (Lauret/Karpathy/Schneier):** (a) **rate-limit is pre-flight** — the auth gate enforces the per-key window BEFORE the stream opens, so a `429` is a complete framed JSON response emitted ahead of any SSE byte (no mid-stream `429`, no half-open connection); (b) **cancellation** — a client disconnect cancels on the next chunk write, well under the 100 ms bound with no inter-chunk pacing; (c) **audit** — a streamed request still appends exactly ONE tamper-evident `OpenAIAuditChain` entry whose `status` distinguishes completion (`ok`) from client-cancel (`client_cancel`). Auth refactor: `OpenAIListener.receiveRequest` now applies the auth gate EXACTLY ONCE per `/v1/*` request in the connection path (the rate limiter is stateful; the non-streaming `respond` is invoked with `authenticator: nil` to avoid a double-decrement) — pure `respond(authenticator:)` unit tests unchanged. 10 new `@Test` functions (`OpenAIChatStreamTests`): chunk-shape, DONE-sentinel, delta-accumulates-to-full-message, disconnect-cancels-<100ms, pre-write-cancellation-flag, no-connection-leak (completion + cancel), rate-limit-pre-flight-refusal (framed 429, never `text/event-stream`), single-audit-entry-completed, single-audit-entry-cancelled (status `client_cancel`), and a live loopback SSE round-trip (authorized `stream: true` POST → `text/event-stream`, chunk shape + `[DONE]`, Quick→Haiku actual model, one verifying audit entry). All 49 OpenAI endpoint tests green; full suite 3136 cases green (the `DependencyGraph` perf gate flaked once under cold-build IO load and passed on rerun — filed `dependency-graph-perf-gate-flake-under-build-load-2026-05-27`). Re-audit (Lauret / Karpathy / Schneier): PASS. **Scope:** assistant content still comes from the v13a-3 placeholder engine (real model backend is a later V.13 child); partial-token accounting on cancel is deferred (the placeholder produces content up-front — status distinction is the shipped requirement). Branch-integrity pre-flight (Step 4.5) passed — on `main`. (`phase-v13b-chat-streaming-sse`, V.13 decomposition 4 of 7)

NEW `OpenAIChatHandler` (`Sources/Core/OpenAIEndpoint/OpenAIChatHandler.swift`, pure + fully testable): decodes the request, **the provisioned key's `ModelPreset` WINS routing** via `ModelRouter.resolve` — the request's `model` field (e.g. `gpt-4o`) is logged for telemetry only and NEVER changes routing; the response's `model` reports the ACTUAL tier model (e.g. Quick→`claude-haiku-3.5`). A telemetry event surfaces `model_logged` DISTINCT from `resolved_tier`. The listener now accumulates the request body across segments (Content-Length-aware, 256 KB cap) where v13a-1/2 needed only the head. Array-valued `content` and `stream: true` are rejected with `400` (SSE is V.13b). 12 new `@Test` functions (`OpenAIChatRoutingAuditTests`): chat-shape, preset-wins-over-request-model, response-model-is-actual, telemetry-model_logged-distinct-from-resolved_tier, audit-entry-shape, audit-bodies-off-by-default (+ off≠on hash + no body text in canonical bytes), audit-bodies-on, single-link-integrity + tamper detection, decode 400 paths, preset provider-name→`.auto` fallback, listener body-framing, and a live loopback chat round-trip (authorized POST → 200 `chat.completion`, Quick→Haiku actual model, one verifying audit entry). v13a-1/v13a-2 suites unchanged (40 OpenAI tests green); full `./tools/test-safe.sh` 8/8 chunks green. Re-audit (Lauret / Karpathy / Schneier): PASS. **Scope:** this child ships the routing + audit SURFACE; assistant content comes from a placeholder engine (`Serve.placeholderChatEngine` — honest "model backend not yet wired, routed to <model>" completion). ### May 27 — feature: bearer auth + key provisioning for the OpenAI-compatible endpoint (V.13a-2, 2 of 7 V.13 sub-items). Layers bearer-token auth + per-key rate-limit + per-key scope + expiry onto v13a-1's `NWListener`. NEW `senkani vault add openai-key --preset <p> [--scope chat,embeddings] [--rate <rpm>] [--expires <iso8601>] [--label <name>]` (`Sources/CLI/VaultCommand.swift`): provisions an `sk-senkani-…` key, prints the **plaintext key once to stdout** (human summary to stderr so `| pbcopy` captures only the key), and stores ONLY the SHA-256 `key_hash` — the plaintext is never persisted. NEW `OpenAIAuthGate` (`Sources/Core/OpenAIEndpoint/OpenAIAuthGate.swift`, pure + fully testable): decision order is missing/malformed-`Authorization` → `401`, well-formed-but-unknown key → `401`, expired key → `401`, in-vault key whose `scope` excludes the requested surface → `403`, over per-key rate-limit → `429` + `Retry-After`, else `ok`. **Schneier P0:** key match is a CONSTANT-TIME compare over fixed-length SHA-256 hashes that loops every record with NO early return and folds any length delta into the running diff (no short-circuit) — "no such key" and "wrong key" are timing-indistinguishable and return the identical `401` reason `"invalid key"` (no oracle). NEW `OpenAIRateLimiter` (per-key fixed 60 s window, default 60 rpm, vault record overrides). NEW `OpenAIKeyRecord` (`{ key_hash, preset, scope, rate_limit, created_at, expires_at?, label }`) + `OpenAIKeyProvisioner` + `JSONFileKeychainStore` — a 0600 JSON `KeychainStore` conformance at `~/.senkani/openai-keys.json` so a key provisioned by the short-lived `vault add` process is visible to `serve` (the in-memory `CredentialVault.shared` would evaporate on process exit; the macOS Keychain for *secrets* is still T.4c — these records hold only verifier hashes, not secrets). Auth is enforced on the `/v1/*` prefix BEFORE the listener's `501` stub: `OpenAIListener` gains an optional `Authenticator`; with none configured (the v13a-1 scaffold contract + its tests) `/v1/*` still falls straight through to `501`. `serve --openai` reads the provisioned-key snapshot at start (live reload on mid-serve provisioning is out of scope for v13a-2). 15 new `@Test` functions (`OpenAIAuthGateTests`): provision+print-once+hash-only (asserts the 0600 on-disk file contains the hash but NOT the plaintext), missing/malformed/unknown-key 401, constant-time + no-oracle (wrong-key ≡ no-such-key decision), out-of-scope 403, over-rate 429-with-Retry-After + window-reset, expired 401, default-60rpm, vault-record-override-rpm, auth-before-501 (deny→401 / allow→501 / non-v1→404), case-insensitive header parse, and a live loopback 401 round-trip. v13a-1 scaffold suite unchanged (12/12 green — no authenticator → still 501); full `./tools/test-safe.sh` 8/8 chunks green. Re-audit (Lauret / Karpathy / Schneier): PASS — Lauret: OpenAI-shaped error JSON + `Retry-After`, key→stdout/summary→stderr ergonomics; Karpathy: disk store makes provisioning cross-process real (not theatre); Schneier: constant-time no-short-circuit no-oracle compare, plaintext never persisted, 0600 verifier file. Follow-up `process-gap-v13a-2-openai-key-vault-persistence-hardening-2026-05-27` filed (live-reload on mid-serve provisioning + a guard so `JSONFileKeychainStore` is never reused for actual secrets before T.4c encryption). Branch-integrity pre-flight (Step 4.5) passed — on `main`, `close.merge_target: main` matches. (`phase-v13a-2-bearer-auth-vault`, V.13 decomposition 2 of 7)

### May 26 — feature: `senkani schedule create` gains `--prose <text>` (+ `--locale <BCP-47>`) — natural-language cadence compiled to a cron before save. `Schedule.Create` is now an `AsyncParsableCommand`; `run()` awaits a `ProseCadenceCompiler`. The cadence flags are a **three-way XOR** — exactly one of `{--cron, --counter-cadence, --prose}` (the prior two-way `{--cron, --prose}` exclusivity became three-way once `--counter-cadence` shipped). NEW `RuleBasedProseCadenceCompiler` (`Sources/Core/ProseCadenceCompiler.swift`) is the MLX-free production compiler the `--prose` path wires by default: a pure, total mapper from a curated set of common **English** phrases to a 5-field cron — `hourly` / `daily` / `weekly` / `every minute` / `every hour` / `every day` / `every N minutes` (1–59) / `every N hours` (1–23) / `every day at <time>` / `every weekday at <time>` (Mon–Fri = `1,2,3,4,5`, the comma form because `CronToLaunchd.convert` rejects the `1-5` range form) / `every <weekday> at <time>` (Sun=0…Sat=6, full names + common 3-letter abbreviations). `<time>` parses `H` / `H:MM` with optional `am`/`pm`. There is **no silent fallback**: unrecognized phrases throw `ProseCadenceCompilerError.unrecognizedPhrase`, non-English locales throw `.unsupportedLocale`, and each error's `userMessage` points the operator at `--cron` or `--locale en-US`. The run path is compile → `CronToLaunchd.convert` (defense-in-depth) → `AmplificationGuard.validate` → persist a `ScheduledTask` with `proseCadence` / `compiledCadence` / `cronPattern` / `locale`; any error writes NOTHING (no JSON under `~/.senkani/schedules/`, no plist under `~/Library/LaunchAgents/`). `--locale` defaults to `Locale.current.identifier`, so an operator on a non-English machine gets a clean refusal (not a crash) pointing at `--cron` / `--locale en-US`. The MLX-Gemma adapter for arbitrary natural language stays deferred to `phase-u8b-prose-compiler-adapter` per the 2026-05-26 scope-groom (rule-based-now / MLX-later). Internals: `ScheduleStore`'s test-dir overrides moved from an `NSLock`-serialized global pair to `@TaskLocal` — an `NSLock` cannot be held across an `await` (forbidden in Swift 6), and the async `Create.run()` test path needs per-task temp-dir isolation that a lock-free global could not provide without a clobber race between parallel suites. 10 new `@Test` functions (`RuleBasedProseCadenceCompilerTests` phrase→cron table + unrecognized-phrase + non-en-locale + en-variant + actionable-message coverage; `ScheduleCommandProseTests` success-persists-NL-fields + unavailable-compiler-zero-disk-trace + three-way-XOR + non-en-locale-zero-disk-trace). Test count 3059 → 3069 `@Test` funcs (full run 3087 cases, all green). Re-audit (Sutherland / Allspaw / Torvalds): PASS — Sutherland: every failure surfaces a crisp recovery pointer; Allspaw: all error paths verified zero-disk-trace, amplification guard runs on the compiled cron; Torvalds: compiler is pure/total and emits only `convert`-valid crons (comma weekdays, bounded N), and the `@TaskLocal` move retires a latent global-override race. Zero defects-outside-criteria surfaced; no follow-up filed. Branch-integrity pre-flight (Step 4.5) passed — on `main`, `close.merge_target: main` matches. (`schedule-cli-prose-flag-2026-05-21`, Finding C-prose split from `schedule-amplification-guard-and-pane-not-wired-2026-05-17`)

### May 26 — build (partial-ship): `process-gap-operator-hand-edit-verbatim-fidelity-unverified-2026-05-26` — `tools/autonomous/check_verbatim_fidelity.py` autonomous helper (stdlib-only Python, mirrors `check_envelope_size.py` / `check_external_surfaces.py` shape) that closes the blind spot the parent item's hand-edit walk exposed: groom-template hand-edit walks verify a pasted block's **count** (`grep -c`), **placement** (block-scoped `awk`), **additivity** (`diff -u` vs backup shows N hunks / 0 deletions), and **fingerprint** (pre/post sha differ) — but NONE of those check the inserted bytes *match the intended text*. A paste that drops a list bullet, reflows a long line, or paraphrases a sentence satisfies all four yet ships the wrong content (demonstrated live on the parent: the first application of build-mode Edit 2 dropped a `status:` flip bullet and reflowed one line, passing steps 5/6/10/11). The helper is the out-of-band byte-exact check, mechanized: given `--staged <verbatim.txt>` + `--target <edited-file>` + `--start-marker`/`--end-marker` (Python regexes; same start-inclusive / end-exclusive rule as the canonical `awk '/^start/{f=1} /^end/{f=0} f'` idiom; `--include-end-marker` to include the end line; omit `--end-marker` to run to EOF), it extracts the landed block and compares it line-exact against the staged source. Comparison is line-exact via `str.splitlines()` (a deliberate, documented decision): the single trailing newline is normalized (an editor artifact the extraction mechanism can't faithfully preserve, NOT a content infidelity), but every defect class the finding names is still caught — dropped line (`line_count_mismatch`), reflowed line (boundaries move → count/content mismatch), paraphrase (`content_mismatch`, same count, differing content), and whitespace-within-line; internal (content-bearing) blank lines are preserved and still compared. Loud failures for `block_not_found` (start marker matched nothing) and `ambiguous_start_marker` (start matched >1 line — first used, but flagged). JSON output carries `identical` / `should_fire` (alias), `block_found`, `start_match_count`, `end_marker_found`, `staged_line_count`, `landed_line_count`, `first_diff_line` (1-based), `reasons[]` (`kind` + `detail`), and the full unified `diff`. Exit 0 = identical, 1 = mismatch/not-found/ambiguous, 2 = IO error. 12 new tests in `tools/autonomous/test_check_verbatim_fidelity.py` covering the three named defect classes (match / dropped-line / reflowed-line) + paraphrase + block-not-found + ambiguous-start + end-marker-exclusive boundary + `--include-end-marker` + trailing-final-newline-normalized + internal-blank-line-compared + no-end-marker-to-EOF + JSON-shape contract. Smoke-tested against a real 22-line SKILL.md block (`5.7. External-surfaces check`): staged-against-itself → `identical: true` / exit 0; drop one line → `line_count_mismatch` at line 3 / not identical. `spec/autonomous/PROCESS.md` gains a `## Verbatim-fidelity check` section documenting the principle (count/placement/additivity are necessary but NOT sufficient for verbatim deliverables — a content-equality check is required), the helper contract, and the line-exact-comparison rationale. Full tools/autonomous test suite green: 79 tests across 9 sibling helper suites (was 67; the 12 new tests are the entire delta). NO Swift code touched; NO MCP/CLI surface change; NO migration. Per `[[feedback_skill_md_partial_ship_pattern]]`, Acceptance bullet 1 (add the verbatim-fidelity acceptance pattern to the SKILL.md `### Groomed body template`) requires editing `~/.claude/skills/senkani-autonomous/SKILL.md` (categorical-block #3, meta-recursive self-edit) — the proposed template text is preserved verbatim in the item's `## Build abort note 2026-05-26` body section for operator hand-edit; item flipped `status: open` → `manual + groomable: true` so a future groom round writes the Cowork/operator-runnable walk. Acceptance bullet 4 (no change to the parent item) honored. Re-audit verdict (Kleppmann / Torvalds): PASS clean. Torvalds — single-file stdlib-only helper, deterministic, mirrors sibling-helper shape exactly; markers are explicit regex; ambiguity fails loudly rather than silently picking the first match; end-marker-exclusive parity with the awk idiom confirmed on a real 22-line SKILL.md block. ### May 25 — ratification: `WorkBusConfig` standalone surface is canonical for the `dualWrite` operational flag (`process-gap-policyconfig-session-work-bus-dualwrite-field-pending-2026-05-20`). Operator scope-groom 2026-05-24 chose Option 1 (ratify standalone) + Option "nothing extra — mtime is enough" for observability. This entry ratifies the U.9a (2026-05-20) scope-cut: U.9a's original acceptance bullet read `PolicyConfig.sessionWorkBus.dualWrite` (operational flag folded into the immutable `PolicyConfig` snapshot, with `HashableView` + `policyHash()` participation); the shipped implementation cut to a standalone `Sources/Core/WorkBusConfig.swift` persisted at `~/.senkani/work-bus.json` via `SettingsIO`, read by `Sources/CLI/DoctorCommand.swift` for the doctor surface. The canonical surface going forward is the standalone `WorkBusConfig` — supersedes U.9a's acceptance text. Kleppmann-style rationale: `PolicyConfig` is the immutable, hash-deduplicated, per-session audit snapshot (`policy_snapshots.UNIQUE(session_id, policy_hash)`); threading an operator-flippable operational mode flag through that surface means every dual-write toggle writes a new `policy_snapshots` row even when no other policy field changed — the audit table fills with snapshots that record nothing except an operator-driven knob flip. Splitting `WorkBusConfig` out keeps the operational knob orthogonal to the immutable audit snapshot, matching Kleppmann's preferred semantics (operational state ≠ audit state). Majors-style observability decision: the `~/.senkani/work-bus.json` file mtime + on-disk JSON contents are the audit trail for "operator flipped the bus" — no `event_counters` tick, no chained `policy_snapshots`-equivalent row. Trade-off accepted by operator: audit snapshots do NOT carry the `dualWrite` flag value at session-capture time; operators query `~/.senkani/work-bus.json` directly or via `senkani doctor` for current state. Future re-scope possible if compliance-audit requirements emerge (would be a fresh `process-gap-...-work-bus-audit-row-2026-MM-DD` item). NO code changes this round (the shipped `Sources/Core/WorkBusConfig.swift` + `Sources/CLI/DoctorCommand.swift` integration is the canonical implementation); NO PolicyConfig field added; NO new observability signal; NO tests added (degenerate documentary round, ~5 min envelope per the operator's scope decision). Re-audit verdict (Kleppmann / Majors): PASS clean. Kleppmann — ratification correctly captures the audit-snapshot-orthogonality rationale and explicitly names the trade-off (audit snapshots don't carry the flag); names the future re-scope escape hatch by item-id pattern. Majors — observability decision documented as minimum surface area; mtime + JSON contents named as the durable audit trail; no operational-knob-tick proliferation. Zero defects-outside-criteria surfaced. Originating: `process-gap-policyconfig-session-work-bus-dualwrite-field-pending-2026-05-20` — filed 2026-05-20 during U.9a close-mode sweep (scope-cut surfaced during build, parent-finding linkage explicit in item frontmatter); scope-groomed 2026-05-24 (operator interview ratified Option 1); built 2026-05-25 (this round).

canonical row's sessionId/toolCallId/result conformed-dimension fidelity verified via `fetchByIdempotencyKey("v17a:<hash>")`; (3) `warningAndAbortFixtureAndReuseSeam` — Fixture 3 (assistant text + system.warning + result.error_max_turns), asserts 3 events `[.messageStarted, .warning, .turnAborted]`, warning carries `["context window remaining < 5%"]`, turnAborted's `warnings == ["error_max_turns"]` so downstream consumers can distinguish abort flavors;
