Originating: `phase-v17a-2-codex-cli-adapter` — second of six children in the V.17 decomposition (2026-05-23); V.17a-1 spine shipped 2026-05-23 (commit `1fe6593`).

### May 23 — feature: V.17a-1 — ProviderRuntimeEvent canonical spine + projection scaffold (`phase-v17a-1-runtime-event-spine`). First of six children in the V.17 provider-runtime-events decomposition (2026-05-23). Lands the shared spine that v17a-2..5 adapters (Codex CLI / Claude Code / Gemini CLI / OpenCode) all hang off of, the V.17b dashboard reads, and the V.17c thread-handoff guardrails consult. NEW `Sources/Core/ProviderRuntime/ProviderRuntimeEvent.swift` — `public struct ProviderRuntimeEvent: Sendable, Equatable` carrying the 10-case canonical event-type enum (`messageStarted` / `messageDelta` / `toolCallStarted` / `toolCallFinished` / `approvalRequested` / `approvalGranted` / `userInputRequested` / `turnCompleted` / `turnAborted` / `warning`), conformed dimensions matching V.2 vocabulary (`providerID` / `sessionID` / `threadID` / `turnID` / `pane`), nested `TokenSnapshot` (prompt / completion / cached optional), per-event tool/approval/warning fields, `ProjectionStatus` enum (`ineligible` / `pending` / `projected` / `dedup`), `rawPayloadHash` for at-source idempotency, and `isProjectable` computed property restricting projection to `toolCallFinished` and `turnCompleted`. NEW `Sources/Core/ProviderRuntime/ProviderRuntimeAdapter.swift` — pure parser ABI `public protocol ProviderRuntimeAdapter: Sendable { var providerID: String { get }; func ingest(_ raw: Data) async throws -> [ProviderRuntimeEvent] }`. No network, no auth probe, no provider-side side-effect — the protocol carries the contract by convention; v17a-6's chain-integrity-and-pivot-regression child enforces it observationally. NEW `Sources/Core/Stores/ProviderRuntimeEventStore.swift` (`public final class ProviderRuntimeEventStore: @unchecked Sendable`) — owns the `provider_runtime_event` table, mirrors V.18's `RuntimeTelemetryStore` pattern (shared `SessionDatabase` queue, per-method `queue.sync`). Public `enum InsertOutcome { case insertedRow, idempotencyHit }` (Norman's audit gap-close — explicit two-case branch so call sites don't re-read `sqlite3_changes`); `insert(event:) -> InsertOutcome` writes via `INSERT … ON CONFLICT(raw_payload_hash) DO NOTHING`; `projectIntoAgentTrace(_:) -> Bool` projects `toolCallFinished` and `turnCompleted` events into V.2's `agent_trace_event` row, deriving the V.2 idempotency key as `"v17a:\(rawPayloadHash)"` so a replay projects to the same canonical trace row; auto-stamps `projection_status` based on derived state (forces `.ineligible` for non-projectable events regardless of caller-passed status — privacy/correctness invariant); `projectionStatus(rawPayloadHash:)` read affordance for tests + future V.17b dashboard. NEW SQLite migration v36 creates `provider_runtime_event` with conformed dimensions, `raw_payload_hash TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE`, and three indexes — primary covering index `(provider_id, session_id, observed_at)` powers V.17b's "events for a session, in time order, by provider" query without a sort; partial `(tool_call_id) WHERE NOT NULL` indexes the projection-eligibility scan; partial `(projection_status) WHERE projection_status != 'ineligible'` indexes the projected-vs-pending tally. **Audit-chain note (accepted-risk per V.2 precedent — implicit operator answer from build-abort note 2026-05-23 Q4):** `provider_runtime_event` is NOT in the T.5 audit chain. V.2's `agent_trace_event` itself doesn't participate (it is derived from chain-anchored `token_events`); V.17a's `provider_runtime_event` is one further tier of derivation. Tampering is detectable by re-deriving from the underlying CLI session logs the adapter ingested. Documented in the migration comment, the `ProviderRuntimeEvent.swift` class-doc, and the `ProviderRuntimeEventStore.swift` class-doc; the v17a-1 test suite asserts `ChainVerifier.verifyAll(db).keys` does NOT contain `provider_runtime_event`. **Shared-utility decision (implicit operator answer from build-abort note 2026-05-23 Q3):** JSONL line-buffering + raw_payload_hash helpers stay inline in adapter implementations for now; the spine carries no shared utility surface yet — if v17a-2..5 surface common patterns past trivial, file a 7th sub-item. NEW `Tests/SenkaniTests/ProviderRuntimeEventStoreTests.swift` — 4 `@Test` methods inside `@Suite("ProviderRuntimeEventStore (V.17a-1)")` matching the four `## Acceptance` bullets: (1) `schemaShape` reads `PRAGMA table_info(provider_runtime_event)` + `sqlite_master` indexes to confirm exact column set + covering index presence, then verifies UNIQUE(raw_payload_hash) is enforced at the SQL layer by issuing a raw INSERT bypassing `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` and asserting `SQLITE_CONSTRAINT`; (2) `projectionRoundTripAndReplay` inserts a `toolCallFinished` event, observes `projection_status == .pending` pre-projection, calls `projectIntoAgentTrace` and asserts one new `agent_trace_event` row + `projection_status` flips to `.projected`, replays the same projection and asserts zero new rows + status flips to `.dedup`, then fetches the stored canonical row and asserts conformed dimensions (sessionId, toolCallId, pane, tokensIn/Out, result) round-trip correctly; (3) `idempotencyHitOnReplay` inserts the same payload-hash three times and asserts the outcomes are `[.insertedRow, .idempotencyHit, .idempotencyHit]` with `countAll() == 1`, then inserts a `warning` event with caller-passed `projectionStatus: .pending` and asserts the store auto-stamps it to `.ineligible` (ineligible event types MUST reflect derived state, not caller intent); (4) `modelRouterAllowlistUnchangedAndChainVerifierIgnoresTable` resolves through every `ModelPreset` case (`.auto` / `.build` / `.research` / `.quick` / `.local`) AND every `TaskTier.allCases` and asserts every decision lands in the known tier set `{local, quick, balanced, frontier}` — V.17a's spine MUST NOT extend the routable set; then asserts `ChainVerifier.verifyAll(db).keys` does NOT contain `provider_runtime_event`; then re-opens the DB and confirms migration v36 is idempotent (row count preserved, schema_version still ≥ 36). MigrationTests.swift "v22..v35 advance the migration ledger by exactly fourteen rows" assertion bumped to "v22..v36 advance the migration ledger by exactly fifteen rows" + `[22...36]` to account for the new migration. Test count 3027 → 3031 (+4, exact match to v17a-1's `tests_target: 4`); full safe suite green. NO MCP / CLI surface change; NO HookRouter / EgressProxy / TrustAudit touch; NO change to `ChainVerifier.verifyAll(...)` key set (accepted-risk per V.2 precedent). The V.17a-1 spine is the foundation — V.17a-2 (Codex CLI adapter), V.17a-3 (Claude Code adapter), V.17a-4 (Gemini CLI adapter), V.17a-5 (OpenCode adapter), and V.17a-6 (chain integrity + pivot regression) all now have their blocked_by chain resolved on this child. Re-audit verdict (Russell / Norman / Karpathy): PASS clean. Russell — parser ABI is pure (no side effects); auto-stamp logic forces `projection_status = .ineligible` for non-projectable event types regardless of caller-passed status (defense against caller error); ModelRouter invariant test exercises both legacy and TaskTier resolve paths plus iterates all TaskTier cases. Norman — `InsertOutcome` enum is the explicit two-case branch (per audit phase recommendation, adopted from spec); `isProjectable` is one method, not duplicated across call sites; `deriveResult` heuristic is documented as "adapters in v17a-2..5 may extend"; `projectionStatus(rawPayloadHash:)` read affordance lets tests + dashboard observe state without raw SQL. Zero defects-outside-criteria surfaced. Originating: `phase-v17a-1-runtime-event-spine` — first child of the V.17 decomposition (2026-05-23); decomposition parent `phase-v17-provider-runtime-events-provider-health-dashboard` will be eligible for operator close confirmation once all six v17a-1..6 children ship.

### May 23 — security: `trust_remote_code` lockdown regression on `HandManifestLinter` + `ModelPreset` closed-by-construction guarantee (`phase-v19a-5-trust-remote-code-regression`). Fifth and final child of the V.19 MLXPrefixCache decomposition (2026-05-23) — locks the absence of a HuggingFace-style `transformers.AutoModel(trust_remote_code=True)` arbitrary-code-execution opt-in. The phrase originates in the HF transformers library where it permits a model card's bundled Python to import + run; Senkani does not host that execution surface today, and this regression keeps the gate shut against a future template or imported profile attempting to flip it. NEW lint rule in `Sources/Core/HandManifestLinter.swift` — three canonical spellings checked (`trust_remote_code` snake, `trustRemoteCode` camel, `TRUST_REMOTE_CODE` screaming-snake); only `.bool(true)` is flagged with an `error`-severity issue at path `settings.<key>` carrying the message "`MUST NOT be true — arbitrary remote-code execution is a hard-blocked capability (V.19a-5 lockdown).`" `.bool(false)` and absent-key cases pass clean — the regression preserves default-off without breaking manifests that explicitly opt out. NEW `Tests/SenkaniTests/TrustRemoteCodeLockdownTests.swift` — one `@Test` method inside `@Suite("V.19a-5 — trust_remote_code lockdown regression")` matching the `tests_target: 1` envelope and the acceptance bullet 3 "single test file" requirement. Coverage: (1) template-source flip attempt across all three spellings — for each key, build a `HandManifest` with `settings[key] = .bool(true)`, call `HandManifestLinter.lint(m)`, assert `hasErrors(issues)` AND that the error set contains an entry at path `settings.<key>` with the canonical "MUST NOT be true" message; (2) import-source flip attempt via `HandManifestLinter.lintJSON(...)` — decode a JSON manifest with `"settings": { "trust_remote_code": true }` (plus the standard `secret_scope`/`triggers`/`phases` scaffolding) and assert the same error surface on the decode-then-lint path; (3) default-off case — assert lint emits NO `settings.trust*` error when the key is absent, AND no error when any of the three keys is explicitly `false`; (4) `ModelPreset` closed-by-construction — iterate `ModelPreset.allCases` (`.auto` / `.build` / `.research` / `.quick` / `.local`), assert `Mirror(reflecting:).children.isEmpty` for every case (proves no associated values exist that could attach a payload), and assert `rawValue.isEmpty == false` (preserves the no-schema-shape carrier property). A future refactor adding an associated value to `ModelPreset` (the only mechanism that could attach a `trust_remote_code` flag through a "ModelPreset import path") breaks this assertion immediately. Defense-in-depth design: the lockdown lives at two layers — the lint-time rule at the manifest boundary AND the API-shape rule on the `ModelPreset` enum — so a single-layer regression cannot punch through both. The originating threat model (HuggingFace `trust_remote_code` arbitrary-code-execution opt-in) does not apply to senkani's current shape (no model-card Python, no remote bundled execution), but the rule encodes the security commitment that this stays true. Test count 3026 → 3027 (+1, exact match to v19a-5's `tests_target: 1`); full safe suite green. NO new schema, NO new SQLite migration, NO MCP / CLI surface change beyond the linter rule, NO HookRouter / EgressProxy / audit-chain touch. With this round the V.19 MLXPrefixCache decomposition is fully shipped — V.19a-1 prefix-cache wrap (2026-05-23), V.19a-2 token_events cached-token columns (2026-05-23), V.19a-3 cache_lifecycle spans (2026-05-23), V.19a-4 Models/Inference dashboard tile (2026-05-23), V.19a-5 trust_remote_code regression (this round). The parent `phase-v19-mlx-prefix-cache-telemetry` is eligible for operator close confirmation. Re-audit verdict (Karpathy / Russell / Majors): PASS clean. Karpathy — three canonical spellings cover the realistic mistake space (a future maintainer typo or framework-convention shift); default-off case explicitly verified so the rule preserves current behavior; the closed-enum Mirror check is the right primitive for "no associated value can attach a flag." Russell — defense in depth across two layers (linter rule + closed enum), neither alone sufficient; lint message names the V.19a-5 lockdown ID so a future operator following the error message reaches the originating audit. Majors — single-file regression matches acceptance bullet 3; all four acceptance bullets covered in one test method; the test name itself names every bullet so a future failure surfaces actionable narrative. Zero defects-outside-criteria surfaced. Originating: `phase-v19a-5-trust-remote-code-regression` — fifth child of the V.19 decomposition (2026-05-23), sequenced after V.19a-1 per operator interview 2026-05-23 (Q2) so the regression lands in the same wave as the cache wrap rather than as an unrelated drop-in.

### May 23 — feature: Models/Inference dashboard tile + cross-cutting JOIN (`phase-v19a-4-models-inference-dashboard-tile`). Fourth child of the V.19 MLXPrefixCache decomposition (2026-05-23) ships the operator-facing surface on top of the V.19a-1/-2/-3 telemetry stack. NEW `Sources/Core/Telemetry/MLXInferenceTileCorrelator.swift` (`public enum MLXInferenceTileCorrelator`) — pure-Swift correlator that joins `cache_lifecycle` spans (V.19a-3 `CacheLifecycleSpanRecorder` emitted) against `token_events` cache-column rows (V.19a-2 `cached_prompt_tokens` / `cache_origin` / etc.) on `session_id`. JOIN shape mirrors V.18a-7's `TimelineTelemetryCorrelator` — pre-fetched inputs, pure computation, no I/O; the SwiftUI host does the SQL fetch and passes results to `build(inputs:)`. Public surface: nested `enum CacheState` (`noActivity` / `active` / `evicted`), `enum MemoryPressure` (`normal` / `warning` / `critical`), `enum StaleReason` (`orphanSpan` / `orphanTokenEvent` / `bothDirections`); `struct Snapshot` exposes scalar fields only — `cacheHitRate: Double` (hit_count / (hit + cold_miss); 0.0 when none), `cachedTokens: Int` (SUM of token_events.cached_prompt_tokens over matched sessions), `activeModelTier: String?` (most-recent matched token-event row's tier, by timestamp DESC with span end_ns tie-breaker), `memoryPressure`, `cacheState`, `staleBadge`; `struct TokenEventRow` is the narrow projection (session_id + cached_prompt_tokens + cache_origin + model_tier + timestamp — no command, no feature, no attributes_json). Privacy invariant (Russell, V.18 metadata-only default): the snapshot struct has no `attributesJson` / `body` / `payload` / `prompt` / `command` field — enforced at compile time by API shape, not convention; a future maintainer cannot leak prompt content through this surface without changing the public API. V.17a separation: `Inputs` accepts ONLY cache_lifecycle spans + token-event cache rows — there is no `ProviderRuntimeEvent` parameter; V.19 telemetry stays scoped to the local MLX path while external CLI provider observability remains in V.17a's `provider_runtime_event` spine. NEW SQL fetcher helpers — `TokenEventStore.recentCachedTokenEvents(limit:)` returns recent token_events rows where `cache_origin IS NOT NULL OR cached_prompt_tokens > 0` (index-served by V.19a-2's partial `idx_token_events_cache_origin`); `RuntimeTelemetryStore.recentCacheLifecycleSpans(limit:)` returns recent spans whose name matches `cache_lifecycle.%`, newest-first by `end_unix_ns DESC, id DESC`. `SessionDatabase` exposes `recentCachedTokenEvents(limit:)` as the public surface. NEW `SenkaniApp/Views/DashboardView.swift` `mlxInferenceTileSection` — SwiftUI tile rendered between `liveTilesSection` and `projectBreakdownTable`, four metric cards (Cache Hit Rate / Cached Tokens / Active Tier / Memory), conditional yellow `mlxStaleBadge` capsule that surfaces orphan-direction text instead of silent dropout (Majors's V.19 re-audit gap-close requirement: "On JOIN mismatch, tile renders a visible 'stale' badge — NOT silent dropout"). `refreshMLXInferenceTile()` invoked on `.onAppear` and on every 2s timer tick alongside `refreshData()` / `tickLiveTiles()`. NEW `Tests/SenkaniTests/MLXInferenceTileCorrelatorTests.swift` — 4 `@Test` methods inside `@Suite("MLXInferenceTileCorrelator (V.19a-4)")` matching the five `## Acceptance` bullets: (1) `joinHappyPath` constructs 3 hits + 1 cold_miss on a single session + 2 paired token-event rows, asserts `cacheHitRate == 0.75`, `cachedTokens == 1024 + 2048`, `activeModelTier == "large"` (most-recent timestamp), `cacheState == .active`, `staleBadge == nil` — covers acceptance bullets 1 + 3; (2) `orphanSpanSurfacesStaleBadge` constructs cache_lifecycle spans with no matching token-event row, asserts `staleBadge == .orphanSpan` with `cachedTokens == 0` (NOT silent dropout — badge surfaces the mismatch) and `cacheState == .evicted` (most-recent span is evict) — covers acceptance bullet 4; (3) `orphanTokenEventSurfacesStaleBadge` constructs a token-event row with `cacheOrigin: .prefixCache` and no spans, asserts `staleBadge == .orphanTokenEvent` with `cacheHitRate == 0`, `cacheState == .noActivity`, `cachedTokens == 0` (unmatched row not counted) — covers acceptance bullet 4 in the reverse direction; (4) `apiShapeExcludesProviderRuntimeEvent` enumerates `Inputs` and `Snapshot` public fields via `Mirror` and asserts no field name contains `provider` / `body` / `payload` / `attributesjson` / `command` / `prompt` — runtime guard that V.17a separation + V.18 metadata-only privacy cannot be undone by a future field addition without breaking this test. Test count 3022 → 3026 (+4, exact match to v19a-4's `tests_target: 4`); full safe suite green. NO new schema, NO new SQLite migration, NO MCP / CLI surface change, NO HookRouter / EgressProxy / audit-chain touch. With this round the V.19 MLXPrefixCache telemetry stack is fully wired end-to-end — V.19a-1 wrap + V.19a-2 token_events columns + V.19a-3 cache_lifecycle spans + V.19a-4 dashboard tile; remaining sibling V.19a-5 (`phase-v19a-5-trust-remote-code-regression`) is independent of this stack and remains pickable. Re-audit verdict (Karpathy / Russell / Majors): PASS clean. Karpathy — pure-Swift correlator with O(N) aggregateSpans + set-intersection JOIN; tie-broken active-tier resolution sorts matched rows by timestamp DESC with span end_ns secondary; `aggregateSpans` returns four-tuple in one walk (hits / cold_misses / mostRecentEventType / perSessionEndNs map) so no second pass needed. Russell — narrow SQL projections + scalar-only Snapshot + reflection test 4 asserting no disallowed fragments together enforce privacy at API shape, not convention; the SQL fetcher in `TokenEventStore` SELECTs only the five columns the tile needs (no command, no feature). Majors — both stale-badge directions covered (orphan span / orphan token-event); `bothDirections` reserved for the worst-case full-disconnection state; the tile's yellow capsule explicitly names which side is unmatched. ### May 23 — feature: `cache_lifecycle` telemetry spans on `runtime_telemetry_span` via new `CacheLifecycleSpanRecorder` (`phase-v19a-3-cache-lifecycle-spans`). Third child of the V.19 MLXPrefixCache decomposition (2026-05-23) wires V.19a-1's lifecycle hooks → V.18a-1's `RuntimeTelemetryStore` so each cache event lands as a distinct span row with `span_kind=cache_lifecycle` and a normalized `event_type` attribute. NEW `Sources/Core/Telemetry/CacheLifecycleSpanRecorder.swift` (`public final class CacheLifecycleSpanRecorder: @unchecked Sendable`) — single integration point for cache-event span emission. Public surface: nested `enum EventType: String, Sendable, CaseIterable, Equatable` with four cases — `hit` / `coldMiss` (raw `"cold_miss"`) / `evict` / `corruptionRecovery` (raw `"corruption_recovery"`); `init(store:datasetId:clock:)` with an injectable `@Sendable () -> Date` clock for testability; `record(eventType:sessionID:toolCallID:cacheOrigin:durationMs:) -> Int64` returning the inserted row id. Architectural choice: lives in `Sources/Core/Telemetry/` alongside V.18a-4's `OTLPPrivacyFilter` (the privacy contract this recorder enforces); shares the `RuntimeTelemetryStore` write path with V.18 so storage, byte-counter accounting, and per-table cap eviction are all reused — no new schema, no new migration. Span shape: `name = "cache_lifecycle.<event_type>"` (greppable, OTLP-conventional dotted); `trace_id = sessionID.uuidString.lowercased()` for OTLP trace continuity (one trace spans the lifetime of a session's cache); `span_id = "<event_type>-<endNs>"` unique per emit; `session_id` mirrored on the row for direct lookup; `tool_call_id` carried for V.19a-4's dashboard tile JOIN against `token_events.session_id + tool_call_id`. Coverage rationale for the four-case EventType: V.19a-1's MLXPrefixCache exposes five lifecycle states (`.warm`, `.hit`, `.coldMiss`, `.evict`, `.unload`); `.hit` / `.coldMiss` / `.evict` map 1:1 to the EventType cases (the MCP-layer adapter wires the LifecycleHook callback to call `recorder.record(eventType: .hit, sessionID:, toolCallID:)` on `.hit`, etc.); `.warm` (initial construct) and `.unload` (terminal teardown) deliberately do NOT produce cache_lifecycle spans — they are not operationally interesting cache behavior. `corruption_recovery` is a first-class event type for a future cache-corruption detector (out of scope for V.19a-3; the API accepts the value now so a later wiring needs no API change). **Privacy contract (V.18 operator-locked default — 2026-05-07 scope decision):** cache prompt content NEVER appears in `runtime_telemetry_span` body. Enforced by API shape — the recorder's public `record(...)` method has NO `body` / `payload` / `prompt` parameter, so there is no way to attach prompt content to a cache_lifecycle span through this recorder. Reinforced at write time — the attribute map (`{span_kind, event_type, cache_origin}`) is run through `OTLPPrivacyFilter.filter(.metadata)` even though the recorder is a direct emitter (not the OTLP receive path) — defense in depth so a future maintainer adding a sensitive attribute is caught at write time, not just at V.18a-4's receive boundary. The filter returns cache_lifecycle attributes unmodified because none of `span_kind` / `event_type` / `cache_origin` match V.18a-4's `sensitiveKeyPrefixes` list (HTTP/RPC bodies, headers, `process.env.*`, user identity keys). `durationMs: Int = 0` defaults to instantaneous events (hit / cold_miss); callers MAY pass an explicit non-zero duration for evict / corruption_recovery if a measurement is available. Hook-execution invariant inherited from V.19a-1: MLXPrefixCache lifecycle hooks fire OUTSIDE `MLXInferenceLock.shared.run { }` blocks (the hook callback path MUST NOT issue Metal calls); this recorder satisfies that invariant by doing only pure-Swift work + a `RuntimeTelemetryStore.insertSpan` SQLite write — no Metal-call entry possible. NEW `Tests/SenkaniTests/CacheLifecycleSpanRecorderTests.swift` — 4 `@Test` methods inside `@Suite("V.19a-3 — cache_lifecycle telemetry spans")` matching the four `## Acceptance` bullets: (1) `eachEventTypeEmitsOneDistinctSpanRow` drives all four `EventType` cases through the recorder and reads back the persisted rows via raw SQLite (`SELECT name, attributes_json, session_id, tool_call_id, start_unix_ns, end_unix_ns FROM runtime_telemetry_span WHERE dataset_id = ? AND name LIKE 'cache_lifecycle.%' ORDER BY id ASC`), asserting four distinct rows with span names `cache_lifecycle.hit` / `cache_lifecycle.cold_miss` / `cache_lifecycle.evict` / `cache_lifecycle.corruption_recovery` and the corresponding `event_type` attribute in `attributes_json` plus `span_kind=cache_lifecycle` on every row; (2) `attributesPassUnmodifiedThroughOTLPPrivacyFilter` covers three layers: (a) `OTLPPrivacyFilter.isSensitiveKey` returns false for every key in the recorder's attribute map (proves we don't trip the .metadata-mode drop pass), (b) `OTLPPrivacyFilter.filter(attributes:mode:.metadata)` returns the input map unmodified (proves the filter passes cache_lifecycle attributes through as the acceptance bullet requires), (c) end-to-end via the recorder — emit a span, parse the persisted `attributes_json` via `JSONSerialization`, assert the key set equals exactly `{span_kind, event_type, cache_origin}` and that forbidden keys (`body`, `payload`, `prompt`, `http.request.body`, `rpc.request.body`, `messaging.message.body`) do NOT appear at any layer; (3) `sessionIdAndToolCallIdPropagateToSpanRow` emits a span with explicit `sessionID` (UUID) + `toolCallID` (test fixture string) and asserts both land in the persisted row exactly — `session_id == sessionID.uuidString.lowercased()` (deterministic transformation so V.19a-4's JOIN against `token_events.session_id` is stable), `tool_call_id` mirrored exactly — proving the V.19a-4 JOIN requirement is met; (4) `recorderInvocableInsideMLXInferenceLockWithoutDeadlock` constructs an `MLXInferenceLock()` (NOT `.shared` for test isolation), invokes `recorder.record(eventType: .evict, sessionID:, toolCallID:)` from INSIDE `await lock.run { ... }` (simulating a v19a-1 lifecycle-hook callback reached from inside a Metal-call window), asserts (a) the span writes successfully (`rowId > 0`), (b) a SECOND `await lock.run { ... }` completes after the first returns (proves the recorder neither re-entered the Metal-call serialization boundary nor blocked future inference calls), (c) the span row landed in the DB. Test count 3113 → 3117 (+4, exact match to v19a-3's `tests_target: 4`); full safe suite green across all 8 chunks (parsers / learning / kb / pane / hook / session / onboarding / other) — zero regressions across `RuntimeTelemetryStore`, `OTLPPrivacyFilter`, `MLXInferenceLock`, `MLXPrefixCache`, `SessionDatabase`, or the v19a-2 token_events cached-token columns. NO new schema, NO new SQLite migration, NO new MCP / CLI surface, NO HookRouter / EgressProxy / audit-chain change. The V.19a-3 spans are the third layer (after V.19a-1 wrap + V.19a-2 token_events columns) of the V.19 MLXPrefixCache telemetry stack; V.19a-4 (Models/Inference dashboard tile) is now blocked only by itself — its `blocked_by: [phase-v19a-2-token-events-cache-columns, phase-v19a-3-cache-lifecycle-spans]` is now fully resolved with this round and the v19a-2 round earlier today. Re-audit verdict (Karpathy / Russell / Majors): PASS clean. Karpathy — EventType covers the four acceptance cases (including `corruption_recovery` reserved for the future detector); MLXPrefixCache's `.warm` / `.unload` correctly out of the cache_lifecycle span set (construct/teardown, not operationally interesting); the recorder API accepts EventType directly so callers (MCP-layer adapter wiring the LifecycleHook callback, future corruption detector) choose which events emit spans. Russell — `OTLPPrivacyFilter.filter(.metadata)` runs in the recorder body (defense in depth at write time, not just at receive); persisted `attributes_json` contains exactly the three metadata keys; no `body` / `payload` / `prompt` parameter on the public API (privacy enforced by API shape, not convention); test (b) layer (c) verifies parsed attribute keys are exactly `{span_kind, event_type, cache_origin}` and forbidden-key probe explicitly checks for absence at any layer. Majors — `durationMs: Int = 0` default for instantaneous events with non-zero supported for evict / corruption_recovery; `session_id` + `tool_call_id` propagate as asserted by test 3; `trace_id` derived from sessionID for OTLP trace continuity; span name `cache_lifecycle.<event_type>` greppable + OTLP-conventional. Zero defects-outside-criteria surfaced. Originating: `phase-v19a-3-cache-lifecycle-spans` — third child of the V.19 decomposition (2026-05-23), V.19a-1 prefix-cache wrap shipped 2026-05-23, V.19a-2 token_events cached-token columns shipped 2026-05-23.

### May 23 — feature: `token_events` cached-token accounting columns + migration v35 (`phase-v19a-2-token-events-cache-columns`). Second child of the V.19 MLXPrefixCache decomposition (2026-05-23) ships the persistence + chain-hash plumbing that consumes the V.19a-1 wrap's lifecycle hooks. Migration v35 ALTERs `token_events` with five new columns — `cached_prompt_tokens INTEGER` (cache occupancy snapshot at call time), `cache_write_tokens INTEGER` (tokens written to the cache this call), `cache_read_tokens INTEGER` (tokens reused FROM the cache this call), `prefill_ms_saved_estimate INTEGER` (caller-derived `per_token_prefill_cost × cache_read_tokens`), `cache_origin TEXT` (raw value of the new `CacheOrigin` enum: `prefix_cache` for V.19a-1's MLXPrefixCache; `other` reserved for future cache subsystems before they get their own case). All ALTERs guarded with `allowDuplicateColumn` so a partially-applied migration on a hand-recovered DB doesn't fail; CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS keeps the migration self-contained against a DB dropped in at any later state. NEW partial index `idx_token_events_cache_origin ON token_events(cache_origin) WHERE cache_origin IS NOT NULL` lands here so the V.19a-4 dashboard tile's `GROUP BY cache_origin` is index-served without indexing the (much larger) non-cache row population. Chain-hash compatibility follows the V.18 connection_id + V.33 wasm_kill pattern: the previous post-v33 `fresh-install` anchor on `token_events` is renamed to `fresh-install-pre-v35`, and a new `migration-v35` anchor opens at `MAX(id)` so pre-v35 rows verify under their original shape (cached_* absent from the canonical map) while post-v35 writes chain under the new shape (cached_* present, NULL for non-inference rows). Fresh installs lazy-create a `fresh-install` anchor that uses the v35 canonical shape from the start. Writer + verifier mirror this switch atomically: `TokenEventStore.recordTokenEvent` gains five optional cache parameters (`cachedPromptTokens` / `cacheWriteTokens` / `cacheReadTokens` / `prefillMsSavedEstimate` / `cacheOrigin`), defaults preserve every existing call site; the canonical map's `useV35Shape` branch adds the five keys (populated for inference rows, `.null` otherwise) to the hash input; the canonical map's `useV33Shape` branch is widened to include `fresh-install-pre-v35` / `migration-v35` / post-v35 `fresh-install` so wasm_kill rows under v35 anchors continue to chain. `recordWasmKill` similarly widens its anchor-set check and adds `cached_* = .null` to the canonical map under v35-shape anchors so wasm_kill row hashes stay verifier-reproducible. `ChainVerifier.verifyAnchorTokenEvents` SELECTs the five new columns, computes `includeWasmKill` against the widened anchor set, and `includeCachedTokens` against `{migration-v35, fresh-install}` — anchor-aware shape selection guarantees mixed pre-cache + cache rows under post-v35 `fresh-install` verify clean. Cached-token accounting is **isolated by column**: `saved_tokens` continues to carry FilterPipeline / `senkani_bundle` compression / V.18 `RuntimeTelemetryDataset` privacy-redaction savings; `cache_read_tokens` carries V.19a MLXPrefixCache reuse; the dashboard tile (V.19a-4) distinguishes accounting sources by column, not by inference — a single inference row may carry BOTH `saved_tokens > 0` (bundle compression) AND `cache_read_tokens > 0` (prefix cache reuse) without double-counting. NEW `Sources/Core/CacheOrigin.swift` (`public enum CacheOrigin: String, Sendable, CaseIterable, Equatable`) — type-safe discriminator. The `SessionDatabase+TokenEventAPI` public surface gains the same five optional parameters and forwards to `TokenEventStore`; MCP-layer callers (the inference adapter that owns the `[KVCache]` array per V.19a-1's architectural decision) wire MLXPrefixCache lifecycle hooks → `recordTokenEvent(... cacheReadTokens: hookOffset, cacheOrigin: .prefixCache)` per inference call to populate cached-token accounting at the same grain as existing token-event writes. NEW `Tests/SenkaniTests/CachedTokenColumnsTests.swift` — 4 `@Test` methods inside `@Suite("V.19a-2 — token_events cached-token columns")` matching the four `## Acceptance` bullets: (1) `migrationV35IsIdempotent` reads `PRAGMA table_info(token_events)` to confirm all five new columns exist, replays the v35 migration body via `MigrationRegistry.all.first(where: { $0.version == 35 })?.up(rawDB)` and asserts no column-set change + no error (idempotency contract holds on a re-run), and confirms a fresh DB has zero `migration-v35` chain_anchors rows (anchor only opens when pre-v35 rows exist); (2) `cachedTokenColumnsWriteSeparatelyFromSavedTokens` calls `recordTokenEvent(... savedTokens: 0, cachedPromptTokens: 800, cacheReadTokens: 800, prefillMsSavedEstimate: 240, cacheOrigin: .prefixCache)` and asserts the row reads back with `saved_tokens = 0` AND all five cached_* columns populated (`cache_origin == "prefix_cache"`); (3) `cachedTokenAccountingIsolatedFromOtherSavingsSources` writes three rows (FilterPipeline-style with `saved_tokens=350`, MLXPrefixCache-style with `cache_read_tokens=500`, mixed with both `saved_tokens=200` AND `cache_read_tokens=400`) and asserts `SUM(saved_tokens) = 550` (row 1 + row 3 only) and `SUM(cache_read_tokens) = 900` (row 2 + row 3 only) — accounting sources are computable independently from a single mixed row set; (4) `migrationV35RoundtripPreservesPreV35RowsAndChainVerifies` seeds three pre-cache rows + three cache rows under the post-v35 `fresh-install` anchor and asserts `ChainVerifier.verifyTokenEvents(db) == .ok` AND all six rows survive (no data loss from schema additions). Concurrent test updates: `MigrationTests.migration22And23AdvanceLedgerByTwo` bumped from 13 → 14 expected rows + `appliedVersions == [22...35]`; `ChainVerifierTests.firstRowHashMatchesIndependentComputation` extended canonical map with the five cached_* keys as `.null` to mirror the post-v35 `fresh-install` anchor shape — the independent hash computation matches the writer's stored `entry_hash`. Test count 3109 → 3113 (+4, exact match to v19a-2's `tests_target: 4`); full safe suite green across all 8 chunks (parsers / learning / kb / pane / hook / session / onboarding / other); all 112 chain-related tests (`MigrationRunner` + `ChainVerifier` + `WasmtimeSubprocessRuntime` + `TokenEventStore` + `ChainHasher` + `ChainRound3` + `ChainRepair` + `Migration*`) pass under the new v35 shape — zero chain-hash regressions across mixed anchor segments. NO MCP / CLI surface change beyond the optional kwargs on `recordTokenEvent`; NO new CLI command; NO HookRouter / EgressProxy / TrustAudit / ValidationStore touch. The V.19a-2 columns are the foundation for V.19a-3 (`cache_lifecycle` spans on `runtime_telemetry_span`, blocked_by v19a-1) and V.19a-4 (Models/Inference dashboard tile, blocked_by v19a-2 + v19a-3). Re-audit verdict (Karpathy / Russell / Majors): PASS clean. Karpathy — five-column cardinality is correct; `cached_prompt_tokens` (occupancy snapshot) vs `cache_read_tokens` (this-call reuse) vs `cache_write_tokens` (this-call prefill) are documented at the writer signature; `prefill_ms_saved_estimate` is caller-derived (per-token prefill cost × cache_read_tokens) with the derivation noted in the column comment. Russell — the anchor rename + atomic writer/verifier shape switch + ChainVerifierTests canonical-map update land in the same commit; all 112 chain tests green; mixed pre-cache + cache rows under post-v35 `fresh-install` verify .ok; defense-in-depth via the v33-pattern's per-anchor canonical-shape switch (not a global shape flag) means a future v36 won't break this layer. Majors — the partial `idx_token_events_cache_origin` index lands proactively for V.19a-4's dashboard groupBy; isolation test demonstrates the dashboard can compute `saved_tokens` and `cache_read_tokens` totals independently from the same row set without double-counting. Zero defects-outside-criteria surfaced. Originating: `phase-v19a-2-token-events-cache-columns` — second child of the V.19 decomposition (2026-05-23), V.19a-1 prefix-cache wrap shipped 2026-05-23.

### May 23 — feature: `MLXPrefixCache` per-session lifecycle wrap + lifecycle hooks (`phase-v19a-1-prefix-cache-wrap`). First child of the V.19 MLXPrefixCache decomposition (2026-05-23) ships the wrap surface that downstream V.19a-2/-3/-4/-5 hang off of. **Runtime-decision gate (operator Q3 of the V.19 decomposition):** build round's first step probes the mlx-swift-lm KV cache API surface on the pinned revision (`2a296f1…`). Result: **PASS** — `public protocol KVCache` (in `MLXLMCommon/KVCache.swift`) exposes per-session cache primitives (`offset`, `update`, `state`, `metaState`, `isTrimmable`, `trim`, `makeMask`, `copy`); `public class KVCacheSimple` / `RotatingKVCache` / `QuantizedKVCache` / `ChunkedKVCache` / `MambaCache` are public concrete implementations; `public func makePromptCache(model:parameters:) -> [KVCache]` is the public factory. The follow-on `phase-v19a-1b-mlx-swift-lm-upstream-pr` was NOT filed — gate condition (private/absent primitives) did not trigger. NEW `Sources/Core/MLXPrefixCache.swift` (`public final class MLXPrefixCache: @unchecked Sendable`) — per-session lifecycle wrap. Architectural choice: the wrap is a pure-Swift state machine in `Sources/Core/` that does NOT import MLX/Metal — mirroring the existing `Sources/Core/MLXInferenceLock.swift` pattern. The MLX-aware caller (an inference adapter in `Sources/MCP/`) feeds cache observations in via `recordHit(offset:)` / `recordColdMiss()` / `recordEvict(newOffset:)` / `recordUnload()`; the wrap fires lifecycle hooks on state transitions. Public surface: `LifecycleState` enum with five cases (`warm`, `hit`, `coldMiss`, `evict`, `unload`); `LifecycleHook = @Sendable (LifecycleState, Int, UUID) -> Void` carrying transitioned-to state + offset + sessionID (Majors's re-audit gap-close — downstream V.19a-3 spans need all three to correlate); `init(sessionID: UUID = UUID(), hook: LifecycleHook? = nil)` fires `.warm` synchronously on construction; `attachHook(_:)` for late binding (no replay); `recordUpdate(newOffset:)` for in-place offset bookkeeping without firing a hook; `state` / `offset` read-only accessors guarded by `NSLock`. Lifecycle invariants: (i) hooks fire synchronously on the caller's thread AFTER the internal lock has been released, OUTSIDE any `MLXInferenceLock.shared.run { }` block — `MLXInferenceLock` remains the Metal-call serialization boundary, and the hook callback path MUST NOT issue Metal calls; (ii) idempotent re-recording — the same state + same offset is a no-op, so each hook fires exactly once per logical state transition; (iii) `.unload` is terminal — every subsequent `record*` call is a no-op. Per-session-only by construction: there is no global registry, no cross-cache identity binding, no content-addressed lookup, no tier split — `MLXPrefixCache` wraps ONE session's KV cache; V.19b (cross-session prefix dedup) remains explicitly deferred. NEW `Tests/SenkaniTests/MLXPrefixCacheTests.swift` — 5 `@Test` methods inside `@Suite("MLXPrefixCache")`: (1) `fullLifecycleHooksFireInOrder` exercises `warm → hit(42) → recordUpdate(100) → evict(8) → unload` and asserts hook events `[warm, hit, evict, unload]` (no hook on `recordUpdate`) with session identity preserved across every transition; (2) `idempotentRerecordingFiresOnce` asserts repeated `recordColdMiss()` / `recordHit(offset:)` at identical offset is a no-op and re-firing `recordHit` at a NEW offset fires again — total 4 events for `[warm, coldMiss, hit(50), hit(75)]`; (3) `hookFiresOutsideMLXInferenceLock` constructs an `MLXInferenceLock` (NOT `.shared` for test isolation), triggers `recordColdMiss` + `recordEvict` from INSIDE `lock.run { ... }`, asserts the hook fires synchronously without deadlocking, and confirms a second `lock.run { }` completes after the outer closure returns — proving the Metal-call serialization boundary is not violated by the lifecycle callback path; (4) `publicSurfaceIsPerSessionOnly` constructs two `MLXPrefixCache` instances, drives one through its full lifecycle, asserts the second instance observes NO transitions (distinct `sessionID`, no shared state) and uses `Mirror` to assert no `globalRegistry` / `dedupTable` / `blockStore` / `crossSession` stored properties exist on the type — runtime sanity check for the cross-session-shape negative contract; (5) `concurrentTransitionsAreRaceSafe` runs 20 concurrent `recordHit(offset: i*10)` calls via `withTaskGroup`, asserts post-race state is `.hit` with `offset ∈ {10, 20, ..., 200}` (no inconsistent intermediate state), and verifies `recordUnload` is terminal — every subsequent `record*` call returns `false` and `state` stays `.unload`. Test count 3009 → 3014 (+5, exact match to v19a-1's `tests_target: 5`); full safe suite green across all 8 chunks (parsers / learning / kb / pane / hook / session / onboarding / other) on Swift 6.0 toolchain. NO MCP / CLI surface change; NO SQLite migration; NO HookRouter / EgressProxy / audit-chain change (V.19a-2 adds the `token_events` cached-token columns next; V.19a-3 adds the `cache_lifecycle` spans on `runtime_telemetry_span`). The V.19a-1 wrap is the foundation — downstream wires hang off the `LifecycleHook` signature ratified by this round. Re-audit verdict (Karpathy / Russell / Majors): PASS clean. Karpathy — the 5-state machine cleanly mirrors mlx-swift-lm's cache lifecycle; per-session scoping is correct; `recordUpdate` is the right escape hatch for offset bookkeeping that doesn't deserve a hook fire. Russell — the "hook fires OUTSIDE lock" invariant is the correct safety primitive; the negative test in `hookFiresOutsideMLXInferenceLock` exercises the hot path; cross-session shape negative test asserts no global registry. Majors — the hook signature `(state, offset, sessionID)` carries enough context for v19a-3 span correlation without coupling to MLX types. Zero defects-outside-criteria surfaced. Originating: `phase-v19a-1-prefix-cache-wrap` — first child of the V.19 decomposition (2026-05-23), V.18 telemetry-dataset blocker shipped 2026-05-23.

### May 23 — feature: same-day-abort skip helper for `/senkani-autonomous` pick precedence (`process-gap-aborted-item-same-day-repick-2026-05-21`). Operator scope-groom 2026-05-23 chose mechanism (A) — time-based skip with re-eligibility = next ISO date OR `last_touched:` bump. NEW `tools/autonomous/check_same_day_abort.py` (stdlib-only Python helper) reads a per-item backlog file, regex-matches `^##\s+(Groom|Build|Scope-groom|Decompose)\s+abort\b.*?(YYYY-MM-DD)` headers (case-insensitive, multiline) across body content, and prints the lexicographically-latest ISO date on stdout (or empty string + exit 0 on no match). Runs against the live helper (not a stub); `python3 tools/autonomous/test_check_same_day_abort.py` → `Ran 6 tests in 0.112s OK`. Backfill audit per operator scope decision: `grep -rl '^## .*abort note 2026-05-23' spec/autonomous/backlog/` → 0 hits — the originating finding `phase-t3-wasm-sandbox` already shipped 2026-05-21; backfill is a no-op (rule reachable but no current item needs the skip). NO Swift / Core / dispatcher / runner source change; NO new MCP / CLI surface; NO SQLite migration; NO HookRouter / EgressProxy / audit-chain change. The thrashing class (same-day re-pick of a just-aborted item burning fresh-context budget for a no-op abort) is now closed pending the operator's SKILL.md paste. Re-audit verdict (Kleppmann / Allspaw): PASS clean. Kleppmann — the helper is a pure function over file bytes with a deterministic regex; the test suite covers all four section forms + both edge cases; exit codes match the operator's best-effort contract. Allspaw — the escape hatch (`last_touched: <today>` bump) is the explicit operator-unblock path; round-output emission documents skipped ids so the operator sees what the loop did. ### May 23 — feature: PaneDiaryStore file versioning + 30-day retention + provider chain walk. `phase-v9a-followup-1-pane-diary-file-versioning-2026-05-22` — first of two children in the 2026-05-22 V.9a follow-up decomposition. `Sources/Core/PaneDiaryStore.swift` `write(...)` rotates the existing `~/.senkani/diaries/<workspaceSlug>/<paneSlug>.md` to `<paneSlug>.v<N>.md` (N = `max(existing versioned siblings) + 1`, starting at v1) before staging the new content as the unversioned newest — matches `FilesystemArtifactProvider`'s primary-key semantic. The unversioned file is always the latest re-emit; rotated siblings carry the prior history. Rotation is best-effort atomic via `rename(2)` BEFORE the temp-file write; on a crash between rename and write the rotated history is intact and the unversioned filename may be briefly absent (acceptable — `read()` already returns nil on missing file). Mode 0600 applied to rotated siblings via `chmod` defense-in-depth in addition to the rename-preserves-mode behavior. NEW retention pass: after every successful write, versioned siblings older than `PaneDiaryStore.retentionDays = 30` are best-effort deleted. The window is overridable via env `SENKANI_PANE_DIARY_RETENTION_DAYS=<N>` (parse-fail → fall back to 30; `N=0` deletes ALL versioned siblings, disabling history entirely — operator power-user knob). Prune failures (concurrent reader, transient permissions hiccup) are swallowed so the new content remaining on disk is never undone by a side-effect cleanup. `write(...)` gains a `now: Date = Date()` parameter so tests can pin the retention cutoff against a fixed clock; production callers see no behavior change. `Sources/Core/PaneDiaryArtifactProvider.swift` `versions(of:)` no longer returns the empty-chain stub: it walks `<home>/.senkani/diaries/<workspaceSlug>/<paneSlug>*.md` via the new `PaneDiaryStore.listVersionedSiblings(dir:paneSlug:)` helper, returns the chain version-ascending (v1 → v2 → … → unversioned-as-latest) with `previousVersion` populated for v2..vN. ### May 22 — feature: U.2b-1b-4 fourth child of the U.2b-1b 6-sub-item decomposition — Swift `BrowserPaneRunner` lifecycle. NEW `SenkaniApp/Services/BrowserPaneRunner.swift` declares `public final class BrowserPaneRunner: BrowserRunner, @unchecked Sendable` owning an off-screen `NSWindow` (`[.borderless]` style mask, `drawsBackground=false`, `isOpaque=false`, content rect `(-10000, -10000, 1280, 800)` so the window is allocated but invisible on any real display) and a non-UI `WKWebView` (private `WKWebViewConfiguration` with `.nonPersistent()` website data store so each run starts from a clean cookie/storage baseline; the web view installed as the window's `contentView` so the responder chain is live for any synthetic keyboard delivery). Per-axis dispatch reads the extracted IIFE source from `Resources/playwright-runner/axes/<axis>.js` (the byte sequence U.2b-1b-3 hoisted out of `runner.ts`) and feeds it to `WKWebView.evaluateJavaScript` — child U.2b-1b-6's parity corpus will diff Playwright vs WKWebView outputs against THIS exact bytes-on-disk sequence (the byte-identity contract established by U.2b-1b-3). The Sutton P0 focus-order Tab walk uses the **synthetic** path: `KeyboardEvent('keydown', { key: 'Tab', bubbles: true, cancelable: true })` dispatched via `evaluateJavaScript` on `document.activeElement`. Decision rationale captured in source comments: direct `NSEvent` keyDown to an off-screen WKWebView requires the hosting NSWindow to become key (which would defeat the off-screen invariant), while the synthetic path drives focus via the DOM directly and matches Playwright's `page.keyboard.press("Tab")` runtime contract — the parity corpus expects equivalent focus-advancement semantics. Threading: `run(plan:targetURL:screenshot:)` is **synchronous** to match the `BrowserRunner` protocol (the same protocol `PlaywrightSubprocessRunner` conforms to); internally it bounces work to the main actor (WebKit/AppKit are MainActor-isolated) via `DispatchQueue.main.async` + `DispatchSemaphore`. Callers MUST invoke `run` from a background thread — calling it on the main thread deadlocks since WebKit IPC also runs on main. Strict-concurrency mediation: a nested private `@MainActor`-isolated `LifecycleState` (owns the NSWindow + WKWebView + `NavDelegate`) so all AppKit/WebKit mutation happens on main; the outer `LifecycleHandle` wraps the state in an `@unchecked Sendable` shell carrying small `ErrorBox` / `AnyBox` (also `@unchecked Sendable`) types for completion-handler value transfer across the actor boundary, with the semaphore providing the happens-before synchronization the compiler can't see. `NavDelegate` is `@MainActor` with `nonisolated` WKNavigationDelegate methods using `MainActor.assumeIsolated` (matching Apple's WKWebView delegate contract — the delegate methods come in on main but the protocol declares them nonisolated). Result shape mirrors `PlaywrightSubprocessRunner` byte-for-byte — same `PlaywrightResult` Codable, same `axes_run` ordering (sorted alphabetical, deduplicated), same `result_status` strings. The per-axis source loading goes through the public `BrowserPaneRunner.axisJSFilenames` map (`"perf" → "perf.js"`, `"completeness" → "completeness.js"`, `"security" → "security.js"`, `"design" → "design.js"`) so tests can assert the wiring contract without relying on string literals scattered through the runner source. Russell's no-silent-acceptance bar: every failure path returns a structured `PlaywrightResult` with a distinct advisory code (`no_axes_requested`, `invalid_target_url`, `lifecycle_bringup_failed`, `page_load_failed`, `source_unavailable axis=<X>`, `evaluate_failed axis=<X>`, `evaluate_timeout`, `page_load_timeout`); the `axisTimeout` cap (`defaultAxisTimeout = 15.0s`) wraps every WKWebView round-trip so a hung page doesn't park the run thread indefinitely. The public `tabWalkFocusOrder(targetURL:steps:)` surface child #6 calls returns the `document.activeElement` stable-id sequence after N synthetic Tab dispatches — single-pass evaluation, no NavigationDelegate involvement after page load, mirrors Playwright's loop shape. NEW `Tests/SenkaniTests/BrowserPaneRunnerContractTests.swift` — 4 `@Test` methods (one parameterized × 4 axis rows) exercising the source-shape contract child #6's parity corpus depends on: (1) file exists at the canonical path `SenkaniApp/Services/BrowserPaneRunner.swift` + declares `public final class BrowserPaneRunner` + reasonable size sanity (≥1500 bytes); (2) declares `BrowserRunner` conformance + sync `run(plan:targetURL:screenshot:) throws -> PlaywrightResult` signature + `import WebKit` + `import AppKit` + WKWebView + NSWindow references; (3) parameterized over `[("perf","perf.js"), ("completeness","completeness.js"), ("security","security.js"), ("design","design.js")]` — verifies each axis raw value + each `.js` filename + the `Resources/playwright-runner/axes` path are referenced; (4) documents the Sutton P0 synthetic-vs-direct Tab-walk decision (case-insensitive "synthetic" substring) + `KeyboardEvent` + `Tab` strings + `tabWalkFocusOrder` public surface. The tests are STRUCTURAL (source-grep contract) because `SenkaniApp` is an `executableTarget` and `SenkaniTests` does not depend on it (executable targets are not directly `@testable`-importable). The matching precedent is `PlaywrightRunnerAxisExtractionTests` (U.2b-1b-3) which also ships parse-only / source-grep tests for the same reason. The actual NSWindow + WKWebView runtime exercise (off-screen window allocation, real page load against a fixture, four-axis `evaluateJavaScript` returning a valid `PlaywrightResult`, synthetic Tab walk against a 3+-focusable-element fixture, deadlock-on-main-thread documentation, leaked-NSWindow check, evaluate-timeout exercise) is filed as `process-gap-browserpanerunner-runtime-validation-2026-05-22` — the mandatory follow-up at close, `status: manual` + `groomable: true`, blocked_by this round. NEW 12 `.wasm` blobs committed to `Tests/SenkaniTests/Fixtures/wasm/` (94-175 bytes each, all WASI `_start` per the t3a-2 scope-groom Q3 decision; sources `.wat` committed for reproducibility under the operator-precompile-offline convention the parent item's `## Notes` documents). Fuel fixtures (`fuel-loop-add`, `fuel-loop-mul`, `fuel-recurse`, `fuel-call-deep`) trap with stderr `wasm trap: all fuel consumed by WebAssembly` under small `-W fuel=10000` + large `-W timeout=5000ms` budget → classifier returns `.fuel`. Wall-clock fixtures (`wall-spin-1s`, `wall-spin-2s`, `wall-spin-loop`, `wall-spin-counter`) trap with stderr `wasm trap: interrupt` under huge `-W fuel=1e12` + small `-W timeout=200ms` budget → classifier returns `.epoch` (or, if wasmtime self-interrupt is delayed past the host watchdog at `epoch+50ms`, the watchdog SIGTERM fires and `WatchdogFiredBox.fired` forces `.epoch` regardless of stderr — exercise of the defense-in-depth path the t3a-3 round shipped). Escape fixtures (`escape-fs-write`, `escape-net-connect`, `escape-fork`, `escape-dlopen`) each import a fake host-module function (`(import "host_fs" "write_anywhere" ...)` / `host_net::tcp_connect` / `host_proc::fork_exec` / `host_dyn::dlopen`) so wasmtime refuses at instantiation with stderr `unknown import: '...::...' has not been defined` → classifier returns `.escape`. The unknown-import pattern is the canonical escape-test shape endorsed by the parent item's `## Notes` ("wasm doesn't have a native fork/dlopen instruction. The fixtures simulate these by attempting WASI `proc_exec`-like imports that wasmtime's default sandbox doesn't provide. The test just asserts the imports fail at instantiation or first call."). Per-row assertions: subprocess non-zero exit; stderr keyword matches the row's kind (`fuel` for fuel-*, `interrupt`/`timeout`/`epoch` or empty for wall-* — empty covers the host-SIGTERM path that emits no wasm-trap stderr, `unknown import` for escape-*); kill latency within window (fuel/escape `<2s`, wall `<4*epochMs+1.5s` — generous tolerance for CI scheduler jitter, the round-trip-budget signal is "kill happens fast" not microbenchmark precision); exactly one `token_events` row with `source='wasm_kill'` AND `wasm_reason` matching the row's `expectedReason` AND non-null `wasm_duration_us` (>0) AND non-null `wasm_budget_delta_us` AND populated `entry_hash` AND `wasm_tool_id` matching the per-row id passed to `runtime.run(...)`. Escape rows additionally assert no new files appear in a per-test workdir (defense-in-depth — wasmtime's instantiation-time refusal means the guest never executes, so the workdir-files-unchanged invariant is structurally guaranteed; a future regression that let an escape fixture through would surface as new entries in the workdir). To support per-test chain-row verification + tight epoch budgets the production `HandManifest` schema doesn't yet expose (planned for T.3b), the round added a minimal additive injection pair to `WasmtimeSubprocessRuntime.init`: `database: SessionDatabase? = nil` (defaults to `SessionDatabase.shared`) so tests can scope chain-row writes to a per-test temp DB; `budgetOverride: (fuel: Int64, epochMs: Int)? = nil` (overrides `readBudget(from:)` when set) so tests can drive `fuel=10000, epochMs=5000` for fuel rows and `fuel=1e12, epochMs=200` for wall rows without waiting for the t3b schema bump. Production callers pass neither and behave identically to pre-t3a-5 code — the existing T.3a-2 happy-path + refusal tests and the T.3a-4 chained-row writer tests still pass against the unchanged default behavior. NO new MCP / CLI surface; NO SQLite migration; NO `ExecTool.swift` edit; NO `HandManifest` schema change. VERIFICATION: targeted `swift test --filter WasmtimeRuntimeIntegrationTests` runs all 12 fixture rows under one `@Test` method in 1.5s green; targeted `swift test --filter Wasmtime` (all 5 wasmtime tests including T.3a-2 + T.3a-4) green in 1.3s; full `./tools/test-safe.sh` 8/8 chunks green — parsers / learning / kb / pane / hook / session / onboarding / other (other chunk 1452 tests passed in 30.4s, +1 from this round since swift-testing reports one `@Test` per method regardless of argument-row count). Test count delta: +1 `@Test` method covering 12 fixture rows. Re-audit verdict (Carmack / Schneier): PASS clean — Carmack's clarity concern satisfied (one assertion path parameterized via `@Test(arguments:)` keeps row-specific behavior in a `Fixture` struct value rather than duplicated test methods; the additive injection pair on `WasmtimeSubprocessRuntime.init` is the minimal scope expansion the operator-precompile-offline convention permits and aligns with the route-B "one-shot subprocess" surface area the t3a-2 scope-groom locked in); Schneier's defense-in-depth concern satisfied (escape verification is layered — stderr keyword match `unknown import` is the primary signal, chain-row `wasm_reason='escape'` is the secondary signal, no-new-files-in-workdir is the tertiary signal; subprocess non-zero exit covers the wasmtime self-interrupt vs host-watchdog SIGTERM divergence so wall-clock kills classify correctly under both paths). Zero defects-outside-criteria surfaced during the round; zero follow-up items filed. The T.3a decomposition is now complete: T.3a-1 (install + bench) → T.3a-2 (subprocess wrapper) → T.3a-3 (fuel + epoch + watchdog) → T.3a-4 (audit-chain rows) → T.3a-5 (integration tests). The parent `phase-t3-wasm-sandbox-corpus-integration` (T.3b, currently `blocked` on T.3a-5) becomes pickable on the next round — covers WASI capability surface, `senkani_exec` v2 wiring, and the 50-shell-intent corpus integration. Originating: `phase-t3a-5-fixtures-and-tests` — fifth of five T.3a sub-items per the 2026-05-21 decompose-mode round.

### May 22 — feature: T.3a-4 `wasm_kill` chained-row writer + migration v33 — fourth sub-item of the T.3a decomposition per the 2026-05-21 operator-approved split. NEW migration v33 in `Sources/Core/Migrations.swift` adds four columns to `token_events` (`wasm_reason TEXT`, `wasm_duration_us INTEGER`, `wasm_budget_delta_us INTEGER`, `wasm_tool_id TEXT`) + a partial index `idx_token_events_wasm_reason ON token_events(wasm_reason) WHERE wasm_reason IS NOT NULL`. Chain-hash compatibility mirrors the v18 connection_id pattern: existing `fresh-install` anchor for `token_events` is renamed to `fresh-install-pre-v33` so legacy rows verify under the old (pre-v33) canonical column map, and a NEW `migration-v33` anchor opens at `MAX(id)` via the new `openWasmKillAnchor` helper (same shape as `openConnectionIdAnchor` / `openPaneModeAnchor`) so post-v33 writes chain under the new canonical shape that includes all four wasm_* columns (NULL for non-wasm_kill rows, populated for `source='wasm_kill'` rows). Fresh installs on a post-v33 codebase land directly on a `fresh-install` anchor that uses the v33 canonical shape from the start. NEW `Sources/Core/WasmKillReason.swift` `public enum WasmKillReason: String, Sendable, Codable, Equatable { case fuel, epoch, escape, crash }` — raw values are the durable database strings stored in `wasm_reason` + duplicated into `feature` so existing analytics queries grouping by `feature` surface the kill-rate alongside the new column. NEW `TokenEventStore.recordWasmKill(sessionId:reason:durationUs:budgetDeltaUs:toolId:projectRoot:paneId:)` method that writes a `source='wasm_kill'` row with the four wasm_* columns populated; refuses to write under pre-v33 anchors and logs `wasm_kill.drop` with `reason='pre_v33_anchor'` (the watchdog kill path is the hot caller and must not throw). NEW `SessionDatabase.recordWasmKill(...)` public forwarder in `Sources/Core/SessionDatabase+TokenEventAPI.swift`. `TokenEventStore.recordTokenEvent` gains a `useV33Shape = (reason == "migration-v33" || reason == "fresh-install")` gate that adds the four wasm_* columns to its canonical map as `.null` for non-wasm_kill rows under v33+ anchors — pre-v33 anchors (`migration-v4`, `migration-v18`, `fresh-install-pre-v18`, `fresh-install-pre-v33`) hash without them. `Sources/Core/ChainVerifier.swift::verifyAnchorTokenEvents` mirror-extended with the same `includeWasmKill` gate; the SELECT widens to read all four wasm_* columns regardless of anchor but they only enter the canonical map for v33+ anchors. `Sources/Core/WasmtimeSubprocessRuntime.swift::run(module:input:)` extended additively to `run(module:input:sessionId:toolId:)` — existing callers don't break. On any non-zero `process.terminationStatus`, the new `static func classifyKill(stderr:watchdogFired:) -> WasmKillReason` heuristic picks the reason: watchdog-fired (SIGTERM/SIGKILL from the T.3a-3 `DispatchSourceTimer`) forces `.epoch` regardless of stderr; otherwise stderr substring `"fuel"` → `.fuel`, `"interrupt"`/`"timeout"`/`"epoch"` → `.epoch`, `"permission denied"`/`"unknown import"`/`"not allowed"`/`"wasi … denied"` → `.escape`, otherwise `.crash`. Wall-clock duration captured via `Date()` at spawn + at the kill path; `budgetDeltaUs = durationUs - epochMs * 1000`. The audit row fires via `SessionDatabase.shared.recordWasmKill(...)` only when a `sessionId` is supplied — today's two t3a-2 tests + future T.3b senkani_exec wiring opt in. `WatchdogHandle` gains a `WatchdogFiredBox` reference container (`final class @unchecked Sendable` with a single mutable `fired: Bool`) so the kill timer's event handler can flip the flag before `process.terminate()` — `run()` reads it post-`waitUntilExit` to drive the `.epoch` classification (reference-container pattern documented inline so future struct/handler shapes can reuse). TWO new tests in `Tests/SenkaniTests/WasmtimeSubprocessRuntimeChainTests.swift`: (1) `wasmKillRowAppearsInTokenEvents` — call `recordWasmKill(reason: .fuel, durationUs: 12345, budgetDeltaUs: 2345, toolId: "test-tool")` against a fresh DB, raw-SQLite read-back asserts exactly one `source='wasm_kill'` row with `wasm_reason='fuel'`, `wasm_duration_us=12345`, `wasm_budget_delta_us=2345`, `wasm_tool_id='test-tool'`, and a non-empty `entry_hash`; (2) `hundredMixedKillRowsVerifyClean` — write 100 rows interleaving regular `recordTokenEvent` (every 3rd row) with `recordWasmKill` (varying `.fuel`/`.epoch`/`.escape`/`.crash` reasons), then `ChainVerifier.verifyTokenEvents` returns `.ok`, proving chain hash determinism across mixed event types under the same v33 anchor. NEW `SessionDatabase.unsafeQueueSync(_:)` test-only extension exposes a raw-SQLite block on the parent queue so chain tests can SELECT the new wasm_* columns directly without going through each store's read path. Two pre-existing tests required in-round contract updates to match the new canonical shape (NOT defects-outside-criteria — these are downstream of the round's deliverable): `MigrationTests::migration22..v32 advance the migration ledger by exactly eleven rows` bumped to twelve (now covers v33); `ChainVerifierTests::firstRowHashMatchesIndependentComputation` added the four wasm_* NULL entries to its independent canonical-map computation so the expected hash matches the writer-side v33 shape. VERIFICATION: targeted `swift test --filter WasmtimeSubprocessRuntime` 4/4 green in 0.108s; full `./tools/test-safe.sh` 8/8 chunks green (parsers 311 / learning 188 / kb 153 / pane 352 / hook 185 / session 332 / onboarding 105 / other 1451). Test count delta 2980 → 2982 (+2). Migration ledger advances v32 → v33. Re-audit verdict (Schneier / Allspaw): PASS clean — Schneier's defense-in-depth concern satisfied (rows ride the existing tamper-evident chain; per-anchor canonical shape switching keeps legacy rows verifiable while the new shape covers every kill; `senkani doctor --verify-chain` transparently covers the new rows); Allspaw's operational concern satisfied (migration follows the exact same anchor-rename pattern as v18 + v23, so the cognitive load on operators reading `chain_anchors` is unchanged; the write-time `useV33Shape` gate is mirrored in the verifier — no drift class possible). Zero defects-outside-criteria filed. Sibling sub-items unblocked: T.3a-5 (12 parameterized integration tests against pre-compiled `.wasm` fixtures) can now build against the shipped `recordWasmKill` writer — its kill-timing assertions will read the chained rows for evidence that the watchdog window held. Originating: `phase-t3a-4-audit-chain-wasm-kill-rows` — fourth of five T.3a sub-items per the 2026-05-21 decompose-mode round.

### May 22 — feature: T.3a-3 fuel + epoch budget flags + DispatchSource 50ms-kill watchdog on `WasmtimeSubprocessRuntime` — third sub-item of the T.3a decomposition per the 2026-05-21 operator-approved split. `Sources/Core/WasmtimeSubprocessRuntime.swift` `run(module:input:)` now extends the wasmtime argv to `["run", "-W", "fuel=\(fuel)", "-W", "timeout=\(epochMs)ms", tmpURL.path]` — wasmtime 45.0.0 exposes the budget knobs under the `-W` Wasm-config namespace (per `wasmtime run -W help`), NOT as top-level `--fuel` / `--max-wall-time` flags as the original t3a-3 acceptance assumed; the build shipped with the correct `-W` syntax and filed `process-gap-t3a-3-acceptance-wrong-wasmtime-flag-names-2026-05-22` as the doc-sync follow-up so any phase-narrative / architecture-spec lines that still carry the wrong flag strings can be cleaned up. NEW `readBudget(from manifest: HandManifest) -> (fuel: Int64, epochMs: Int)` helper — defensive `Mirror`-based reflection that walks `HandManifest`'s top-level children and unwraps optional shapes via a new private `unwrapOptional(_:)` shim, accepting both `Int64?` and `Int64` so future schema migrations are transparent; tolerates future `sandboxFuel: Int64?` / `sandboxEpochMs: Int?` fields without a hard schema dep. Today's `HandSandbox` enum carries neither field, so every call falls back to the t3a-3 defaults `(fuel: 10_000_000, epochMs: 5000)`. T.3b promotes the fields to required and the helper switches to direct reads — runtime API does not change. NEW `armWatchdog(for: Process, epochMs: Int) -> WatchdogHandle` nonisolated method — creates two `DispatchSourceTimer`s on a dedicated `com.senkani.wasmtime.watchdog` queue. Kill timer schedules at `.now() + .milliseconds(epochMs + 50)`, checks `process.isRunning`, sends `process.terminate()` (SIGTERM), and reschedules the escalate timer at `+50ms`. Escalate timer's handler re-checks `process.isRunning` and sends `kill(processIdentifier, SIGKILL)` via the Darwin/Glibc `kill(_:_:)` syscall (gated on `#if canImport(Darwin) / Glibc`). Total kill window worst-case is `epochMs + 100ms`, well inside the T.3a parent's stated tolerance. NEW top-level `WatchdogHandle` struct owns the timer pair and exposes a single idempotent `cancel()`. `run()` invokes `defer { watchdog.cancel() }` immediately after arming so every exit path — happy, throw, watchdog-driven kill — releases both timer sources. Route B has no warm pool to share; the defensive cancellation matters under concurrent `run()` invocations. CRITICAL `DispatchSource` lifecycle pattern documented inline at `armWatchdog`: both timers are created suspended (per the `DispatchSource.makeTimerSource(queue:)` contract) and MUST be resumed at least once before `cancel()` / deinit, or libdispatch crashes with a SIGTRAP precondition fail ("release of suspended source"). First implementation attempt called `setEventHandler` on the escalate timer lazily inside the kill timer's handler, leaving the escalate timer suspended on the happy path — `swift test --filter WasmtimeSubprocessRuntime` crashed with signal code 5 in 0.120s into the echo test. Fix: hoist the escalate timer's `setEventHandler` + `resume()` up to creation time, park at `.distantFuture` until the kill timer reschedules it. This pattern is now documented inline so future watchdog-shape additions don't reintroduce the bug. NO new tests this round — t3a-5 owns the kill-timing parameterized tests against fuel-* / wall-* / escape-* `.wasm` fixtures. NO changes to `Sources/Core/HandManifest.swift` (read-only access via reflection; schema bump is T.3b). NO changes to MCP / CLI surface. VERIFICATION: targeted `swift test --filter WasmtimeSubprocessRuntime` 2/2 green in 0.127s (the echo fixture round-trips successfully under the `-W` syntax); full `./tools/test-safe.sh` 8/8 chunks green on first attempt — parsers 311 / learning 188 / kb 153 / pane 352 / hook 185 / session 330 / onboarding 105 / other 1451. Test count delta 2980 → 2980 (+0). Re-audit verdict (Torvalds / Schneier): PASS clean — Torvalds's API concern satisfied (stdlib `Process.terminate()` + Darwin/Glibc `kill(_:_:)` only; both timers resume up-front so SIGTRAP precondition is unreachable); Schneier's defense-in-depth concern satisfied (soft cap inside wasmtime via `-W fuel=N` + `-W timeout=Nms`, hard cap via host-side SIGTERM → 50ms grace → SIGKILL escalation; total kill window stays under T.3a tolerance; `process.isRunning` guard on both stages prevents spurious signals to already-exited processes). One defect-outside-criteria filed: `process-gap-t3a-3-acceptance-wrong-wasmtime-flag-names-2026-05-22` — the literal flag-string mismatch (`--fuel` / `--max-wall-time` → `-W fuel=N` / `-W timeout=Nms`); P3, size small, doc-only cleanup of phase narrative + architecture spec lines that may still carry the wrong strings. Sibling sub-items unblocked: T.3a-4 (`wasm_kill` audit-chain rows) can build against the shipped watchdog — `armWatchdog`'s kill / escalate handlers are the call sites that need to record the kill into the audit chain. Originating: `phase-t3a-3-fuel-epoch-watchdog` — third of five T.3a sub-items per the 2026-05-21 decompose-mode round.

### May 22 — feature: T.3a-2 `WasmtimeSubprocessRuntime` actor (one-shot subprocess + WASI `_start`) — second sub-item of the T.3a decomposition per the 2026-05-21 operator-approved split; scope-groomed 2026-05-22 (route B chosen over the route-A shim binary + route-C deferral; warm pool + binary framing dropped because t3a-1's bench already showed warm-median 7-8 ms is acceptable for v0.4.0 and the pool benefit is small). NEW `Sources/Core/WasmtimeSubprocessRuntime.swift` — `public actor WasmtimeSubprocessRuntime` with `init(manifest: HandManifest, wasmtimeLookup: WasmtimeLookup? = nil)` (injectable lookup closure so the refusal path is testable without PATH override) + `public func run(module: Data, input: Data) async throws -> Data` (writes module bytes to a `NSTemporaryDirectory()`-anchored `wasmtime-runtime-<UUID>.wasm` temp file with `defer`-based cleanup, spawns `wasmtime run <tempfile>`, pipes `input` to stdin / closes write end / reads stdout + stderr to EOF / waits exit, returns stdout bytes on success or throws `.subprocessFailed` on non-zero). NEW `WasmtimeRunnerError` 2-case enum (`.wasmtime_missing(installHint: String)` for the `which wasmtime` empty-result refusal + `.subprocessFailed(exitCode: Int32, stderr: String)` for spawn + non-zero-exit) with `Equatable` conformance + `CustomStringConvertible` — `Equatable` is what lets the refusal test assert the install-hint string by value. NEW `WasmtimeSubprocessRuntime.installHint = "brew install wasmtime"` static constant — same canonical hint t3a-1's `scripts/bench-wasmtime.sh` + `spec/architecture.md` "WASM runtime decision (2026-05-22)" section already use, so the operator sees one consistent install string regardless of which surface surfaces the refusal. NEW default lookup closure (`WasmtimeSubprocessRuntime.defaultLookup`) runs `/usr/bin/which wasmtime`, trims, throws `.wasmtime_missing` on empty / non-zero exit; memoized after first successful lookup so the per-call cost stays in the bench-confirmed 7-8 ms warm-median envelope rather than paying `which` overhead every spawn. NEW fixture `Tests/SenkaniTests/Fixtures/wasm/echo.wasm` (213 bytes; WASI command exporting `_start` that calls `fd_read` on fd 0 then `fd_write` on fd 1 with the actual bytes-read length) + source `Tests/SenkaniTests/Fixtures/wasm/echo.wat` (commented memory-layout sketch + the `wasm-tools parse` build command) committed for reproducibility. Package.swift `SenkaniTests` target gains `.copy("Fixtures/wasm")` resource registration so the test bundle ships the `.wasm` blob. NO new MCP / CLI surface; NO SQLite migration; NO `ExecTool.swift` edit. VERIFICATION: targeted `swift test --filter WasmtimeSubprocessRuntime` 2/2 green in 0.127s (happy path 0.126s including subprocess spawn + WASI round-trip, refusal 0.001s); full `./tools/test-safe.sh` 8/8 chunks green on first attempt — parsers 311 / learning 188 / kb 153 / pane 352 / hook 185 / session 330 / onboarding 105 / other 1451 (chunk[other] is the catch-all so the new tests land there). Test count delta 2978 → 2980 (+2). Re-audit verdict (Torvalds / Carmack): PASS clean — Torvalds's API concern satisfied (stdlib `Process`/`Pipe`/`waitUntilExit` only, no Foundation-extension or third-party dep; actor isolation is correct for the per-call lifecycle the route-B scope-groom prescribed); Carmack's latency concern satisfied (per-call cold spawn measured at ~126 ms wall-clock end-to-end including fixture load is within the bench-confirmed cold envelope, lookup cached after first call keeps subsequent calls in the warm-median 7-8 ms band, no warm pool means zero pool-state lifecycle complexity for the t3a-3 watchdog to reason about). Zero defects-outside-criteria surfaced during the round; zero follow-up items filed. ### May 22 — feature: V.18b-2 `senkani exec --telemetry` flag — ninth and terminating sub-item of the V.18 chain per the 2026-05-22 operator-approved decomposition (operator interview Q3=(b): V.18b-2 serializes after V.18b-1 so it builds against the helper V.18b-1 lands). NEW `--telemetry` `@Flag` on `Sources/CLI/ExecCommand.swift::Exec`; when set, the child process spawned by `senkani exec` receives `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:<port>` in its env, resolved via the V.18b-1 `RuntimeTelemetryEndpoint.localLoopback()` helper (same persisted-port path the dev-server pane bundle uses). The operator's explicit flag IS the opt-in — unlike V.18b-1's pane path, the dev-server command allowlist does NOT gate `exec`, because `senkani exec` runs arbitrary operator-chosen commands by design. NEW pure helper `Exec.resolveTelemetryEnv(baseEnv:telemetryEnabled:endpoint:) -> [String:String]` layers the OTLP key on top of the parent's env when both the flag is on AND a non-empty endpoint is present; absence of either short-circuits to the unchanged base env, so the failure mode matches V.18b-1's "non-instrumented is the failure mode" semantics. When the operator passes `--telemetry` but the receiver has no bound port (`localLoopback()` returns nil), `senkani exec` writes one stderr line — `senkani: --telemetry passed but runtime-telemetry receiver has no bound port; OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT not injected` — so the operator sees the misconfiguration instead of a silent no-op (closing Schneier's first-pass CONCERN).
