### May 22 — feature: V.18a-7 Agent Timeline runtime-error badge surface — seventh of nine V.18 sub-items per the 2026-05-22 operator-approved decomposition. NEW `Sources/Core/Telemetry/TimelineTelemetryCorrelator.swift` (pure module, ~190 lines) takes a `[TimelineTelemetryCorrelator.EventKeys]` (event id + optional `sessionId`/`toolCallId`/`validationRunId` correlation keys) plus a `[RuntimeTelemetryStore.SpanResult]` window and returns `[Int64: RowCorrelation]` per-event badge + compact summary. Badge tiers: `.error` when any matched span has `status_code = ERROR` (OTLP code 2); `.slow` when no ERROR but at least one matched span exceeds the window-p99 duration threshold; `.none` otherwise. p99 is computed across the entire visible window via `idx = max(0, floor(N × 0.99) - 1)` so the threshold sits at the boundary below which 99% of spans fall — top-1% outliers register under the `duration > p99` strict comparison instead of being hidden when the maximum itself equals p99 (the naïve `idx = floor(N × 0.99)` landing on the max). Window is gated at `count >= 10` so a 1-of-5-spans "p99" is treated as noise, not signal. `CompactSummary` carries ONLY `slowSpans: [SlowSpan(name, durationMs)]` capped at `maxSlowSpansInline = 5` (sorted DESC by duration so the heaviest entries surface first) + `errorCount` + `totalDurationMs` + `primaryTraceId` — by compile-time type signature it has no span-tree field, no `parent_span_id`, no `attributes_json`, no `status_message`. The Schneier-flagged "Span tree is NOT embedded in prompt context — only the compact summary is" invariant (V.18a-7 acceptance bullet 4) is enforced both by type system AND by an exhaustive disallowed-keys assertion in the test suite (rejects `spans`, `tree`, `children`, `attributes_json`, `parent_span_id`, `links`, `events`, `resource`). `Sources/Core/SessionDatabase+TokenEventAPI.swift::TimelineEvent` extended with `sessionId: String?` (additive, defaulted-nil init keeps the 3 existing test-site call shapes source-compatible); `Sources/Core/Stores/TokenEventStore.swift::recentTokenEvents` + `recentTokenEventsAllProjects` SELECT statements + `parseTimelineRows` updated to include the `session_id` column. `SenkaniApp/Views/AgentTimelinePane.swift` refactored from a single `VStack` into `HStack { timelineColumn ; [optional] TimelineSpanSidePane }`. New `correlationTask` polls runtime telemetry on a slower 2 s cadence (vs. the existing 500 ms event refresh) — per-refresh batches the unique sessionId set across the visible 100 events, caps at 10 sessions, fetches up to 200 spans per session via `RuntimeTelemetryStore.querySpans`, runs the pure correlator, and writes the result map to a `@State` dict consumed by `TimelineRow`. Badge dot (6×6 px, red for `.error` or amber for `.slow`) renders inline with `.help(...)` tooltip + accessibility label (`"<n> error span(s) · click for details"` or `"<n> slow span(s) · click for details"`). First tap on a row expands the existing inline detail panel and appends three new monospaced rows: `errors: <count>`, `dur: <ms>`, and a capped `slow:` list of "name — Nms" entries; a small footer hint reads `click again → open trace side pane` when a `primaryTraceId` exists. Second tap (already-expanded row with a badge that has a `primaryTraceId`) sets the pane's `openTraceId` `@State`, which mounts `TimelineSpanSidePane(traceId:)` as a sibling column (`minWidth: 280, idealWidth: 320, maxWidth: 420`) that calls `TelemetryQueryDispatcher.getTrace` on appear and renders one row per span sorted by `start_unix_ns ASC` with `ERR`/`OK` status + name + duration ms columns; a `TRUNCATED` marker appears when the trace exceeds the dispatcher's 10K-span cap. NEW `Tests/SenkaniTests/TimelineTelemetryCorrelatorTests.swift` (V.18a-7 `tests_target: 2`): (1) `badgeCorrelationByCorrelationKeys` builds a 13-span window mixing 10 baseline 5ms spans on session `s-baseline`, one 500ms span on `s-slow`, one 5ms ERROR span on `tc-err` (toolCallId-only correlation), and one 5ms OK span on `run-clean` (validationRunId-only correlation); asserts events keyed on each correlation column resolve correctly (sessionId hit returns `.slow` + correct `primaryTraceId`, toolCallId hit returns `.error` + `errorCount == 1`, validationRunId hit returns `.none` because the matched span is OK + below p99, baseline-only session returns `.none`, event with no keys is omitted from the map entirely); (2) `compactSummaryIsSummaryOnly` writes 20 ERROR spans on one session (every ERROR span counts toward the slow-list filter regardless of p99, so the cap proof is deterministic), asserts `slowSpans.count <= maxSlowSpansInline (= 5)`, that the list is sorted DESC by duration, that `SlowSpan` carries only `(name, durationMs)`, and runs a JSON-encode probe asserting the inline payload exposes exactly `{errorCount, primaryTraceId, slowSpans, totalDurationMs}` while every disallowed full-tree key is absent. VERIFICATION: targeted `swift test --filter TimelineTelemetryCorrelatorTests` 2/2 green in 0.009s; full `swift test` 2973/2973 green in 14.7s; `swift build` clean (one pre-existing `onChange(of:perform:)` deprecation in `ArtifactGalleryView.swift` carries over). Test count delta 2971 → 2973 (+2 net). Re-audit verdict (Majors / Tufte / Schneier): PASS clean — Majors's observability concern satisfied (badge surfaces ERROR + p99 outliers without requiring operator-driven query; correlator is pure-Swift + testable without a live store; refresh is debounced to 2 s and capped at 10 unique sessions per pass so 100-row windows don't induce DB storms); Tufte's data-density concern satisfied (6×6 badge dot uses two colors with no animation; inline summary is monospaced + right-aligned numbers; side pane is a single column with status + name + duration; the inline summary is summary-only and the side pane is gated by a deliberate second click); Schneier's prompt-context concern satisfied (the `CompactSummary` type has no span-tree field by compile-time signature; the disallowed-keys assertion in the test suite catches any future drift; full span tree is fetched only on explicit operator action via `TelemetryQueryDispatcher.getTrace` whose 10K-span cap + receive-time `SecretDetector` redaction already shipped under V.18a-6). Zero defects-outside-criteria surfaced during the round; zero follow-up items filed. Out of scope and queued for subsequent rounds per the operator-approved decomposition: V.18b-1 (dev-server pane allowlist + OTEL env injection), V.18b-2 (`senkani exec --telemetry` flag). Future work the V.18a-7 design accepts but does not require this round: extending `token_events` with `tool_call_id` / `validation_run_id` columns when V.18a-5's `agent_trace_event` linkage proves useful for non-validation tool calls — the correlator's `EventKeys` already accepts those keys today so the schema extension is additive. Originating: `phase-v18a-7-timeline-link` — seventh of nine V.18 sub-items per the 2026-05-22 operator-approved decompose-mode round.

### May 22 — feature: V.18a-6 read-only query tools for runtime telemetry — sixth of nine V.18 sub-items per the 2026-05-22 operator-approved decomposition. NEW `Sources/Core/Telemetry/TelemetryQueryDispatcher.swift` (pure module, ~190 lines) is the shared dispatcher that backs both the MCP tool layer and the CLI subcommand — byte-stable JSON via `[.sortedKeys, .withoutEscapingSlashes]` so MCP + CLI output bytes match (matches the V.18a-4 dispatcher precedent for `validate_browser`). Three public dispatch surfaces: `list(store:projectId:) -> ListResponse` walks `RuntimeTelemetryStore.listDatasets`; `query(store:filter:limit:cursorAfterId:maxResponseBytes:) throws -> QueryResponse` walks `querySpans` with cursor pagination + dual budget enforcement (row + byte) + empty-filter refusal (Schneier: no blind table scans); `getTrace(store:traceId:maxSpans:) -> TraceResponse` walks `spansForTrace` with `truncated: true` when the trace overflows the 10K-span cap (a single trace is one unit, not paginated — operator re-queries with tighter `start_unix_ns` window if needed). Output routing satisfies V.18a-6 acceptance bullet 4: every text field that could carry a leaked secret (span `name`, `attributes_json`, `parent_span_id`, `session_id`, `tool_call_id`, `validation_run_id`) is run through `SecretDetector.scan(...).redacted` before serialisation; numeric columns + random-hex trace/span ids pass through verbatim (regex doesn't fire on hex + the byte budget needs stable widths). Byte budget mechanism (V.18a-6 acceptance bullets 2 + 5): query fetches `limit + 1` rows so it detects row-limit exhaustion without a second probe query; tallies accumulated JSON size during iteration; when adding the next row would exceed `maxResponseBytes` (default 1 MB), returns `next_cursor` = last admitted row's `id` + `truncated_by: byte_budget`; when raw rows exceed clamped row limit, returns `truncated_by: row_limit`; clean exhaustion returns `next_cursor: null + truncated_by: null`. Cursor is monotonic (`WHERE id > cursorAfterId ORDER BY id ASC`) so re-queries with the same filter pick up exactly where they left off. NEW store-layer reader methods on `RuntimeTelemetryStore`: `DatasetRow` struct + `listDatasets(projectId:) -> [DatasetRow]` returns dataset metadata ordered `created_at DESC, id DESC` for deterministic output, scope-filtered by `project_id` when supplied; `SpanResult` struct (full column set: id, datasetId, traceId, spanId, parentSpanId, name, startUnixNs, endUnixNs, attributesJson, statusCode, sessionId, toolCallId, validationRunId) + `QueryFilter` struct (`datasetId / traceId / sessionId / toolCallId / validationRunId / startUnixNsAtOrAfter / endUnixNsAtOrBefore` — every field optional but at least one MUST be set) + `querySpans(filter:limit:cursorAfterId:)` with `hasAnyFilter` guard returning empty on blind scans; `spansForTrace(traceId:maxSpans:)` walks `idx_runtime_telemetry_span_trace` ordered `start_unix_ns ASC, id ASC` with cap. THREE new MCP tools registered in `Sources/MCP/Tools/TelemetryTools.swift` + `Sources/MCP/ToolRegistry.swift`: `senkani_telemetry_list` (single optional `project_id` arg), `senkani_telemetry_query` (7 filter args + `limit` + `cursor`), `senkani_telemetry_get_trace` (required `trace_id` + optional `max_spans`); all three carry `readOnlyHint: true` + `idempotentHint: true` + `openWorldHint: false` annotations. NEW `Sources/CLI/TelemetryCommand.swift` ships `senkani telemetry` parent command with three ArgumentParser sub-subcommands: `list` (`--project-id`), `query` (`--dataset-id` / `--trace-id` / `--session-id` / `--tool-call-id` / `--validation-run-id` / `--start-ns-at-or-after` / `--end-ns-at-or-before` / `--limit` / `--cursor`), `get-trace` (`--trace-id` required, `--max-spans` optional). Output is byte-stable JSON identical to the MCP tool — no human-readable formatting this round (the operator-facing surface for runtime telemetry is the Agent Timeline link landing in V.18a-7; the CLI is a backstop / scripting aid). Registered as `Telemetry.self` in `Sources/CLI/Senkani.swift` subcommands list as the 35th top-level command. 2 new query-tool tests in `Tests/SenkaniTests/TelemetryQueryToolsTests.swift`: (1) `queryLimitAndCursor` writes 7 spans tagged with `session_id = "s-page"`, calls `query` three times with `limit: 3` paginated by cursor, asserts page 1 returns 3 rows + cursor + `truncated_by: rowLimit`, page 2 returns 3 more rows + new cursor + `truncated_by: rowLimit`, page 3 returns the final 1 row + `next_cursor: nil + truncated_by: nil` (clean exhaustion); cross-checks cursor monotonicity (page1.last.id == cursor1, page2.first.id > cursor1); asserts empty filter throws `DispatchError.emptyFilter`; (2) `byteBudgetAndSecretRedaction` writes 5 spans whose `attributes_json` smuggles an Anthropic API key (`sk-ant-api01-AAAA...`, 108 chars), calls `query` with `maxResponseBytes: 500` (deliberately tight), asserts at least 1 but fewer than 5 rows admitted + `truncated_by: byteBudget` + non-nil cursor + every emitted span's `attributes_json` is missing the raw `sk-ant-api01-` prefix AND contains the `[REDACTED:ANTHROPIC_API_KEY]` marker; next-page query with the returned cursor continues admitting + redacting under the same byte budget. One pre-existing test updated: `ToolRouterRegistryTests::registryCoversAllPreviouslyDispatchedTools` expected-tool-set extended by `senkani_telemetry_list`, `senkani_telemetry_query`, `senkani_telemetry_get_trace` (no test logic changed — just the canonical tool-surface drift guard). VERIFICATION: targeted `swift test --filter TelemetryQueryTools` 2/2 green in 0.094s; full `swift test` 2971/2971 green in 14.425s; `swift build` clean. Chunked safe runner test-count: 3,064 → 3,066 (+2 net for the new TelemetryQueryToolsTests suite). Re-audit verdict (Majors / Tufte / Schneier): PASS clean — Majors's observability concern satisfied (cursor-paginated query uses existing v30 + v32 indexes for index-only seeks; per-page byte cap prevents response-blow-up; explicit `truncated_by` enum makes the truncation reason machine-readable); Tufte's data-density concern satisfied (every emitted field carries domain meaning, no padding; byte-stable JSON makes diffs reviewable; pass-results case returns `next_cursor: nil + truncated_by: nil` cleanly for completion detection); Schneier's secret-leak concern satisfied (`SecretDetector.scan` routes every text field including `parent_span_id` / `session_id` / `tool_call_id` / `validation_run_id` — none of which carry secrets in production but the defense-in-depth posture is automatic + adds zero surface); empty-filter rejection at the dispatcher boundary prevents blind table scans (rather than serving them slowly); trace/span ids stay verbatim because they're random hex + adding scan cost wouldn't reduce leak surface. Zero defects-outside-criteria surfaced during the round; zero follow-up items filed. Out of scope and queued for subsequent rounds per the operator-approved decomposition: V.18a-7 (Agent Timeline runtime-error badge — consumes V.18a-6's `query` + V.18a-5's `traceSummary`/`crossCuttingTraceJoin` helpers), V.18b-1 (dev-server pane allowlist + OTEL env injection), V.18b-2 (`senkani exec --telemetry` flag). Per-tool stub HTML pages (`docs/reference/mcp/senkani_telemetry_*.html`) intentionally NOT shipped this round — the prior V.18a-1/-2/-3/-4/-5 sub-items also did not add per-tool stub pages; the topic-map MCP index page (`docs/reference/mcp.html`) sidebar + listing rows + sidebar count update satisfy the doc-sync `mcp_tool_added` rule. Originating: `phase-v18a-6-query-tools` — sixth of nine V.18 sub-items per the 2026-05-22 operator-approved decompose-mode round.

### May 22 — feature: V.18a-5 validation-source wiring for runtime telemetry — fifth of nine V.18 sub-items per the 2026-05-22 operator-approved decomposition. NEW migration v32 closes the schema gap the V.18 scope-groom Q4 decision (2026-05-07) assumed but the existing schema didn't provide: `agent_trace_event` gains `session_id TEXT` + `tool_call_id TEXT` columns + composite index `idx_agent_trace_session_tool` so the cross-cutting JOIN `agent_trace_event ↔ runtime_telemetry_span ON (session_id, tool_call_id)` returns matched rows natively, and `validation_results` gains `validation_run_id TEXT` + index `idx_validation_results_run` as the JOIN key against `runtime_telemetry_span.validation_run_id` (the v30 column from V.18a-1). Chain note: `agent_trace_event` is not a chain participant so its new columns are free; `validation_results.validation_run_id` is deliberately excluded from `ValidationStore.canonicalColumns` (it's a derived link/index field, not a primary fact) so the v22 chain shape verifier walk continues to match without anchor work. Migration is self-contained per the established v8/v10/v14/v16 pattern (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS `agent_trace_event` ahead of the ALTER) so the v21-baseline migration ledger test works against the new ledger row count. `ValidationStore.insertValidationResult` + `insertBrowserValidationResult` gained optional `validationRunId: String?` parameters that bind into the new column; `SessionDatabase+ValidationAPI` mirrors the façade and exposes `validationRunId(forResultId:)` + `mostRecentValidationResultId(sessionId:)` lookups for tests + future query tools. `AgentTraceEventStore` writes both new columns (NULL-safe for pre-v32 rows + non-routed paths), reads them on `fetchByIdempotencyKey` + `rowsInWindow`, and the `AgentTraceEvent` public struct gained `sessionId: String? = nil` + `toolCallId: String? = nil` initializer parameters (backward-compatible additive). `BrowserValidationDispatcher.dispatch` was extended with a `validation_run_id` UUID generation step (dispatcher-synthesized, never caller-supplied per Schneier) + 16-byte hex trace_id + 8-byte hex span_id generation + one OTLP-shape span emission per dispatch via a new optional `spanSink: SpanSink = noopSpanSink` parameter, span attributes encoded as byte-stable sorted-keys JSON carrying only metadata (axes list, result_status, assertions_passed, assertions_failed — no payload, Schneier guard); the dispatched `BrowserValidationRow` carries both `validationRunId` and `toolCallId` through to the persisted `validation_results` row so the JOIN works end-to-end; `Request` gained a `toolCallId: String = UUID().uuidString` defaulted parameter so existing MCP + CLI callers stay source-compatible. MCP `ValidateBrowserTool` + CLI `ValidateCommand` updated to pass `row.validationRunId` through to `insertBrowserValidationResult`. NEW `RuntimeTelemetryStore.traceSummary(validationRunId:) -> ValidationTraceSummary?` returns the validation-failure attach summary the V.18 spec calls for: top-3 slowest spans (by `end_unix_ns - start_unix_ns`), error count (`status_code > 1` per OTLP Error semantic), total duration (`max(end) - min(start)`), trace_id link target, and span count; returns `nil` when no spans are tagged (pass-results case attaches nothing, per V.18 acceptance bullet 5). NEW `RuntimeTelemetryStore.crossCuttingTraceJoin(sessionId:toolCallId:limit:) -> [CrossCuttingTraceRow]` returns one row per matched `(agent_trace_event, runtime_telemetry_span)` pair; SQL refuses to match NULL session_id / NULL tool_call_id rows so pre-v32 traces correctly don't bleed into the JOIN; both helpers walk the new + existing indexes (`idx_agent_trace_session_tool` + `idx_runtime_telemetry_span_session_tool`) so the query stays cheap on long sessions. 4 new validation-source tests in `Tests/SenkaniTests/RuntimeTelemetryValidationSourceTests.swift`: (1) `validationRunIdRoundTrip` asserts `insertValidationResult` with `validationRunId:` writes the id + the round-trip read returns it; backward-compat call shape (no `validationRunId:`) still works + leaves the column NULL; (2) `dispatchEmitsTaggedSpan` runs `BrowserValidationDispatcher.dispatch` with a deterministic pass-stub runner + capturing `spanSink`, asserts exactly one span emitted carrying the dispatch's `validation_run_id` + caller-provided `(session_id, tool_call_id)` + OTLP status code 1 (Ok) + sorted-keys attributes containing axes + result_status but no target URL leak (Schneier); the dispatched `BrowserValidationRow` carries the same `validation_run_id` so the persistence wiring matches; (3) `failureSummaryShape` writes 5 spans (durations 100/200/300/400/500ns, one errored) tagged with a known run id, asserts `traceSummary` returns spanCount=5, errorCount=1, topSlowestSpans=[500, 400, 300]ns, totalDurationNs=4500, traceId matches; pass-results case (no spans tagged with the queried run id) returns nil; (4) `crossCuttingJoinReturnsMatchedRows` writes one paired agent_trace_event + span on `(s1, t1)`, one trace-only row with `(s1, t2)` + no span, one span-only row with `(s9, t9)` + no trace, plus one pre-v32-shape row with NULL session_id; both scoped JOIN (`sessionId: "s1", toolCallId: "t1"`) and unscoped JOIN return exactly the one matched pair — the NULL row + the trace-only + span-only rows correctly don't match. Two existing tests updated to reflect the schema delta: `AgentTraceEventStoreTests::schemaShape` expected-columns set extended by `session_id` + `tool_call_id`; `MigrationTests::migration22And23AdvanceLedgerByTwo` ledger-advance count flipped 10 → 11 and `appliedVersions` extended to `[22..32]` (display name updated to reflect v32 inclusion). VERIFICATION: targeted `swift test --filter RuntimeTelemetryValidationSource` 4/4 green in 0.056s; full suite `swift test` 2969/2969 green in 14.148s; `swift build` clean. Re-audit verdict (Majors / Tufte / Schneier): PASS clean — Majors's observability concern satisfied (dispatch span carries the run id + session/tool-call tuple + trace/span ids + OTLP status; attributes JSON is sorted-keys deterministic; `traceSummary` returns the structured shape an `AgentTimelinePane` consumer needs; per-step granularity is a documented follow-up since per-dispatch is sufficient for the V.18a-7 badge story); Tufte's analytics concern satisfied (both helpers return structured values not strings — callers compose the agent-visible text; cross-cutting JOIN is one SQL statement using the new + existing indexes; pass-results case returns nil for the attach so the next agent-visible row attaches nothing per V.18 bullet 5); Schneier's security concern satisfied (validation_run_id is dispatcher-synthesized UUID, never caller-supplied; trace/span ids are random; attributes JSON carries only metadata never payload; cross-cutting JOIN refuses NULL-session matches; chain verifier walk for `validation_results` is unchanged because `validation_run_id` is excluded from `canonicalColumns`; the v32 column add is self-contained so the v21-baseline ledger test continues to pass). Zero defects-outside-criteria surfaced during the round; zero follow-up items filed. Out of scope and queued for subsequent rounds per the operator-approved decomposition: V.18a-6 (read-only query MCP/CLI tools — `senkani_telemetry_list/query/get_trace` consuming this round's `traceSummary` + `crossCuttingTraceJoin` helpers), V.18a-7 (Agent Timeline runtime-error badge — consumes both helpers via `AgentTimelinePane`), V.18b-1 (dev-server pane allowlist + OTEL env injection), V.18b-2 (`senkani exec --telemetry` flag). Per-step span granularity (one span per `ValidationStep` rather than one per dispatch) is filed as an out-of-scope follow-up the V.18a-7 round can re-scope if the badge surface needs it. Originating: `phase-v18a-5-validation-source` — fifth of nine V.18 sub-items per the 2026-05-22 operator-approved decompose-mode round.

### May 22 — feature: V.18a-4 receive-time privacy filter for runtime telemetry — fourth of nine V.18 sub-items per the 2026-05-22 operator-approved decomposition. NEW `Sources/Core/Telemetry/OTLPPrivacyFilter.swift` ships a pure module that takes a decoded OTLP attribute dict + a `HandRuntimeTelemetry.CaptureMode` and returns the privacy-filtered dict ready to be JSON-encoded into the V.18a-1 `attributes_json` column. Three modes: `.metadata` (default — drops `http.request.body`, `http.response.body`, `http.request.header*`, `http.response.header*`, `http.request.cookies`, `http.response.cookies`, `rpc.request.body`, `rpc.response.body`, `rpc.request.metadata`, `rpc.response.metadata`, `messaging.message.body`, `messaging.message.payload`, `db.statement.parameters`, `process.env.*`, `process.environment_variables`, `user.email`/`user.name`, `enduser.id`/`enduser.email`, `client.address` attribute key prefixes entirely, and routes every kept value through `SecretDetector` so an accidentally-embedded API key in `url.full` / `db.statement` is still redacted before persist), `.redactedBodies` (captures the sensitive keys but every value sensitive AND non-sensitive runs through `SecretDetector`), `.full` (verbatim pass-through, no filter — requires operator to populate `validated_fields`). OTLP attribute extraction wired into both wire formats: `OTLPDecoder.decodeSpan` now walks Span field 9 (repeated KeyValue) and `OTLPDecoder.decodeLogRecord` walks LogRecord field 6 (same shape) using a new `decodeKeyValue` + `renderAnyValue` pair covering five `AnyValue` primitives (string field 1 / bool field 2 / int field 3 / double field 4 / bytes field 7 with a `b64:` rendering prefix); composite `array_value` and `kvlist_value` are skipped as a deliberate fidelity gap (documented in `spec/architecture.md`). The V.18a-3 placeholder of stashing `{"otlp_raw_b64":"..."}` in `attributes_json` is GONE — every span/log row now carries a privacy-filtered, sorted-keys, stable-JSON-encoded structured attribute object. OTLP/JSON path mirrors the protobuf path via `decodeJSONAttributes` honoring both camelCase + snake_case `stringValue`/`boolValue`/`intValue`/`doubleValue`/`bytesValue` keys plus OTLP-spec string encoding of 64-bit ints. Log-body handling: `LogRow.bodyText` is treated as a synthetic `log.body` attribute by the filter so it gets the same per-mode treatment (kept + SecretDetector-scanned in `.metadata`/`.redactedBodies`, pass-through in `.full`). `RuntimeTelemetryReceiver.Config` gains `captureModesBySource: [String: HandRuntimeTelemetry.CaptureMode]` (default empty — sources not registered default to `.metadata`); `processBody` looks up the mode for the `X-Senkani-Source` header and builds the filter closure once per request before dispatching to the decoder. `Sources/Core/HandManifest.swift` adds optional `runtimeTelemetry: HandRuntimeTelemetry?` field (backward-compatible v1 extension — pre-V.18a-4 manifests decode as nil → metadata-mode default at the receiver) with `HandRuntimeTelemetry` struct carrying `capture: CaptureMode` (`metadata` / `redacted_bodies` / `full`) + optional `validated_fields: [String: String]` (per-key reason map for the `// validated: <reason>` operator audit annotation). HandManifest docstring's "v1 frozen" note clarified: backward-compatible optional additions with safe defaults remain allowed under v1 (precedent: `runtimeTelemetry`); breaking changes still require v2. `Sources/Core/HandManifestLinter.swift` gains two new warning rules: (a) when `capture == .full` and `validated_fields` is nil or empty → `runtime_telemetry.validated_fields` warning; (b) per-key warning when a `validated_fields[k]` reason is whitespace-only → `runtime_telemetry.validated_fields[k]` warning. NEW `spec/architecture.md` section `## Runtime telemetry privacy filter — SecretDetector coverage gap (Phase V.18a-4)` documents the accepted-risk surface: novel secret formats slip through (regex-only), attribute keys are not scanned (only values), composite AnyValue types are dropped (fidelity gap, not leak), `process.env.*` is dropped wholesale (no per-key allowlist), log bodies follow the attribute filter. The V.18a-3 trust-boundary section's "Privacy filter on receive (V.18a-4 — pending)" bullet flipped to "(V.18a-4 — shipped 2026-05-22)" with the new behavior fully described. `spec/skills.md` schema-v1 table gains the `runtime_telemetry` row + a new `### runtime_telemetry` subsection documenting the three modes + YAML example + the lint rules table gains the two warning entries. 3 new privacy-filter tests in `Tests/SenkaniTests/OTLPPrivacyFilterTests.swift` cover all three modes against a realistic 9-attribute payload mixing http.method/url/status_code/db.system metadata with sensitive http.request.body/header.authorization/response.body/process.env entries AND a sneaky AWS access key embedded in an otherwise-non-sensitive `messaging.consumer.id`: (1) `metadataModeDropsAndScansKeptValues` asserts sensitive keys gone + non-sensitive kept verbatim + the embedded AKIA-pattern redacted to `[REDACTED:AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID]`; (2) `redactedBodiesModeKeepsButRedacts` asserts sensitive keys retained but their `sk-ant-` / `sk-proj-` / `sk-` values rewritten to the corresponding `[REDACTED:ANTHROPIC_API_KEY]` / `[REDACTED:OPENAI_PROJECT_KEY]` / `[REDACTED:OPENAI_API_KEY]` markers (no original secret bytes survive) while non-secret values like `{"ok":true}` pass through verbatim; (3) `fullModePassesThroughAndLinterWarns` asserts `full` mode is bit-exact pass-through AND that `HandManifestLinter.lint(...)` emits the new warning when `runtime_telemetry.capture: full` lands with empty `validated_fields`, is quiet when every captured key has a non-empty reason, and warns per-key when a reason is whitespace-only. ### May 22 — feature: V.18a-3 RuntimeTelemetryReceiver actor (127.0.0.1 OTLP/HTTP, OTLP/protobuf + OTLP/JSON, 413/415, per-source rate cap, drop counter, no-auth-loopback misuse fixture) landed — third of nine V.18 sub-items per the 2026-05-22 operator-approved decomposition. NEW `Sources/Core/Telemetry/` package ships four files: `RuntimeTelemetryReceiverConfig.swift` (Codable port + drop-counter + per-source-cap snapshot persisted to `~/.senkani/runtime-telemetry-receiver.json`, with `SENKANI_HOME` env override for tests, via the shared `SettingsIO` atomic-write + backup helpers), `OTLPWireReader.swift` (minimal protobuf wire-format reader — varint, tag, length-delimited, fixed64, fixed32 — sufficient to walk the OTLP `ExportTraceServiceRequest` / `ExportLogsServiceRequest` nesting without taking a dependency on swift-protobuf; unknown fields skipped by wire type for forward compatibility; `OTLPHex` companion encodes the 16-byte trace_id / 8-byte span_id into the canonical hex strings the V.18a-1 schema stores), `OTLPDecoder.swift` (lifts `[SpanRow]` from both protobuf and JSON traces bodies + `[LogRow]` from both protobuf and JSON logs bodies — five Span fields extracted: trace_id / span_id / parent_span_id / name / start_time_unix_nano / end_time_unix_nano plus status code; JSON path honors both camelCase and snake_case keys plus the OTLP/JSON-spec string encoding of fixed64 ints; raw body bytes / JSON object stashed in `attributes_json` as `{"otlp_raw_b64":"..."}` so V.18a-4 can re-filter at receive without re-shipping the receiver), `RuntimeTelemetryReceiver.swift` (`@unchecked Sendable` final class wrapping a BSD socket loopback listener on a dedicated `receiver-accept` queue + per-connection short-lived dispatch on a concurrent `receiver-conn` queue — pattern lifted from `EgressListener` including fd-ownership-by-local-capture, peer-address belt-and-braces check that drops any non-loopback peer, and `SO_RCVTIMEO` read timeout on the request head). Receiver enforces all V.18a-3 acceptance bullets: bind 127.0.0.1 only (sockaddr_in literal `0x7F00_0001` — not a configurable string), routes `POST /v1/traces` and `POST /v1/logs` only (everything else → 404), refuses `Content-Type` outside `application/x-protobuf`/`application/json` (with `;`-stripped param tolerance) → 415, refuses bodies whose Content-Length exceeds the configurable `maxBodyBytes` (default 4 MB) → 413 — checked both at Content-Length parse AND mid-read so an over-promising client cannot drain past the cap, per-source token-bucket rate limiter keyed by the `X-Senkani-Source: <key>` header (default `"default"` when missing) with `perSourceSpansPerSecond` default 1000, overflow drops increment the receiver's `totalDrops` counter (snapshotted to the config file on start / stop for `senkani doctor` to read without IPC). NEW doctor surface in `Sources/CLI/DoctorCommand.swift` (#21): `checkRuntimeTelemetryReceiver` reads the persisted config and prints last-bound port + cumulative drops + rate cap setting + `loopback boundary: performative (local-user trust)` so the operator's mental model never confuses a loopback bind with an authenticated endpoint. NEW `spec/architecture.md` section `## Runtime telemetry receiver — trust boundary (Phase V.18a-3)` documents the trust boundary at the local user account, not the loopback interface — with five defense-in-depth measures (loopback-literal bind, accept-time peer check, 413 body cap, 415 content-type allowlist, per-source rate cap) and explicit operator implications (no `socat`, no SSH `-R`, no Docker port forward; suspected-hostile-process recovery via `runtime-telemetry-receiver.json` deletion + `senkani prune --dataset N --target-bytes 0`). 5 new receiver tests in `Tests/SenkaniTests/RuntimeTelemetryReceiverTests.swift`: (1) `acceptsJSONTracesAndCountsDrops` binds with `perSourceSpansPerSecond: 2`, posts 3 OTLP/JSON spans, asserts HTTP 200 + 2 rows inserted + `currentDrops == 1` + persisted config snapshot port matches `recv.port`; (2) `acceptsProtobufTraces` posts hand-built OTLP/protobuf bytes (`ExportTraceServiceRequest → ResourceSpans → ScopeSpans → Span` with the six required field tags varint-encoded by the test helper) and asserts HTTP 200 + 1 row inserted with the trace_id/span_id round-trip through `OTLPHex.encode`; (3) `rejectsOversizeBodyWith413` builds a receiver with a 4 KB cap, posts an 8 KB body, asserts `HTTP/1.1 413 Payload Too Large` + 0 rows; (4) `rejectsUnknownContentTypeWith415` posts `text/plain`, asserts `HTTP/1.1 415 Unsupported Media Type` + 0 rows; (5) `loopbackBindIsPerformative` (the **no-auth-loopback misuse fixture**) stands up two independent receivers (different stores + different dataset IDs + different ports), posts the same OTLP/JSON payload to each, asserts both accept with HTTP 200 + both row-counts == 1 — directly demonstrating that nothing senkani does grants its receiver exclusive rights to the OTLP scheme on loopback. VERIFICATION: targeted `swift test --filter RuntimeTelemetryReceiverTests` 5/5 green in 0.08s; `swift build --target Core` clean; `swift build --target CLI` clean; full chunked harness `./tools/test-safe.sh` runs the new tests inside `chunk[session]` alongside the V.18a-1/V.18a-2 baselines. Zero new MCP/CLI subcommands ship in V.18a-3 — the receiver is internal plumbing; the operator-visible surface is the `senkani doctor` line + the `~/.senkani/runtime-telemetry-receiver.json` file. Out of scope and queued for subsequent rounds: V.18a-4 (privacy filter at receive — rewrites the `otlp_raw_b64` stash with metadata-only filtered payload, adds `HandManifest.runtime_telemetry.capture` enum + linter warning path), V.18a-5 (validation-source wiring — `ValidationStore` + `PlaywrightSubprocessRunner` emit OTLP with `validation_run_id`), V.18a-6 (read-only query MCP/CLI tools), V.18a-7 (Agent Timeline runtime-error badge), V.18b-1 (dev-server pane allowlist + OTEL env injection — unblocked by V.18a-3 per the parent decomposition's `blocked_by` graph), V.18b-2 (`senkani exec --telemetry` flag — serialized after V.18b-1). ### May 22 — feature: V.18a-2 RuntimeTelemetryStore + per-table 500 MB cap + `senkani prune --dataset` CLI landed — second of nine V.18 sub-items per the 2026-05-22 operator-approved decomposition. NEW migration v31 adds two per-table byte counters (`span_bytes`, `log_bytes`) on `runtime_telemetry_dataset` so the prune write-path can decide which table needs eviction without an aggregate scan on every insert; `bytes_used` (V.18a-1) stays as the denormalised dataset total kept in sync inside the same UPDATE for cheap dataset-level reads. NEW `Sources/Core/Stores/RuntimeTelemetryStore.swift` (`final class @unchecked Sendable` sharing `parent.queue` per the documented `SessionDatabase` queue-affinity invariant — the spec's "actor" wording is shorthand for thread-safe Sendable wrapper; an actual Swift `actor` would conflict with the SQLite-handle-on-queue contract): public API covers `createDataset(projectId:workstreamId:) → Int64`, `insertSpan(datasetId:span:capBytes:) → Int64` (auto-evicts oldest spans when `span_bytes > capBytes`), `insertLog(datasetId:log:capBytes:) → Int64` (mirror for logs), `recordBytes(datasetId:table:delta:countDelta:)` (atomic UPDATE bumping `<table>_bytes` + `bytes_used` + `<table>_count` in one statement so a reader never sees a torn row), `pruneTableToCap(datasetId:table:capBytes:) → Int`, `pruneDatasetToTarget(datasetId:targetBytes:) → (spansDeleted, logsDeleted)` (proportional drain across both tables), `bytesUsed(datasetId:)`, `tableBytes(datasetId:table:)`, `rowCount(datasetId:table:)`. Cap = 500 MB per table per dataset (`RuntimeTelemetryStore.defaultTableCapBytes`). Oldest-evict eviction loop pulls 256-row batches in `(time-column ASC, id ASC)` order using the v30 `idx_runtime_telemetry_<table>_dataset_*` indexes, deletes row-at-a-time with per-row counter decrement so the counter stays exact (no drift even on interrupted prune), and includes defensive drift-repair when `<table>_count == 0` but `<table>_bytes != 0`. Byte-size accounting is the sum of UTF-8 byte counts of all variable-length columns plus a fixed 40 B per-row overhead (covers INTEGER PRIMARY KEY + dataset_id + status code/severity + SQLite page metadata); coarse but deterministic — tests pin the formula so a future schema add bumps the constant intentionally. Wired into both `SessionDatabase.init` paths (singleton + testable `init(path:)`) immediately after `surrogateWritesStore`. NEW `Sources/CLI/PruneCommand.swift` ships `senkani prune --dataset <id> [--target-bytes <N>] [--json]` (default `--target-bytes` = 500 MB so a no-op when the dataset is below the live cap); human output formats bytes via `formatBytes` (B/KB/MB), JSON output emits a single sorted-key record `{dataset, target_bytes, bytes_before, bytes_after, spans_deleted, logs_deleted, noop}`. CLI validates `--dataset > 0` + `--target-bytes >= 0` at entry; the columnname formatter inside the store uses enum-derived literals (never user input) so the dynamic-SQL pattern remains injection-safe. Registered in `Sources/CLI/Senkani.swift` subcommands list as the 35th subcommand. 2 new prune tests in `Tests/SenkaniTests/RuntimeTelemetryPruneTests.swift`: (1) `writeStormEvictsOldest` writes 500 ~700 B spans under a 64 KB synthetic cap and asserts `span_bytes <= cap`, oldest-evict ordering (survivor `MIN(start_unix_ns) > 0`), denormalisation invariant `bytes_used == span_bytes + log_bytes`, and `span_count` matches the on-disk row count; (2) `cliPruneIsIdempotent` fills 200 spans under an oversized cap then runs `pruneDatasetToTarget(target: 32 KB)` twice — first run deletes spans + drains to target, second run deletes 0 spans + 0 logs and leaves `bytes_used` unchanged (pins the CLI's documented idempotence guarantee). Pre-existing `MigrationTests::migration22And23AdvanceLedgerByTwo` (which hard-codes the v22..vN application-count assertion) updated from 9 → 10 rows for v22..v31 inclusion; display name now references the v31 inclusion. VERIFICATION: targeted `swift test --filter RuntimeTelemetry` 6/6 green in 0.145s (4 V.18a-1 migration tests + 2 V.18a-2 prune tests); `swift test --filter Migration` 56/56 green in 1.473s; full chunked harness `./tools/test-safe.sh --skip-daemon-sweep` 8/8 chunks green (chunk[session] +2 tests covering the prune store, chunk[other] unchanged) in 37s wall-time. Test count 3038 → 3040 (+2 net: +2 new in `RuntimeTelemetryPruneTests`; `migration22And23AdvanceLedgerByTwo` was updated in place). CLI smoke verified: `.build/debug/senkani prune --help` lists all four flags with the 524288000 (=500 MB) default reflected in the help text. Re-audit verdict (Majors / Tufte / Schneier): PASS clean — Majors's performance concern satisfied (256-row eviction batch keeps the parent.queue.sync window short; oldest-evict scans use the `(dataset_id, start_unix_ns DESC)` / `(dataset_id, unix_ns DESC)` v30 indexes; byte-counter UPDATE is one statement per row); Tufte's denormalisation concern satisfied (`bytes_used = span_bytes + log_bytes` invariant cross-checked by both new tests; per-row UPDATE keeps the counter exact across partial prunes; defensive drift-repair when the count column hits zero before the byte column converges); Schneier's destructive-action concern satisfied (CLI requires explicit numeric `--dataset` + `--target-bytes`, refuses negatives at parse time, JSON output is machine-auditable with sorted keys, no `--yes` gate needed since `prune` is per-dataset trim, not whole-DB wipe). NEW migration v30 in `Sources/Core/Migrations.swift` creates three telemetry tables co-located in the existing session DB so cross-cutting JOINs (`agent_trace_event ↔ runtime_telemetry_span` on `session_id + tool_call_id`) work natively without `ATTACH` overhead: `runtime_telemetry_dataset` (metadata: project_id, workstream_id, created_at, bytes_used, span_count, log_count), `runtime_telemetry_span` (bulk: trace_id, span_id, parent_span_id, name, start_unix_ns, end_unix_ns, attributes_json, status_code, session_id, tool_call_id, validation_run_id) with FK `ON DELETE CASCADE` to dataset (Tufte audit close — V.18a-2's prune can rely on parent-child semantics), `runtime_telemetry_log` (unix_ns, severity_text, body_text, attributes_json, trace_id, span_id, session_id) with the same FK CASCADE. NEW `SessionDatabase.tuneTelemetryPragmas()` runs OUTSIDE the migration transaction (VACUUM cannot run inside `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`) and is invoked by both `SessionDatabase` initializers after migrations: sets `PRAGMA page_size = 8192` and `PRAGMA auto_vacuum = INCREMENTAL` and runs `VACUUM` only when current pragma values don't match the targets (idempotent — subsequent boots skip the rewrite). SQLite gotcha workaround: `PRAGMA page_size` cannot be changed while the DB is in WAL journal mode, so when a page_size change is required the helper switches `journal_mode = DELETE` for the VACUUM-rewrite then restores `WAL`. The Schneier audit-close VACUUM-pause concern is addressed with two log events (`db.session.telemetry_pragmas_tuning` before / `db.session.telemetry_pragmas_tuned` after) so operators see the one-time cause. 4 new schema/migration tests in `Tests/SenkaniTests/RuntimeTelemetryMigrationTests.swift` cover (1) v30 creates the three tables + six indexes via `sqlite_master` inspection, (2) v30 ledger-advance via `schema_migrations` row count + `user_version` bump + description-contains check, (3) `PRAGMA page_size = 8192` after `SessionDatabase` init, (4) `PRAGMA journal_mode = wal` + `PRAGMA auto_vacuum = 2` (INCREMENTAL) after init — each test spawns a fresh temp-file DB via `SessionDatabase(path:)` so the shared singleton stays untouched. ### May 21 — hardening: `tools/test-safe.sh` pre-test daemon sweep — kills stale `SenkaniApp` / `senkani-mcp-server` / leaked `swift-test` and `swiftpm-testing-helper` and `senkaniPackageTests` processes before each chunk starts so integration tests don't race prior-session daemons holding SQLite locks / listening sockets / port assignments; `--skip-daemon-sweep` (and `SKIP_DAEMON_SWEEP=1`) opt-out for tests that intentionally target a long-running senkani daemon, or when running parallel `test-safe` invocations from multiple shells. Originating: `indexer-backend-iterative-walk-c-2026-05-11` 2026-05-18 evidence section — `ps aux` surfaced two senkani daemons alive across sessions (PID 17389 `tools/soak/runner/SenkaniApp.app/Contents/MacOS/SenkaniApp` at 1102 min CPU, PID 29727 `SenkaniApp --mcp-server` at the same day) that may have held resources expected free by the integration suite, contributing to the full-suite stall the round documented. Implementation: NEW `sweep_stale_daemons()` shell function in `tools/test-safe.sh` (between `preflight()` and `mig_helper_zombie_guard()`) iterates the five canonical patterns, uses `pgrep -f "$p"` to detect matches first and `pkill -f "$p"` only when matches exist (so `pkill` returning non-zero on an empty match is impossible — best-effort hygiene that never aborts the script even when `pkill` itself fails on a single pattern); sleeps 1s after any kill to let the kernel reap before `swift test` launches; logs "no stale daemons found" on a clean machine for idempotent observability. `preflight()` calls `sweep_stale_daemons` as its first step so it fires for `--filter` / `--chunk` / no-arg (`all`) modes but NOT for `--list-chunks` (which never invokes preflight). New `--skip-daemon-sweep` flag added to the case-based arg parser before the catch-all `*)` branch; sets `SKIP_DAEMON_SWEEP=1` which the sweep function honors by returning early. Script docstring header gained a new "Pre-test daemon sweep" paragraph + a `SKIP_DAEMON_SWEEP` entry under "Knobs" documenting the env var + the CLI flag + the concurrent-`swift test` caveat (the `swift-test` substring pattern can collide with a parallel test-safe run in another shell tab; opt-out is the escape valve). VERIFICATION: behavioral isolation tests (sweep function sourced via `sed -n` extraction so the script's case-dispatch doesn't fire) — TEST B (SKIP_DAEMON_SWEEP=1) leaves two canary processes (`exec -a 'SenkaniApp-fake-canary-A' sleep 60` and `exec -a 'senkani-fake-canary-B --mcp-server' sleep 60`) alive; TEST A (no skip) kills both canaries plus a real pre-existing stale daemon (PID 88286, `SenkaniApp --mcp-server` from the operator's Xcode DerivedData build, alive 43 min) — sweep logged "killing 2 stale process(es) matching 'SenkaniApp'" + "killing 2 stale process(es) matching 'senkani.*--mcp-server'"; TEST C (clean machine after kills) logs only "sweep_stale_daemons: no stale daemons found". Integrated CLI flag test: `./tools/test-safe.sh --skip-daemon-sweep --filter NonExistentTestXYZ123` with a fresh canary kept the canary alive across the script's preflight + a real `swift test --filter NonExistentTestXYZ123` invocation (Build complete! / 0 tests executed / canary survived). Notes section of the item explicitly bounded scope away from `/tmp` cleanup since bulk-sweeping could mask a real leak. ### May 21 — defect: `MCPSessionMetricsDiagnosticsTests` parallel-mode flake closed — `Tests/SenkaniTests/MCPSessionTests.swift::MCPSessionMetricsDiagnosticsTests` migrated all four pre-existing tests + two new regression-watch tests to a unique-`tool_name` filter pattern, eliminating the cross-suite contamination where `savingsDebugEnvOptInEmitsPerCallVerbose` recorded 80 events when expecting 1. ROOT CAUSE: `SENKANI_SAVINGS_DEBUG` is a process-global env var + `Logger._testSink` is a process-global storage slot. While the opt-in test set the env to `1` + installed a sink, peer suites running concurrently in parallel mode (`MCPSessionActorIsolationTests.concurrentMutatorsConverge` with `feature: "race"`, `MCPSessionRegistryIsolationTests` with `feature: "registry-iso"`) also called `MCPSession.recordMetrics` and emitted `mcp.metrics.recorded` events through whichever sink was currently installed (ours). `.loggerSinkGate` serializes sink-USING suites against each other; it does NOT block production `Logger.log` writes from peer suites — that's the documented contract limitation in `Tests/SenkaniTests/LoggerSinkGate.swift`. The canonical mitigation (per LoggerSinkGate.swift's body comment) is to filter `sink.events` by a unique field value, mirroring the `pathField(...)` filter `LoggerRoutingTests` uses. FIX: each test stamps its `feature:` argument with a UUID-derived unique value (`"savings-debug-optin-<UUID>"` etc.) and filters `sink.events` by `tool_name == uniqueFeature` before asserting counts. Peer events with `tool_name == "race"` / `"registry-iso"` / `"test"` are excluded by construction. Same shape applied defensively to the three sibling tests in the suite (`negativeCompressionDeltaEmitsDiagnosticEvent`, `positiveCompressionDeltaSuppressesDiagnosticEvent`, `savingsDebugDisabledByDefault`) so the convention is consistent. NEW regression-watch tests `sinkIsolationFirstScopeSeesOnlyOwnEmission` + `sinkIsolationSecondScopeSeesOnlyOwnEmission` written back-to-back demonstrate that two sink-scopes with UUID-stamped unique features each see only their own emissions — satisfies acceptance bullet 4 (sink-isolation pinned explicitly). Suite docstring now carries the full parallel-mode flake mechanism + the LoggerSinkGate.swift filter-convention cross-reference. VERIFICATION: targeted filter `swift test --filter MCPSessionMetricsDiagnostics` 6/6 green in 0.239s (was 4 tests + 2 new); `./tools/test-safe.sh` 8/8 chunks green — chunk[other] 1427 → 1429 (+2 from the new isolation tests); **4 consecutive `swift test` (no args, default parallelism) runs all green** at 12.99s / 12.86s / 11.62s / 11.85s — was 4 deterministic issues per parallel-mode run pre-fix per the 2026-05-13 originating evidence + the 2026-05-18 `swift-test-serial-full-suite-stall-investigation` post-fix verification + the 2026-05-21 `index-engine-hashing-fd-baseline` post-fix verification (the savings-debug flake was the second of the two pre-existing parallel-mode flakes those rounds surfaced; the IndexEngine one closed first per the 2026-05-21 close, this one closes now). Total tests 3043 → 3045. Production code: ZERO changes — the fix is test-only (`test-flake-mcpsession-savings-debug-env-shared-sink-2026-05-13`)

### May 21 — feature: T.6 macOS local notification production wiring landed — SenkaniApp now owns a UN-backed `LocalNotifierBridge`, instantiates a `NotificationRouter` at App boot, requests UN authorization, and the first production producer (`OnboardingMilestoneStore.record` on first-time `firstNonzeroSavings`) fires `NotifyEvent.notifyDone` through the router. NEW `Sources/Core/NotificationDelivery.swift` is the process-global router holder (default `nil` → CLI / MCP / test processes that never call `install(_:)` see no banners; lock-protected install/deliver/reset for testing). NEW `SenkaniApp/Services/UNNotifierBridge.swift` conforms to `LocalNotifierBridge` and schedules immediate `UNNotificationRequest`s through `UNUserNotificationCenter.current()` with per-call UUID identifiers (so a double-fire can't collapse banners) and a `@Sendable` `centerProvider` seam for tests. NEW `SenkaniApp/Services/NotificationBootstrap.swift` exposes `bootstrap(configPath:bridge:)` (loads `~/.senkani/notifications.json` via `NotificationRouter.loadConfig`, builds the router over `StdoutSink` + a UN-backed `MacOSLocalSink`, calls `NotificationDelivery.install(router)`) and `requestAuthorizationIfNeeded()` (calls `UNUserNotificationCenter.current().requestAuthorization(options: [.alert, .sound])` fire-and-forget); `SenkaniGUI.init()` calls both in order — install first so an immediately-following `NotificationDelivery.deliver(...)` reaches the now non-nil router, authorization request second since UN's grant is async-cached and the in-process router is correct regardless of the operator's decision. Production producer: `Sources/Core/OnboardingMilestoneStore.swift::record` now resolves the first-record flag inside `recordLock`, releases the lock, and fires `NotifyEvent.notifyDone(toolName: "onboarding", summary: copy.title)` if and only if (a) this is the first record for the milestone AND (b) the milestone is `.firstNonzeroSavings` — the celebrate moment ("Save your first tokens"). `projectSelected` is intentionally silent because users who just configured the app don't need a banner to confirm what they just clicked; this round's frontmatter explicitly chose one user-visible signal over noisy fan-out. `PresetPrerequisiteCheck` doc comment + `probe` switch now treat `macos-local-notification-sink` as shipped (probe returns nil — no warning) since the App boot wires `NotificationDelivery` before any preset can fire an event. The Pushover sink stays as a known gap (always warns) per its separately-tracked backlog item. 8 new swift-testing cases in `Tests/SenkaniTests/NotificationDeliveryTests.swift` cover (i) default `nil` holder + silent no-op `deliver`, (ii) install + fan-out to subscribed `MacOSLocalSink` via `SpyLocalNotifierBridge` with payload-byte assertions, (iii) install-replaces-prior (second `install` wins; first router's bridge stays empty), (iv) ConfirmationGate-adjacent subscription scoping (a sink subscribed only to `notifyFailure` + `scheduleEnd` MUST NOT receive `notifyDone`), (v) `OnboardingMilestoneStore.record(.firstNonzeroSavings)` fires NotifyEvent on first record and the second record is a no-op (no re-fire), (vi) `OnboardingMilestoneStore.record(.projectSelected)` is silent (no banner), (vii) production producer is no-op when `NotificationDelivery` is uninstalled (CLI / test default), (viii) `PresetPrerequisiteCheck.check` for a synthetic preset declaring `macos-local-notification-sink` returns zero warnings + the prereq in `ready`. The `@Suite` is `.serialized` because tests share the process-global holder. Targeted run green in 0.017s (8/8 cases); full chunked harness via `./tools/test-safe.sh` green across all 8 chunks (total 3035 → 3043, +8 from this round, all in chunk[other]). Acceptance bullets 1-6 + 8-10 satisfied; bullet 7 (real macOS banner integration test) and bullet 11 (re-run surface-pass walk step 2) require operator-machine state and are routed to MANDATORY follow-ups (a) `t6-notification-cowork-banner-walk-2026-05-21` (status `manual + groomable: true` — Cowork-runnable banner verification) and (b) `t6-settings-notifications-matrix-ui-2026-05-21` (status `manual + scope_groomable: true` — operator decides whether the matrix UI ships in v0.4.0 or v0.5.0); bullet 4-secondary (`scheduleEnd` from CLI launchd path) is filed as (c) `t6-schedule-end-cli-to-app-bridge-2026-05-21` (status `manual + scope_groomable: true` — needs IPC/XPC architecture decision before build); bullet 8-secondary (deeper ConfirmationGate respect at the router layer if today's per-sink event filter is judged insufficient by the operator pane round) is filed as (d) `t6-notification-confirmation-gate-deeper-respect-2026-05-21` (status `manual + scope_groomable: true`). Originating: `release-v0-3-0-surface-pass` Step 2 sub-check filed as `t6-notification-production-hookup-missing-2026-05-17`. Luminary verdict (Norman / Sutherland / Kleppmann): PASS clean — Norman's user-facing concern satisfied (one celebrate moment, deterministic, opt-out-able via the disk config); Sutherland's UI-discipline concern satisfied (single producer per round, hierarchy-of-acceptance respected via four follow-up filings, App-boot wiring is the only mutable global state); Kleppmann's correctness concern satisfied (`NotificationDelivery` is lock-protected with snapshot-then-dispatch outside the lock so a slow sink can't block other producers, and the default `nil` state guarantees CLI / test processes see no banners they didn't ask for) (`t6-notification-production-hookup-missing-2026-05-17`)

### May 21 — defect: `IndexEngineHashingTests.hashingDoesNotLeakFDs` migrated from process-global count-difference to fd-set difference for parallel-mode robustness — `Tests/SenkaniTests/IndexEngineHashingTests.swift::hashingDoesNotLeakFDs` is the regression-watch for the 2026-05-15 EMFILE crash fix (`senkani-app-emfile-crash-during-pane-launch`), asserting that the in-process `Insecure.SHA1` rewrite of `IndexEngine.gitBlobHash` doesn't leak fds across a 200-file hash batch. The original shape compared `/dev/fd` entry counts before vs after the loop with a tight `delta ≤ 16` budget; under default-parallel `swift test`, peer test cases (SessionDatabase sidecars, TempSessionDatabase artifacts, etc.) concurrently open files in the same process and inflate the process-global count beyond the budget — a 2026-05-21 run observed `delta=76` against the `≤ 16` budget, while the chunked harness (per-chunk process isolation) avoided the issue. Originating finding: `swift-test-serial-full-suite-stall-investigation-2026-05-18` post-fix full-suite verification (2026-05-21) surfaced this pre-existing test-design gap that was previously masked by the `OnboardingMilestoneStore` lock-inversion hang. Fix: capture the fd SET at each sample (`/dev/fd` entries as `Set<String>`), compute `after.subtracting(before)`, and assert `< 100`. Set-difference excludes fds that peer tests opened-and-closed during the loop window (the flicker no longer survives the post-loop snapshot). The relaxed `< 100` bound absorbs residual peer-held fd noise while still catching the EMFILE-class regression — the per-file-subprocess pre-fix path's lower bound is 200+ concurrent fds, so peer noise + a real leak would clear 100 easily. Same file (`Tests/SenkaniTests/IndexEngineHashingTests.swift`): test display name updated to "hashing 200 files does not leak fds (set-diff < 100 above baseline)"; new private helper `openFDSet() -> Set<String>` replaces the prior `openFDCount() -> Int`; the doc comment on the test body now carries the full parallel-mode robustness rationale (peer-flicker exclusion + relaxed bound) cross-referencing this item. ### May 21 — defect: full-suite `swift test` (parallel default) AB-BA deadlock between `OnboardingMilestoneStore.recordLock` and `testHomeOverrideLock` resolved — the 2026-05-18 originating finding (`swift test` (no args) stalls 30+ min wall / 19s CPU / S-state with 0 bytes of test output) traced to a classic cross-thread lock-order inversion surfaced via `sample` on the hung `swiftpm-testing-helper` (capture at `/tmp/senkani-hang-current.txt`, 2026-05-21): nine cooperative-pool threads parked at `_pthread_mutex_firstfit_lock_wait` for `OnboardingMilestoneStore.swift:214` (`recordLock.lock()` inside `record(_:at:home:env:)`) while one thread (running `MCPSessionRegistryIsolationTests.concurrentRecordMetricsAcrossSessionsDoesNotLeak`) held `recordLock` and was parked one frame deeper at `OnboardingMilestoneStore.swift:128` (`resolveDefaultHome()` → `testHomeOverrideLock.lock()`); peer test `SprintReviewSeedFixtureTests.seedRefusesWhenMilestoneAlreadyCompletedUnlessForced` held `testHomeOverrideLock` (via `withTestHome(home)`'s body covering line 145) and was itself parked at `recordLock.lock()` for an inner `record` call inside the body. AB-BA. Fix: `record(_:at:home:env:)` now resolves `home` BEFORE taking `recordLock` (single line: `let resolvedHome = home ?? resolveDefaultHome()` above the lock), and passes the resolved value to `completed(home:env:)` and `write(_:home:)` so neither re-enters `resolveDefaultHome` inside the critical section. The ordering rule is now `testHomeOverrideLock < recordLock` everywhere — codified in the type-level "Atomicity contract" doc on `OnboardingMilestoneStore`. NEW regression-watch test `Tests/SenkaniTests/OnboardingMilestoneTests.swift::recordWithNilHomeDoesNotDeadlockAgainstWithTestHome` deterministically reproduces the inversion via two `DispatchQueue.global(qos: .userInitiated).async` workers coordinated by a `DispatchSemaphore`: T1 enters `withTestHome(home)` + sleeps 150ms (giving T2 time to commit to `record(home: nil)`) + calls its own inner `record(home: nil)`; T2 waits for T1's "entered" signal then calls `record(home: nil)` directly. Bounded at `.timeLimit(.minutes(1))` with a 30s `DispatchGroup.wait` inside — pre-fix the test fails deterministically at the 30s timeout (`Expectation failed: (timeout → .timedOut) == .success`, verified by a temporary revert), post-fix it completes in 0.164s and the canonical `.projectSelected` assertion holds (T1's inner record landed in the temp home). Full chunked harness 8/8 green in 72s (parsers 10s / learning 3s / kb 6s / pane 11s / hook 2s / session 7s / onboarding 1s / other 31s) — chunk[other] 1418 → 1419 cases (+1 from this round). Both flakes are parallel-mode shared-state issues that the chunked harness avoids by per-chunk process isolation — the canonical CI surface (`tools/test-safe.sh`) remains green and the chunked-as-equivalent rule in `spec/testing.md` continues to hold. The deadlock itself is gone; the surfaced flakes are test-design gaps in pre-existing peer tests, not regressions of the round (`swift-test-serial-full-suite-stall-investigation-2026-05-18`)

### May 21 — defect: latent SQLITE_STATIC dangling-pointer pattern eradicated across `Sources/Indexer/SymbolFTSStore.swift` (11 sites, 1 file) — parallel-drift sweep from the same-day `Sources/Core/` audit. The originating `sqlite-bind-static-dangling-pointer-audit-2026-05-21` round's defects-outside-criteria scan greped all four auto-derived pre-audit roots and surfaced exactly one production-code site outside the round's `Sources/Core/` scope: `SymbolFTSStore.swift` lines 94-98, 121, 135-139, 182 carry the identical `sqlite3_bind_text(stmt, N, (<Swift String> as NSString).utf8String, -1, nil)` pattern. The Indexer module does not participate in the tamper-evident audit chain (FTS5 backing store for code-symbol BM25 search, not an integer-keyed audit table) — corruption mode here is silent FTS5 index drift (a query for "foo" returns rows whose name column reads as garbage from an adjacent bind) rather than ChainVerifier failure — but the underlying Swift-bridge-temporary lifetime mechanism is identical. This round converted ALL 11 production-code bind sites in the file from the `nil` (SQLITE_STATIC) destructor to a new fileprivate `SQLITE_TRANSIENT_DESTRUCTOR: sqlite3_destructor_type = unsafeBitCast(OpaquePointer(bitPattern: -1), to: sqlite3_destructor_type.self)` constant defined at the top of `Sources/Indexer/SymbolFTSStore.swift` (the Indexer SwiftPM target does not depend on Core so the parent round's internal `SQLITE_TRANSIENT_DESTRUCTOR` in `Sources/Core/SQLiteTransient.swift` is not visible here; the local mirror is byte-identical to the Core form and the item's acceptance explicitly authorised this shape over adding a Core dependency). All 11 sites span three call paths: `rebuild` (lines 104-108, the 5 TEXT columns of an INSERT against `symbols_fts`), `update` (line 131 for the DELETE bind enumerated over `removedFiles`, lines 145-149 for the 5 TEXT columns of the per-added-entry INSERT), and `search` (line 192 binding the sanitized FTS5 MATCH query). Note: the parent_finding's frontmatter cited 9 sites at lines 94-98, 121, 135-138; the actual count is 11 — the parent's line-range cite missed line 139 (the `file` column in update's INSERT, same pattern as line 138's `kind` column above it) and line 182 (the search query bind, same Swift-String temporary). All eleven match the documented pattern verbatim and were converted by the same mechanical transform. NEW `Tests/SenkaniTests/SearchFusionTests.swift::ftsRoundTripPreservesAllColumnsByteForByte` in the existing `@Suite("SymbolFTSStore")` (5 → 6 cases in the suite) inserts five `IndexEntry` rows via the public `store.rebuild(entries:)` writer with distinct values per column (so a cross-column corruption like the file path bleeding into container is detectable), queries them back via `store.search(query: "alpha", limit: 50)`, and asserts byte-for-byte equality of every column (`name`, `signature`, `container`, `kind`, `file`, `startLine`) against the originals via a name → original lookup so BM25 ordering doesn't affect the comparison. Pre-conversion the test would not necessarily have caught the latent UB on every run (ARC release timing is non-deterministic) but post-conversion it must stay green forever — and the targeted run is green (6/6 cases pass in 0.030s, including the new round-trip). Full safe-suite chunked run via `./tools/test-safe.sh` green across all 8 chunks (parsers/learning/kb/pane/hook/session/onboarding/other) — chunk[other] 1418 → 1419 cases (+1 from this round, matching the +1 acceptance bullet for the new test). Pre-audit grep `sqlite3_bind_text.*, nil)` against `Sources/Indexer/` returns ZERO hits post-conversion — acceptance bullet 4 satisfied. The wider drift sweep across all four roots (`Sources/`, `SenkaniApp/`, `tools/`, `Tests/`) returns zero production-code hits outside Sources/Core/ and Sources/Indexer/SymbolFTSStore.swift; test-file occurrences (11 files under `Tests/SenkaniTests/`) remain deferred per the parent round's split AND this item's "Out of scope" line — tests are short-lived single-process so the ARC timing concern is materially smaller, and the round's new round-trip test uses the production writer API not raw bind_text. Re-audit verdict (Schneier / Kleppmann): PASS clean — Schneier's silent-index-drift concern satisfied (SQLITE_TRANSIENT copies bytes during the bind call, eliminating the dangling-pointer window; round-trip test proves no byte-corruption survives one rebuild→search cycle); Kleppmann's writer-side-correctness concern satisfied (the destructor argument is a SQLite-side instruction about how the bound bytes are managed, not a writer-side behavior change; bound payload, column types, prepared-statement SQL, FTS5 tokenize config, and BM25 ranking semantics all unchanged). Zero new abstractions beyond the single fileprivate constant that mirrors the parent's Core-internal constant byte-for-byte. Defects-outside-criteria sweep filed zero new items — the round's grep across all four pre-audit roots returned the single Sources/Indexer/SymbolFTSStore.swift parallel that was the round's primary scope and zero other parallels; test-file occurrences are pre-existing parent deferrals not new findings (`sqlite-bind-static-indexer-symbolftsstore-2026-05-21`, defects-outside-criteria split from `sqlite-bind-static-dangling-pointer-audit-2026-05-21`)

### May 21 — defect: latent SQLITE_STATIC dangling-pointer pattern eradicated across `Sources/Core/` (243 sites, 29 files) — every `sqlite3_bind_text(stmt, N, (<Swift String> as NSString).utf8String, -1, nil)` call in `Sources/Core/` was binding an expression-temporary C-string pointer with the `nil` (SQLITE_STATIC) destructor, which requires the pointer to remain valid until `sqlite3_step`; Swift's String→C-string bridge does NOT guarantee that lifetime, so the temporary may be freed before step reads it. The originating bug (`process-gap-validation-results-migration-v22-anchor-pending-2026-05-19` Execution evidence, 2026-05-21) tripped this in `insertBrowserValidationResult` after v29's column-shape evolution forced re-hashing all 18 columns — the verifier detected `category` reading as `["perf"` (an axes-column fragment from a stale-pointer read) and `validator_name` reading as empty; the originating round fixed only the browser writer. This round audited the remaining surface: NEW `Sources/Core/SQLiteTransient.swift` exposes a single internal `SQLITE_TRANSIENT_DESTRUCTOR: sqlite3_destructor_type = unsafeBitCast(OpaquePointer(bitPattern: -1), to: sqlite3_destructor_type.self)` (the canonical SQLite `(sqlite3_destructor_type)(-1)` sentinel that copies the bound bytes during the bind call); a single anchored-regex pass converted 243 bind sites across 29 files (CommandStore 27, TokenEventStore 22, TrustAuditStore 20, EntityStore 15, ValidationStore 12, AnnotationStore 12, SessionDatabase 12, AgentTraceEventStore 11, SessionWorkQueueStore 10, EgressDecisionStore 10, PaneRefreshStateStore 9, PackAuditStore 8, SandboxStore 7, PolicyStore 7, EnrichmentStore 7, SessionEventStreamStore 6, SessionDatabase+WorkBusAPI 6, DecisionStore 6, SurrogateWritesStore 5, EvalResultsStore 5, ContextPlanStore 5, ConfirmationStore 5, ChainRepairer 5, Migrations 3, LinkStore 3, ChainState 2, AnnotationRateCapStore 1, MigrationRunner 1, ChainVerifier 1). The regex anchored on `sqlite3_bind_text(` so `sqlite3_prepare_v2(..., -1, &stmt, nil)`'s 4-arg-after-`-1` shape did NOT match (verified post-conversion); pre-existing `SQLITE_TRANSIENT` local-let usages in `SurrogateVault.swift` and `transient` local-let usage in `ValidationStore.swift::insertBrowserValidationResult` were also not matched (they were the originating round's manually-converted prior art and never had `nil` as the destructor). New `Tests/SenkaniTests/SQLiteTransientBindAuditTests.swift` adds 3 single-row chain-verify + tamper-detection cases mirroring `ValidationResultsMigrationV22AnchorTests.resultStatusTamperDetected`'s shape (`commands.command`, `token_events.tool_name`, `eval_results.fixture_id`) — each test asserts chain-green pre-tamper (proves SQLITE_TRANSIENT round-trip doesn't corrupt the bound bytes) and post-tamper break detection at the tampered row id (proves tamper-evidence still fires on TEXT columns flowing through the converted sites); targeted run green in 0.059s; full safe suite green across all 8 chunks (3031 → 3034, +3). MANDATORY defects-outside-criteria follow-up filed: `sqlite-bind-static-indexer-symbolftsstore-2026-05-21` (parallel-drift site at `Sources/Indexer/SymbolFTSStore.swift` — non-chained FTS5 store with the same latent-UB pattern; corruption mode is silent index drift rather than chain-verifier failure) (`sqlite-bind-static-dangling-pointer-audit-2026-05-21`)

### May 21 — bug: workstream/project remove step ordering reversed — worktree-first → branch-second lets a dual-toggle force-retry heal in ONE call (`remove-step-ordering-worktree-before-branch-2026-05-21`)

- **`SenkaniApp/Models/WorkspaceModel.swift` `removeProject(id:options:)`** — swapped Step 1 (branches) and Step 2 (worktree dirs). The function now runs worktree-remove FIRST, then branch-delete. `// Step 1: worktree dirs` and `// Step 2: branches` comment markers updated accordingly. Docstring step list rewritten + new rationale paragraph explaining one-call dual-toggle force-retry healing.
- **`SenkaniApp/Models/WorkspaceModel.swift` `removeWorkstream(id:from:options:)`** — same swap. Added `// Step 1: worktree dir.` and `// Step 2: branch.` numeric markers (function previously used prose comments without numeric prefixes) to mirror `removeProject` and enable a matching source-level order guard. Docstring step list reordered.
- **`spec/app.md` "Order of execution (model-side)" subsection** — step 1/2 swapped, lead with worktree-first rationale, test-count claim updated 32 → 34 cases.
- **Root cause.** Pre-fix ordering ran `git branch -D` before `git worktree remove`. The dialog's `Force-remove` toggle binds only to `git worktree remove --force` (there is no `--force` flavor of `git branch -D`; `-D` is already the destructive form). For the typical workstream where the branch is checked out at the worktree (any workstream created via `addWorkstream`), the operator's dual-toggle force-retry was structurally broken: Step 1 `git branch -D` still refused (`error: cannot delete branch '<branch>' checked out at '<worktree-path>'`) even though force was on, because the worktree hadn't been removed yet. The operator was forced into a three-click workaround: deselect the branch toggle, force-retry to remove the worktree, re-tick the branch toggle, and click a third time. Reordering so the worktree goes first means worktree-remove `--force` succeeds, detaches the branch, and the same call's Step 2 `branch -D` succeeds against a no-longer-checked-out branch — one operator click for a single conceptual "remove this workstream with force" intent.
- **Tests.** `Tests/SenkaniTests/ProjectWorkstreamRemoveUITests.swift` — two new cases (32 → 34 across seven suites): new `removeWorkstreamOrder` source-level test in Suite 3 asserting `// Step 1: worktree dir.` precedes `// Step 2: branch.` precedes `// Step 3: sidebar` inside the `removeWorkstream` body (mirrors the existing `removeProjectOrder` shape for the analog test on `removeProject`), and new Suite 7d behavioural test `dualToggleForceRetryHealsInOneCall` that drives `/usr/bin/git` against a real temp repo: dual-toggle ON + force=false on call 1 → both fail, sidebar stays (deferred-sidebar invariant); dual-toggle ON + force=true on call 2 → ONE call, worktree removed, branch removed, sidebar dropped, `failures.isEmpty`. The existing `removeProjectOrder` test was updated to assert the new ordering. Three inline mirrors (`mirrorRemoveWorkstream`, `idempotentMirrorRemoveWorkstream`, `buggyMirror`) reordered to match production. Existing Suite 7b/7c tests continue to pass with the new ordering — they exercise the deferred-sidebar and pre-check-idempotency invariants which are independent of step order.
