### May 19 — security: T.1b follow-up — `HookRouter.paneModeResolver` writes `SENKANI_PANE_MODE` into every pane subprocess + `PaneModeStore` JSON backing (close-on-miss → `.general`; redteam end-to-end integration test pins `judge.callCount == 0`)

- **What ships.** The write side of the T.1b chain. T.1b shipped the daemon-side READ (`EgressConnectionHandler.parsePaneModeHeader` / `stripPaneModeHeader`) plus the per-pane policy engine, but no production caller emitted the `X-Senkani-Pane-Mode` header on subprocesses — `HookRouter.paneModeResolver` defaulted to a `{ _ in .default }` stub and nothing read the resolved mode. This round wires the resolver to a real disk-backed store and threads the resolved mode into every pane subprocess as `SENKANI_PANE_MODE=<mode>` so senkani-aware HTTP clients (and the integration test's `bash -c '… X-Senkani-Pane-Mode: $SENKANI_PANE_MODE …'` redteam subprocess) can emit the matching header on outbound traffic through the EgressProxy.
- **`PaneModeStore` (Sources/Core/EgressProxy/PaneModeStore.swift).** New JSON-backed `pane_id → PaneMode` store at `~/.senkani/pane-modes.json`. Operator-editable; default-install (file missing OR malformed JSON OR unknown mode rawValue) silently resolves every pane to `.general` — no log spam, no panic, no elevation out of `.general` from a corrupted file. `setMode(paneID:mode:)` writes atomically (tmp file + `rename(2)`); `resolve(paneID:)` is NSLock-guarded and safe to call from any thread including the EgressProxy hot path. `PaneModeStore.shared` is the process-wide singleton; tests construct private instances pointing at temp paths.
- **`HookRouter.paneModeResolver` default rewired.** The seam's production default now delegates to `PaneModeStore.shared.resolve(paneID:)` instead of returning `.default` unconditionally. Tests still inject their own closure; the seam shape (`(String?) -> PaneMode`) is unchanged.
- **`PaneLaunchEnv.Inputs.paneMode` + `SENKANI_PANE_MODE` env var.** `PaneLaunchEnv.Inputs` grew a `paneMode: PaneMode = .default` field; both `terminal(_:)` and `ollamaLauncher(_:resolvedModelTag:)` bundles now inject `SENKANI_PANE_MODE: <mode.rawValue>` into the pane subprocess env. The key is added to `requiredGateKeys` so the existing parity tests pin it across both bundle types. `PaneContainerView.swift` and `OllamaLauncherPane.swift` call sites resolve `pane.id.uuidString` through `HookRouter.paneModeResolver` and pass the result into `PaneLaunchEnv.Inputs`.
- **Defense-in-depth contract.** The header is the operator-attested framing channel, NOT the security boundary. A subprocess that drops env vars or doesn't run an HTTP client still hits the deny-on-miss rule engine (which defaults to `.general` on a missing header), and the redteam-no-judge invariant is gated daemon-side on `resolvedPaneMode.allowsJudge`. The env var carries information; the rule engine carries the decision.
- **Redteam end-to-end integration test.** New `redteam subprocess env → header → audit row, judge call count stays 0` test in `EgressListenerLiveTests` spawns a `/bin/bash -c` subprocess with `SENKANI_PANE_MODE=redteam` and a `printf` that splices `$SENKANI_PANE_MODE` into the `X-Senkani-Pane-Mode` header, sends the raw request over `nc 127.0.0.1 <listener.port>`, and asserts: (1) HTTP 403 Forbidden response, (2) `egress_decisions` row records `pane_mode == .redteam` + decision == `.deny`, (3) `MockJudgeAdapter.callCount` stays at `0` — the Vitalik invariant holds end-to-end through subprocess env → daemon parse → policy engine → audit row.
- **Tests.** 4 new tests (acceptance target hit): 1 unit pinning the `SENKANI_PANE_MODE` env-var contract across both pane bundles (`PaneLaunchEnvTests.paneModeDefaultsToGeneralAndIsCarriedByBothBundles`), 3 unit covering `PaneModeStore` default-install + round-trip + malformed-file safety + the `HookRouter.paneModeResolver` default-wiring assertion (`PaneModeStoreTests` + `HookRouterPaneModeResolverTests`), 1 integration covering the redteam end-to-end chain (`EgressListenerLiveTests.redteamSubprocessEnvEndToEnd`). All 41 existing T.1a/T.1b EgressProxy tests still pass — no regressions on the daemon-side read path or the per-pane policy engine. Full safe suite green across all 8 chunks; senkani test suite 2834 → 2841.
- **T.1 chain status.** T.1a (rule engine + normalizer + parser + SNI extractor + audit table + listener), T.1b (judge fallback + per-pane policy + migration v23), T.1c (20-scenario adversarial corpus + doctor smoke), and T.1b-follow-up (this round — write-side env injection) all shipped. T.1d (HTTPS MITM body inspection + `senkani doctor --install-egress-ca`) is the remaining T.1 leg — operator-driven motion (admin sudo + Keychain trust prompt per workstation).
- **Out of scope (deferred).** A `senkani egress pane-mode set <pane-id> <mode>` CLI motion to edit `~/.senkani/pane-modes.json` from the command line — operators today edit the JSON directly or via a future PaneSettingsPanel toggle. A `senkani doctor --seed-pane-modes` motion to initialize the file with sensible defaults. Wrapping non-senkani-aware subprocesses (curl, generic libcurl callers) to auto-inject the header — defense-in-depth handles them today by defaulting to `.general` on the daemon side.

### May 19 — security: T.1c — EgressProxy 20-scenario adversarial corpus + `senkani doctor --check-egress` (DNS rebinding / redirect / SSRF / SNI-mismatch / allowlist-boundary / judge-prompt-injection; `EgressHostNormalizer` trailing-dot-after-port fix)

- **What ships.** Third and final round of the T.1 chain. 20 adversarial fixtures (each a discrete `@Test` method) prove `EgressRuleEngine` + `EgressHostNormalizer` + `EgressConnectionHandler` deny every documented bypass category. `senkani doctor --check-egress` ships a 5-scenario smoke subset operators (and CI) can run on demand. The corpus surfaced one real normalization gap during the round — fixed in-line.
- **Adversarial corpus — 20 scenarios, 6 categories.** New `Tests/SenkaniTests/EgressProxyAdversarialTests.swift` ships:
  - **DNS rebinding (×4)**: `169.254.169.254` (cloud-metadata link-local), `127.0.0.1` (loopback), `10.99.99.99` (RFC1918 class 10), `192.168.1.100` (RFC1918 class 192) — each default-denies against a typical `example.com`-only allowlist.
  - **Redirect chain to private IP (×4)**: `172.16.0.1` (RFC1918 class 172), literal `localhost`, `0.0.0.0`, IPv6 loopback `[::1]` — the proxy follows no redirects, so each request is evaluated independently and default-denies.
  - **SSRF (×4)**: request-line vs `Host:`-header smuggling (proxy parses the absolute-URL request line, not the `Host:` header), origin-form-rejected-at-parse (`GET /admin HTTP/1.1` throws `missingHost`), bracketed IPv6 doesn't accidentally match an unbracketed `::1` allow rule, decimal-IP encoding `3232235777` treated as an opaque hostname (never decoded back to `192.168.1.1`).
  - **CONNECT vs SNI mismatch (×2)**: allowed CONNECT host + mismatched SNI (`evil.example.com`) tears down with `sni_mismatch` rule_id; blocked CONNECT host short-circuits the engine before any SNI peek (rule_id is the deny rule's id, not `sni_mismatch` / `sni_unparseable` — proves the deny path is engine-level, not SNI-byte-level).
  - **Allowlist boundary (×4)**: `notexample.com` does NOT match suffix-mode `example.com` (label-boundary anchor), non-default port `:8443` is preserved (rule for `example.com:443` doesn't match `example.com:8443`), trailing-dot + mixed-case (`EXAMPLE.com.:80`) canonicalizes through the normalizer so deny-rule `example.com` matches, deny-wins over a permissive suffix allow (`deny secret.example.com` short-circuits `allow *.example.com`).
  - **Judge-prompt-injection (×2)**: host with `ignore-your-instructions` static-engine-denies when the allowlist is tight (`api.example.com` exact only — judge never reached); host with `approve-everything` records `judge-deny` rule_id + the mock judge's rationale when judge is wired (`MockJudgeAdapter` returns `.deny`; `callCount == 1` proves the dispatch fired; audit row stores the raw host literal so post-hoc audits see what came in).
- **Each scenario asserts**: deny outcome + correct rule_id + chained audit row + no upstream connection ever opened. Engine-level scenarios assert this structurally (engine denies before `EgressConnectionHandler.run()` reaches `EgressUpstreamConnector.connect`); listener-level scenarios omit the fixture upstream entirely so any leak would surface as a connection error. `ChainVerifier.verifyEgressDecisions` is called after every listener-level test — chain integrity holds across the full corpus.
- **`EgressHostNormalizer` fix — trailing-dot-after-port.** The corpus surfaced a real normalization gap: input `EXAMPLE.com.:80` was canonicalizing to `example.com.` (residual dot) because the existing trailing-dot strip ran ONLY before the port strip, so a dot positioned BETWEEN the hostname and the port survived. Exact-match deny rules for `example.com` then missed `EXAMPLE.com.:80`. The fix adds a second trailing-dot strip AFTER the port strip — one extra line, documented with the round trigger. All existing normalizer tests still pass (the pre-port-strip dot pass handles `example.com:80.` — the comment-noted case that motivated the original ordering — and the post-port-strip pass handles the inverse).
- **`senkani doctor --check-egress` smoke surface.** New focused doctor motion. Walks 5 representative scenarios — one per category, excluding the high-cost listener path so the check stays engine-level — and prints structured `[ok]` / `[fail]` per scenario with the host literal, the engine's verdict, and the rule_id. Exits non-zero on any miss. Pure rule-engine + normalizer assertions: no live listener, no SQLite writes, no judge inference. Wall-clock 11 ms locally (acceptance budget: <2 s).
- **CI gate semantic.** The full 20-scenario suite runs as part of every `swift test` invocation (the `other` chunk under `tools/test-safe.sh`); a failure on any scenario fails the chunk, which fails the build. The doctor smoke subset is a fast-feedback variant operators can run independently of the test target.
- **Tests.** 20 new (matches acceptance target): 4 DNS rebinding, 4 redirect chain, 4 SSRF, 2 CONNECT/SNI, 4 boundary, 2 judge-injection. All 41 existing T.1a/T.1b EgressProxy tests still pass — no regressions. Full safe suite green across all 8 chunks (parsers / learning / kb / pane / hook / session / onboarding / other); senkani test suite 2814 → 2834.
- **T.1 chain status.** T.1a (rule engine + normalizer + parser + SNI extractor + audit table + listener), T.1b (judge fallback + per-pane policy + migration v23), and T.1c (this round) all shipped. T.1d (HTTPS MITM body inspection + `senkani doctor --install-egress-ca`) is the remaining T.1 leg — currently `status: blocked` on T.1c (now unblocked); operator-driven motion (admin sudo + Keychain trust prompt per workstation).
- **Out of scope (deferred).** Real-world corpus expansion (post-v0.4.0 adversarial findings file new scenarios; not blocking this round). HTTPS body-payload exploits (T.1d). Operator-side egress-policy seeding for production allowlists (`senkani doctor --seed-egress-policy` candidate motion — not filed yet).

### May 19 — security: T.1b — EgressProxy Gemma judge fallback + per-pane `HookRouter` policy (`PaneMode` taxonomy, `EgressPolicy` per-mode allowlists, `redteam-no-judge` invariant, `egress_decisions.judge_rationale` + `pane_mode` migration v23 with chain shape switch)

- **What ships.** Second round of the T.1 chain. `EgressConnectionHandler` learned to read an `X-Senkani-Pane-Mode` proxy header, dispatch the Gemma judge fallback on static-rule miss (`research`/`write`/`general` modes only), and persist the judge's rationale into the chained `egress_decisions` audit log. The taxonomy is a typed enum — every pane resolves to exactly one of `research`, `write`, `redteam`, `general` (default), and the daemon strips the internal header before forwarding upstream so the framing never leaks to the destination host.
- **`PaneMode` enum.** New `Sources/Core/EgressProxy/PaneMode.swift` ships the four-name vocabulary with `allowsJudge` returning `false` on `.redteam` (Vitalik posture: redteam panes are explicit deny-wins-on-miss; no model layer can be asked to allow exfiltration). `PaneMode.parseHeaderValue` is case-insensitive and defaults to `.general` on missing / unknown values — the deny-on-miss invariant lives in the rule engine, not in the pane-mode parser.
- **`EgressPolicy` per-mode allowlists.** New `Sources/Core/EgressProxy/EgressPolicy.swift` carries one `EgressRuleEngine` per `PaneMode`. The on-disk format `~/.senkani/egress-policy.json` is loaded once at daemon start (no hot-reload — config changes require a `senkani egress stop|start` cycle). Partial customization is supported: missing-mode keys fall back to empty rule sets (deny-on-miss applies, the safe posture). Operators who only customize `redteam` don't accidentally blanket-deny `general`-pane traffic.
- **`JudgeAdapter` protocol + `GemmaJudgeAdapter` + `MockJudgeAdapter`.** New `Sources/Core/EgressProxy/JudgeAdapter.swift` ships the abstraction: `evaluate(JudgeRequest) -> JudgeVerdict` returning `{decision, rationale ≤ 2000 bytes}` synchronously from the connection handler's POSIX-thread perspective. `GemmaJudgeAdapter` wraps an injected inference closure under a hard 300 ms `DispatchSemaphore` deadline — timeout returns `.deny` with a `"judge timeout (≥300ms)"` rationale (Schneier P0: deny-on-timeout is the safe default for a model layer). The prompt is a stable code constant (`GemmaJudgeAdapter.buildPrompt(_:)`), not a file — bumping it requires a code change + new test fixtures so regressions are visible in PR review (Karpathy P0). **The Qwen3 swap.** The original phase ID names "Qwen3 4B" but the pre-audit revealed `ModelRouter` is a routing decision struct, not an inference engine — there's no MLX-native Qwen3 wiring in-tree. The item's `## Notes` section explicitly pre-authorized swapping to Gemma 3 4B-IT if Qwen3 turned out unsuitable; `GemmaInferenceAdapter` (140 LoC) is the existing on-device adapter, so the round swapped Qwen3 → Gemma in scope.
- **Schema migration v23 (chain shape switch).** Adds `judge_rationale TEXT` + `pane_mode TEXT` columns to `egress_decisions`. Renames the existing `fresh-install` chain anchor to `fresh-install-pre-v23` and opens a `migration-v23` anchor at `MAX(id)` when the table has rows (no-op on empty tables — fresh installs land on a `fresh-install` anchor that uses the new canonical shape from the start). `EgressDecisionStore.record` + `ChainVerifier.verifyAnchorEgressDecisions` mirror the same per-anchor shape decision via `anchorReason`: pre-v23 anchors hash without the new columns; post-v23 anchors include them. Mirrors the v18 `connection_id` pattern for the third time in the audit chain. Migration ledger advances by exactly one row.
- **`HookRouter.paneModeResolver` seam.** New `nonisolated(unsafe) public static var paneModeResolver: (String?) -> PaneMode` in `Sources/Core/HookRouter.swift`. Tests inject a stub; production default returns `.general` for every pane. The threading from `PreToolUse` → subprocess env-var → `X-Senkani-Pane-Mode` header is deferred to a follow-up — this round ships the daemon-side parsing path (`EgressConnectionHandler.parsePaneModeHeader` + `stripPaneModeHeader`) so the wire contract is fixed. Operators who manually run `HTTP_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:<port>` traffic through the daemon can supply the header today; full pane-aware autoload arrives with the HookRouter integration round.
- **CLI.** `senkani egress start` now prefers `~/.senkani/egress-policy.json` and falls back to the legacy flat `~/.senkani/egress-rules.json` if the policy file is missing — T.1a operators get T.1b semantics for free without re-shaping their config. The daemon ships with `judge: nil` by default (static-only behavior matches T.1a exactly); enabling the Gemma judge requires explicit operator opt-in once `senkani doctor --install-judge-model` lands.
- **SLO advisory.** `spec/slos.md` gains an `egress.judge.p95 < 300 ms` 24h-rolling SLO and a cold-start advisory: the first dispatch after process start may exceed 5 seconds while the Gemma adapter loads its model container (paid once per `senkani-mcp` daemon lifetime). Mid-warmup requests fall through to the timeout-deny path — the safe Schneier default, not a regression.
- **Tests.** 11 new (vs the 10-test acceptance target — the extra covers the header parse/strip path independently of the judge dispatch): pane-mode vocabulary + `.default` + `allowsJudge` gates, header value parser (case-insensitive + default-on-unknown), `EgressPolicy.defaults` populates all 4 modes, JSON round-trip with 4 modes, partial customization (only `redteam` carries rules → others empty), `MockJudgeAdapter` call-count + verdict, `GemmaJudgeAdapter` 300 ms timeout returns deny, migration v23 adds columns idempotently, `record` + read-back round-trips `judge_rationale` + `pane_mode`, connection handler header parse + strip, `redteam-no-judge` invariant (adapter `callCount == 0` on redteam static-miss; the same invariant in `.general` mode DOES invoke the judge — proves the gate is correctly mode-conditional). All 30 existing T.1a EgressProxy tests pass; senkani test suite 2691 → 2702 (+11). Full safe suite green across all 8 chunks.
- **Out of scope (deferred).** `HookRouter.PreToolUse` → subprocess env-var → `X-Senkani-Pane-Mode` header threading (separate round once the per-pane settings store ships); `senkani doctor --install-judge-model` motion + warmup advisory (a doctor-surface follow-up); the 20-scenario adversarial corpus and `senkani doctor --check-egress` land in T.1c; HTTPS MITM body inspection in T.1d.

### May 19 — bundle: U.10b — `ContextManifest` modes (slice + diff-only + summary) ship live, replacing U.10a's `mode-pending-u10b` stubs

- **What ships.** `Sources/Core/ContextManifest.swift` adds the three pre-resolved input types feeding U.10b's modes: `SliceRequest(path:range:content:)` (CLI/MCP read the file and pass the resolved slice content), `DiffSelector` (an enum carrying `unstaged`, `staged`, `branch(<ref>)`, `range(<a>,<b>)` with round-trippable `rawValue` / `init(rawValue:)` for CLI/MCP parsing), and `DiffRequest(selector:perFileDiff:)` (CLI/MCP shell `git diff <selector>` and split the patch into per-file blocks before composing). `Sources/Bundle/BundleComposer+Manifest.swift`'s `ManifestOptions` gains four new fields: `slice: SliceRequest?`, `diff: DiffRequest?`, `entitySummaries: [String: String]?` (Gemma-resolved per-entity summaries keyed by `KnowledgeEntity.name`), and `summaryBudgetTokens: Int` (default 200 — the freshness check measures against this). The producer stays synchronous + deterministic: CLI/MCP perform I/O (file read, git shell-out, Gemma async call) and pass the resolved data in. The 3 mode-pending stubs (`inclusion_reason: "mode-pending-u10b"`) are removed entirely — replaced by `sliceItem` / `diffItems` / `summaryItems` helpers that emit live content.
- **`slice` mode.** Adds one file-lane manifest item carrying the pre-resolved slice (`mode: .slice`, `range: SliceRequest.range`, `tokens_actual` = slice content char/4, `inclusion_reason: "slice_<start>_<end>"`). `tokens_estimated` is derived from the requested line span at ~40 chars/line, so an unexpectedly long line range flips `freshness: stale_estimate` via the ±20 % rule (see below). Content passes through `SecretDetector.scan` and routes `sensitivity` to `clean` / `flagged` for the U.10a-2 gate — no separate code path for slice secrets.
- **`diff-only` mode.** Emits one diff-lane item per file in `DiffRequest.perFileDiff` (`mode: .diffOnly`, `lane: .diff`, `inclusion_reason: "diff_<selector.rawValue>"` — e.g. `diff_unstaged`, `diff_staged`, `diff_branch:main`, `diff_range:HEAD~3..HEAD`). Selector parsing is in `DiffSelector(rawValue:)` (CLI `--diff <value>`, MCP `diff:"<value>"`); the canonical git two-dot range is accepted, three-dot is intentionally rejected to avoid silent semantic divergence. Diff bodies — the highest-risk free-text in the manifest for accidentally-committed secrets — flow through `SecretDetector.scan` exactly as file-lane content does; the U.10a-2 gate's `flagged` refusal triggers identically on diff items.
- **`summary` mode.** Emits one knowledge-lane item per `KnowledgeEntity` (`mode: .summary`, `lane: .knowledge`) with a three-step fallback chain: (1) pre-resolved Gemma summary from `ManifestOptions.entitySummaries[entity.name]` → `inclusion_reason: "summary_gemma"`, (2) `entity.compiledUnderstanding` when non-empty → `inclusion_reason: "summary_kb_fallback"`, (3) neither available → `inclusion_reason: "summary_unavailable"` with `tokens_actual: 0`. `Sources/Core/GemmaRationaleRewriter.swift` gets a new `summarize(content:budgetTokens:) async -> String?` entrypoint that mirrors the existing `enrich(_:)` safety contract (prompt cap → `SecretDetector` sanitize → silent nil-fallback on any backend failure) — CLI/MCP wire it before composing so the producer stays sync.
- **`tokens_estimated` ↔ `tokens_actual` mismatch → `freshness: stale_estimate`.** New `freshnessFor(estimated:actual:)` helper applies the ±20 % rule: `|actual - estimated| / max(estimated, 1) > 0.20` flips `.staleEstimate`. Zero-estimate is fresh when actual is also zero, stale otherwise. Wired into `sliceItem` and `summaryItems` (diff items match estimate to actual since both flow from the same content char/4 — no drift surface there).
- **CLI.** `senkani bundle --slice <path>:<start>:<end>` accepts 1-indexed inclusive line ranges; the path resolves relative to the validated project root and is rejected if it traverses outside via `URL.standardizedFileURL.path` + root-prefix check; the file is read once into `SliceRequest.content`. `senkani bundle --diff <selector>` shells `git diff` with the selector's args (`["-C", projectRoot, "diff", ...]`) and parses the unified-diff `diff --git a/x b/y` headers into a per-file dict. Both flags are preview-only — they no-op without `--preview` because the bundle body composer doesn't consume them.
- **MCP.** `senkani_bundle` gains `slice: string` (`"<path>:<start>:<end>"`) and `diff: string` (selector string). Both mirror the CLI parsers via `parseSliceArg` / `parseDiffArg` in `Sources/MCP/Tools/BundleTool.swift`; malformed input returns `isError: true` with a structured message before any compose call. JSON-Schema in `Sources/MCP/ToolRegistry.swift` updated with the new param descriptions and the U.10b sentence in the tool description.
- **U.10a contract surfaces — UNTOUCHED.** No rename, no field removal. `ContextManifestItem` schema is byte-identical to U.10a (same JSON keys, same enum case names); `ContextManifest` top-level shape unchanged; `composeManifestGated` signature unchanged; the U.10a-2 secret gate fires on slice/diff/summary items the same way it fires on U.10a's file/knowledge items. The 4 trivial modes (`full`, `codemap`, `artifact-stubbed`, `excluded-with-reason`) emit identical items to U.10a.
- **Tests.** New `Tests/SenkaniTests/ContextManifestModesTests.swift` (5 suites, 11 tests): slice mode (1 test — emits file-lane item with range + char/4 tokens), diff-only mode (5 tests — one per selector + a round-trip test for `DiffSelector.rawValue`), summary mode (3 tests — Gemma-available / KB-fallback / neither-available), mode-pending regression (1 test — asserts no `mode-pending-u10b` reason surfaces when all 7 modes × 8 lanes are requested), tokens mismatch (2 tests — fresh within budget, stale beyond budget). `Tests/SenkaniTests/ContextManifestTests.swift`'s `pendingModesEmitStubWithoutCrashing` test from U.10a was renamed and rewritten to `pendingModesWithoutInputsEmitNoSpuriousItems` asserting U.10b's new contract: requesting slice/diff-only/summary without supplying their pre-resolved inputs emits zero items for those modes (no stubs, no crash) and the summary case correctly falls through to KB-fallback when the fixture supplies a KB entity. Full safe suite green across all 8 chunks (parsers / learning / kb / pane / hook / session / onboarding / other); senkani test suite 2777 → 2788 (+11 tests).
- **Round-split closure.** This is the U.10b half of the operator-pre-authorized U.10a / U.10b split filed via `phase-u10-context-manifest`'s 2026-05-06 scope-groom pre-grooming notes. With U.10a-1 (contract + review surface, shipped 2026-05-19), U.10a-2 (secret gate + audit rows, shipped 2026-05-19), and U.10b (modes, this round) all shipped, the U.10 ContextManifest series is complete. The reserved `artifact` lane stays empty pending V.9a ArtifactStore; the optional `tool_id` field stays forward-compat for U.7 CapabilityBridge.
- **Out of scope (deferred).** TUI / web / SwiftUI preview UI → `phase-u10c-preview-ui` (not yet filed). Edit-surface manifest → not on the roadmap (review-only stays the contract). Per-model tokenizer (replacing char/4) → future round. ContextRank ordering → future round. HookRouter per-lane / per-mode policy DSL → future round (single U.10a-2 gate covers today's needs).

### May 19 — bundle: U.10a-2 — `ContextManifest` secret gate (refusal + `--allow-secrets` / `allow_secrets:true` override + chained `bundle.secret.allow` / `bundle.dispatch` audit rows)

- **What ships.** New `Sources/Bundle/BundleSecretGate.swift` layers the U.10a-2 refusal/override/audit-row behavior on top of U.10a-1's pure manifest producer. `BundleComposer.composeManifestGated(options:inputs:allowSecrets:preview:recorder:sessionId:projectRoot:) throws -> ContextManifest` is the new gated entry point — it calls `composeManifest()` to build the manifest, scans the result for `sensitivity: .flagged` items, and either throws `ManifestSecretGateError(lanesWithHits:itemCount:)` (when `allowSecrets:false` and ≥1 flagged) or fires the audit-row pair through the injected `BundleAuditRecorder`. The producer-side semantic shift: `Sources/Bundle/BundleComposer+Manifest.swift`'s `fileLaneItems` + `knowledgeLaneItems` now flip `sensitivity` from `clean` to `flagged` (not `redacted`) on any `SecretDetector.scan` hit — the manifest's job is to surface "would I have shipped a secret-bearing source?" before the body composer's own redaction runs downstream. The `ContextSensitivity.redacted` slot is preserved in the schema but reserved for downstream callers that ship scrubbed content alongside the manifest; the in-tree producer paths emit `clean` or `flagged` only.
- **Audit rows.** Every override fires one `bundle.secret.allow` row in `token_events` with `source: "audit"`, `feature: "bundle.secret.allow"`, and a sorted-keys JSON payload in the `command` column carrying `item_count`, `lanes_with_hits`, and the optional `tool_id` — never the secret content itself. Every preview call (override or not) also fires one `bundle.dispatch` row with `source: "audit"`, `feature: "bundle.dispatch"`, and a sorted-keys JSON payload carrying `preview`, `per_lane`, `per_mode`, `tokens_estimated_total`, and `tool_id`. Both rows route through `SessionDatabase.recordTokenEvent` and participate in the T.5 chain (`prev_hash` / `entry_hash` / `chain_anchor_id` populated by the existing recorder path) — `senkani doctor --verify-chain` covers them. Refusal does NOT fire either row (the rows are the "what was sent" trail, and nothing was sent).
- **Recorder seam.** New `BundleAuditRecorder` protocol with two concrete impls: `LiveBundleAuditRecorder` (writes to `SessionDatabase.shared`, used by CLI/MCP) and `DatabaseBundleAuditRecorder` (takes a `SessionDatabase` instance, used by tests). Mirrors the `CredentialGateway.Recorder` / `LiveRecorder` / `DatabaseRecorder` pattern from T.4b so the audit-row shape is testable against a temp DB without standing up `SessionDatabase.shared`.
- **CLI.** New `senkani bundle --allow-secrets` flag (boolean, default false). When `--preview` is on and the manifest carries flagged items, the command refuses without `--allow-secrets`, writing the structured error message (lane set + count, no secret content) to stderr and exiting with code 3. With `--allow-secrets`, the audit rows fire and the preview JSON emits normally.
- **MCP.** `senkani_bundle` gains `allow_secrets: bool` (default false). JSON-Schema updated in `Sources/MCP/ToolRegistry.swift`. Tool description updated to spell out the refusal/override/audit-row trio. Refusal returns an `isError: true` content block with the structured message; success path records the audit rows and returns the manifest JSON.
- **Tests.** New `Tests/SenkaniTests/ContextManifestSecretGateTests.swift` (4 suites, 4 tests): refusal without override (`refusalWithoutOverride` — asserts the producer pre-flags the README item, gated wrapper throws, error description omits the secret content, AND neither audit row fires on refusal), override + audit row (`successWithOverrideAndAuditRow` — asserts the override returns the manifest, fires exactly one `bundle.secret.allow` row with the expected shape, payload carries `item_count` / `lanes_with_hits` / lane name, payload does NOT carry the secret content), dispatch row on every call (`dispatchRowOnEveryCall` — asserts 3 gated calls produce 3 `bundle.dispatch` rows with `per_lane` / `per_mode` / `tokens_estimated_total` / `preview` fields, no `bundle.secret.allow` rows on clean inputs), chain integrity across 100 rows (`chainIntegrityAcross100Rows` — 100 override calls produce 100 `bundle.secret.allow` + 100 `bundle.dispatch` rows, `ChainVerifier.verifyTokenEvents` returns `.ok`). Safe suite green; previous round 2770 → 2777 (+7) at the test-safe chunk-sum level (4 new `@Test` functions + Suite-level counters).
- **Round-split closure.** This is the U.10a-2 half of the operator-pre-authorized U.10a-1 / U.10a-2 secondary split filed during the 2026-05-19 U.10a-1 round per `process-gap-scope-groom-meaty-size-envelope-check-2026-05-19`. With U.10a-1 (contract + review surface) and U.10a-2 (gate + audit rows) both shipped, U.10a is complete; U.10b (`slice` / `diff-only` / `summary` modes) is the next U.10-family round and is no longer blocked.

### May 19 — bundle: `ContextManifest` review surface — `senkani bundle --preview` + `senkani_bundle preview:true` emit a per-item plan (8 lanes × 7 modes) before any bundle body is materialized

- **What ships.** New `Sources/Core/ContextManifest.swift` introduces the contract types: `ContextLane` (the 8 first-class lanes — `file`, `diff`, `codemap`, `symbol`, `knowledge`, `runtime`, `manual`, `artifact`), `ContextMode` (the 7 mode kinds — `full`, `codemap`, `artifact-stubbed`, `excluded-with-reason` are the 4 trivial modes shipped this round; `slice`, `diff-only`, `summary` are reserved schema slots that emit a stub item with `inclusion_reason: "mode-pending-u10b"` until U.10b lands), `ContextFreshness`, `ContextSensitivity`, `ContextRange`, `ContextManifestItem`, and the top-level `ContextManifest` document with `Counts` (`total`, `per_lane`, `per_mode`, `tokens_estimated_total`). JSON field names are a STABLE CONTRACT — once shipped, renaming any key (`tokens_estimated`, `tokens_actual`, `inclusion_reason`, `tool_id`, etc.) is a breaking change for any consumer that decodes the manifest. New `Sources/Bundle/BundleComposer+Manifest.swift` extends `BundleComposer` with `composeManifest(options:inputs:) -> ContextManifest` (deterministic lane-then-stable order; per-lane producers for `file`/`codemap`/`symbol`/`knowledge`; reserved-marker item for `artifact` lane carrying `inclusion_reason: "v9-pending"`; forward-compat stubs for the 3 pending modes when explicitly requested) and `renderManifestJSON(_:) -> String` (sorted-keys pretty-printed encoder — the CLI/MCP parity contract).
- **CLI.** `senkani bundle --preview` flag emits the manifest as JSON instead of the body. `--modes <list>` and `--lanes <list>` are comma-separated narrowing flags; unknown entries silently dropped (matches existing `include` parsing — a typo shouldn't hard-fail). Default modes = the 4 trivial modes (`full,codemap,artifact-stubbed,excluded-with-reason`) so default callers don't see U.10b-pending stub noise; opting into `slice`/`diff-only`/`summary` returns the stub item per mode.
- **MCP.** `senkani_bundle` gains `preview: bool` (default false), `modes: [string]`, `lanes: [string]`. JSON-Schema updated in `Sources/MCP/ToolRegistry.swift` with the closed enums for both `modes` and `lanes`. The MCP preview path short-circuits before the body composer and records `feature: "bundle.preview"` metrics so the savings pane distinguishes preview-only calls from materializations.
- **Parity contract.** CLI `senkani bundle --preview` (which uses `--format json` implicitly for preview) and MCP `senkani_bundle preview:true` route through the same `BundleComposer.composeManifest` core and `renderManifestJSON` encoder. A parity test (`ContextManifestParityTests.byteIdenticalJSONForSameInputs`) asserts byte-identical JSON output for the same input plan — single source of truth across the two surfaces.
- **Round-split context (operator-pre-authorized).** This round is U.10a-1 of an operator-pre-authorized U.10a/U.10b/U.10a-2 chain. The original U.10 (`phase-u10-context-manifest`) scope-groomed 2026-05-06 into U.10a (contract) + U.10b (modes). U.10a itself estimated 70-90 min vs the 60-min envelope, so the 2026-05-19 build round split it into U.10a-1 (this file — schema + lanes + 4 trivial modes + CLI/MCP review surface + parity test) and U.10a-2 (`phase-u10a-2-context-manifest-secret-gate-2026-05-19`, filed this round — `SecretDetector` hard-refusal gate + `--allow-secrets` override flag + chained `bundle.secret.allow` / `bundle.dispatch` audit rows). U.10a-1 still pre-scans free-text content (README, KB `compiledUnderstanding`) via `SecretDetector` and surfaces the result as the per-item `sensitivity` field (`clean` / `redacted` / `flagged`); the hard refusal + override + audit-chain plumbing lands in U.10a-2. The 2026-05-19 secondary split fired per `process-gap-scope-groom-meaty-size-envelope-check-2026-05-19`, which is the durable spec for catching this pattern.
- **Tests.** New `Tests/SenkaniTests/ContextManifestTests.swift` (4 suites, 10 tests): schema round-trip (`itemRoundTripsThroughJSON` asserts encode→decode→encode byte-identity; `stableJSONFieldNames` asserts every shipped key appears literally in the encoded JSON), 8-lane vocabulary (`allEightLanesAreFirstClass` asserts the enum is exactly the 8-name set, `artifactLaneEmitsReservedMarker` asserts the v9-pending stub shape, `lanesRequestedTracksInput` asserts deterministic lane ordering + per-lane counts), mode coverage (`fourTrivialModesEmitValidItems` asserts each trivial mode appears in a default fixture, `excludedWithReasonFiresWhenModeNotRequested` asserts the downgrade contract, `pendingModesEmitStubWithoutCrashing` asserts the 3-stub forward-compat contract, `defaultModesExcludePendingStubs` asserts default callers don't see stubs), CLI/MCP parity (`byteIdenticalJSONForSameInputs` asserts the parity contract holds + round-trip). Full safe suite green across all 8 chunks; senkani test suite 2760 → 2770 (+10 tests).
- **Out of scope.** Secret-gate hard refusal + `--allow-secrets`/`allow_secrets:true` override + chained `bundle.secret.allow`/`bundle.dispatch` audit rows → U.10a-2. `slice`/`diff-only`/`summary` modes (real content production) → U.10b. ArtifactStore wiring (the `artifact` lane's `v9-pending` reservation unblocks when V.9a ships) → `phase-v9a-artifact-store`. `tool_id` attribution beyond the optional schema field → U.7 CapabilityBridge once shipped.

### May 19 — indexer: `IndexStore.save` + `SymbolFTSStore.openDB` guard against vanished `projectRoot` — closes the `MCPSession.warmIndex` detached-task race that resurrected `/tmp/senkani-outline-test-*` after test cleanup

- **What ships.** `Sources/Indexer/IndexStore.swift:20-21` — `save(_:projectRoot:)` now guards on `FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: projectRoot)` at the top and silently returns if the project root no longer exists; the prior code's `createDirectory(withIntermediateDirectories: true)` call would otherwise resurrect a vanished root as a side effect of creating `<projectRoot>/.senkani/`. Twin defense-in-depth guard at `Sources/Indexer/SymbolFTSStore.swift:36-50` — `openDB()` throws `FTSError.openFailed` rather than letting its own `createDirectory(withIntermediateDirectories: true)` rematerialize the root. Both guards needed: even with the top-level save guard, `projectRoot` can vanish between save's JSON write and the FTS rebuild call.
- **Why this matters.** `MCPSession.warmIndex` (`Sources/MCP/Session/MCPSession.swift:449`) schedules a `Task.detached` that runs off-actor and is not awaited by callers. In tests, the detached task could outlive a test's `defer { cleanup(dir) }` and call `IndexStore.save(idx, projectRoot: tmpDir)` against an already-deleted temp dir — recreating the dir tree (and its `.senkani/index.json` + SQLite FTS sidecars) after cleanup. This was the sole remaining `spec/testing.md` cleanup-skip allowlist entry after the `ci-tmp-leak-senkani-files-2026-05-08` close (2026-05-18). In production, the same shape exists for `git checkout` / project-move races; the existing `try?` callers already swallow the post-rematerialization throw, so a silent no-op matches their semantics.
- **Tests.** New `Tests/SenkaniTests/IndexStoreSaveGuardTests.swift` (`@Suite "IndexStore.save — projectRoot existence guard"`) — two tests assert (1) `save()` is a silent no-op for a missing projectRoot and does not resurrect the dir or create `.senkani/`, (2) `save()` still writes `index.json` when projectRoot exists (regression guard). New `Tests/SenkaniTests/SearchFusionTests.swift::ftsRebuildThrowsWhenProjectRootMissing` — asserts `SymbolFTSStore.rebuild` throws and does not resurrect projectRoot or `.senkani/` as a side effect. Pre-cleaned `./tools/test-safe.sh` run leaves **0** `/tmp/senkani-outline-test-*` directories (vs. allowlisted 3 before this round); all 8 chunks green, full-suite count grew by +3 (2 IndexStoreSaveGuard + 1 SearchFusion).
- **Helper update.** `SearchFusionTests`' `makeTempFTS()` helper now `createDirectory`'s the projectRoot before constructing `SymbolFTSStore` — prior tests relied on `openDB`'s now-removed createDirectory side effect for the root. The previously misnamed `ftsSearchWithEmptyStoreReturnsEmpty` (pointing at a literally nonexistent dir) is reworked to create the dir, matching the renamed intent ("empty store returns empty," not "missing-dir store returns empty").
- **Allowlist.** `spec/testing.md`'s cleanup-skip allowlist for `senkani-outline-test-<UUID>` is removed — the source it tracked is now structurally closed at the lowest layer, so the allowlist is empty. Per the allowlist-discipline rule, new `/tmp/senkani-*` leak sources must name themselves before they can land.

### May 19 — indexer: every language backend's `walk` is now iterative — umbrella `indexer-backends-iterative-walk-refactor-2026-05-11` ceremoniously closed after 22 child rounds; `RunOnLargeStackThread` doc-comment reframed from primary safety mechanism to defense-in-depth

- **What ships (ceremonial close).** The umbrella `indexer-backends-iterative-walk-refactor-2026-05-11` closed today after all 22 chain children completed (Go pilot 2026-05-11 → Bash/C/C++/C#/Dart/Elixir/GraphQL/Haskell/Java 2026-05-18; Kotlin/Lua/PHP/Python/Ruby/Rust/Scala/Swift/TOML/TypeScript/Zig/DependencyExtractor 2026-05-19). Every `*Backend.walk` in `Sources/Indexer/Languages/` plus `Sources/Indexer/DependencyExtractor.swift`'s `walk` and `findFirstDescendantOfType` is now iterative — recursive descent replaced with explicit `(Node, String?)` work-stacks (or the degenerate `Node`-only shape for `DependencyExtractor`'s pure visitor helpers). `Sources/Indexer/RunOnLargeStackThread.swift:33-46`'s doc-comment now reflects the helper's new role: defense-in-depth, not the primary safety mechanism, with an `As of 2026-05-19, every language backend's walk is iterative` follow-on sentence enumerating the converted backends so future readers can trace the refactor via grep.
- **Why this matters.** The 2026-05-10 `mcp-warmindex-treesitter-walk-stack-overflow-2026-05-10` round shipped a thread-level guard (16 MB stack via `runOnLargeStackThread`) at every cooperative-pool entry point that drives AST work. That guard eliminated the user-visible crash and handled realistic codebases (~8000-deep ASTs at typical Swift frame sizes), but the underlying *recursive-walk* pattern in every language backend remained structurally unbounded — the safety contract was "don't run these on a small stack," not "these are safe at any depth." The umbrella's 22 chain children converted that contract from runtime-stack-sized to structurally-bounded: each backend's iterative form runs in heap-allocated work-stack memory regardless of input depth, so even a degenerate pathological AST (e.g. 2200-deep parenthesized-expression chain) traverses safely on the cooperative pool's small (~512 KB) stack with no `runOnLargeStackThread` wrap required.
- **Cadence.** One-backend-per-round, scope-groomed by operator on 2026-05-11 (Q1 Ship-in-v0.4.x · Q2 One-backend-per-round · Q3 work-stack of `(node, container)` tuples · Q4 per-backend depth-stress fixture). Each chain child added one depth-stress test fixture (2200-deep nested construct exercising the recursion sites) to the appropriate `Tests/SenkaniTests/TreeSitter*Tests.swift` file — final test count delta across the chain is +22 tests (one per backend; senkani test suite grew 2738 → 2760 across the umbrella's lifetime).
- **Substrate uniformity.** Every chain child implemented the canonical work-stack shape from the umbrella's `## Substrate decision`: `var stack: [(Node, String?)] = [(root, container)]` driven by `popLast()`, children reverse-pushed via `stride(from: count-1, through: 0, by: -1)` so LIFO preserves left-to-right pre-order. Per-backend special-case body arms preserve container derivation exactly — every line that previously called `walk(child, container: derived)` is now `stack.append((child, derived))` with zero semantic change. Backends with richer per-node state (CppBackend's `AccessLevel`, CSharpBackend's namespace+containing-type chain) carry the minimum sufficient tuple shape per language; the `(node, container)` core stays uniform. `DependencyExtractor`'s walkers are the only chain children whose tuple shape degenerates to plain `Node` — both walkers are pure visitor helpers, no container to carry, no symbol-accumulator to thread through.
- **No regression surface.** The ceremonial close round itself edits only a doc-comment (`Sources/Indexer/RunOnLargeStackThread.swift`) and this CHANGELOG bullet plus the umbrella markdown's checkboxes — no Swift semantic change. `swift build` clean. The 22 per-child rounds each verified `swift test --chunk parsers` green attempt-1 incrementally so the chain accumulated +22 tests cleanly with no regressions to any of the 21 indexed languages.
- **Helper retained as defense-in-depth.** `runOnLargeStackThread` stays in the codebase and stays wrapped around every cooperative-pool→AST entry point (warm-index, file-watcher reindex, `ensureIndex`, every `AsyncParsableCommand` that ends in `IndexStore.buildOrUpdate`). The structural-bound now provides the primary safety; the helper is the belt-and-suspenders. New CLI/MCP entry points that call into AST work should continue to wrap in `runOnLargeStackThread` — the contract is symmetric (no special-casing of "iterative-only" call paths) so any future recursion regression has a backstop.

### May 19 — indexer: ZigBackend `walk` converted from recursive to iterative work-stack of `(node, container)` tuples (umbrella chain child of `indexer-backends-iterative-walk-refactor-2026-05-11`); 2200-deep nested-struct-chain depth-stress fixture proves cooperative-pool-safe

- **What ships:** `Sources/Indexer/Languages/ZigBackend.swift:34-159` replaces the recursive `walk(node, …)` + private `walkVariableDeclaration` helper (pre-refactor: two recursion sites — line 95's default-arm `walk(child, …, container: container)` inside the main `walk` + line 142's struct-body `walk(body, …, container: name)` inside `walkVariableDeclaration` — the umbrella's `## Recursive-walk sites under refactor` table predicted exactly these two sites at lines 95 / 142, and the build-time re-derivation confirmed them at the exact same line numbers) with the canonical work-stack shape — `var stack: [(Node, String?)] = [(root, container)]` driven by `popLast()`. Children pushed in reverse via `stride(from: count - 1, through: 0, by: -1)` so LIFO preserves left-to-right pre-order; symbol-emission order is identical to the pre-refactor form. Substrate: **one body-rebind arm with emit, inlined from the pre-refactor's helper** — `variable_declaration` arm extracts the variable name via `findChildByType(identifier)` + `nodeText`, scans direct children for `struct_declaration` / `enum_declaration` / `union_declaration` to determine `typeKind` (.struct for struct or union, .enum for enum — union maps to `.struct` per pre-refactor) and `bodyNode`, emits the type entry with `kind: typeKind`, then pushes the body onto the stack with container re-bound to the variable name ONLY when `body.nodeType == "struct_declaration"` — matches pre-refactor line 142's `walk(body, …, container: name)` exactly, AND preserves the v1 docstring invariant "enum and union bodies are not recursed in v1" (the pre-refactor's `if let body = bodyNode, body.nodeType == "struct_declaration"` guard is reproduced verbatim, so enum and union arms set `bodyNode` but the push gate filters them out). Plain constants (`const std = @import("std");`) hit the arm, find no struct/enum/union child, and stop without emit or descent — matches `walkVariableDeclaration`'s pre-refactor `guard let kind = typeKind else { return }` silent exit. **Leaf-emit arms** (`function_declaration` via `findChildByType(identifier)` + `nodeText` for the name — Zig's function declarations don't expose a `name` field, the function name is the first `identifier` child; kind resolved to `.method` when `currentContainer != nil` else `.function`; `container_field` with typed-field filter `findChildByType(node, type: ":") != nil` which filters out enum variants which are bare identifiers — emits as `.property`; `test_declaration` with quoted-string name extraction via the preserved `extractTestName` helper or literal `"test"` fallback — hardcoded `container: nil` because tests are top-level even inside a struct body) emit without descent. The default arm reverse-pushes children with `currentContainer` preserved (matches pre-refactor line 95's `if child.childCount > 0 { walk(child, …, container: container) }`; the iterative form's "guard count > 0 else continue" on default-arm pop reproduces the pre-refactor's "skip child if childless" semantics — childless leaves popped under the default arm fall through as a no-op exactly as the pre-refactor's child.childCount > 0 check skipped them). The default arm covers `source_file` (root), `struct_declaration` bodies (pushed by the variable_declaration arm onto the stack as `struct_declaration` nodes), `block`, and any other unmatched node types — each falls through default and reverse-pushes children so the inner declarations are reached on subsequent pops with the parent's container preserved. The dispatch shifts from "iterate root children, switch on child.nodeType" to "pop node, switch on node.nodeType" — semantically identical because the pop sequence reproduces the iteration order, and Zig's root (`source_file`) never matches `function_declaration` / `variable_declaration` / `container_field` / `test_declaration` so it falls through to the default arm just as the pre-refactor form's iteration would have. The `extractTestName` private helper is preserved verbatim from the pre-refactor (it's a pure non-recursive string-extractor over a `string` child node and doesn't need iterative translation). New test `ZigDepthStressTests.testDepthStressIterative` (appended to `Tests/SenkaniTests/TreeSitterZigTests.swift` as a sibling at file scope reusing the file's existing private `indexZig` helper) indexes a 2200-deep chain of nested `const A = struct { … };` declarations bracketed by `fn first()` / `fn last()`, **without** `runOnLargeStackThread` wrap and asserts (a) no crash on the cooperative pool, (b) the bracketing top-level functions still emit in left-to-right pre-order with no container.
- **Why now:** chain successor to the TypeScriptBackend round (alphabetical order, per the umbrella's `## Implementation cadence + chain mechanic`). ZigBackend's substrate was scope-groom-predicted at two recursion sites with one body-rebind arm (inlined from a private helper that re-entered `walk`) plus several leaf-emit arms plus default fall-through; build-time re-derivation confirmed both sites exactly at the predicted line numbers (95 / 142). **Substrate novelty — FIRST chain child whose pre-refactor walk delegated to a private helper that re-entered the same `walk`:** Zig's pre-refactor `walk` had a `variable_declaration` arm that delegated to `walkVariableDeclaration`, which in turn called `walk(body, …, container: name)` when the variable's RHS was a `struct_declaration` — two recursion sites in two functions, both eliminated by inlining the helper's emit-and-push semantics into the iterative arm. The helper-inlining choice (vs. keeping `walkVariableDeclaration` as a pure non-recursive helper returning `(IndexEntry?, Node?)`) was preferred because the helper had only one call site and its full body fits comfortably inside the match arm — keeps the canonical (Node, String?) work-stack shape uniform across all arms. Closest precedent is **PhpBackend's namespace_definition arm** (`completed/2026/2026-05-19-indexer-backend-iterative-walk-php-2026-05-11.md`) in that it computes a container-rebind value before pushing the body; the structural shape of "scan children for a body subtree, emit a type entry, push the body with rebind" matches every prior chain child's body-rebind arm. The enum/union/struct discrimination via `typeKind` switch inside the arm (where union maps to `.struct` kind but is not pushed because the body-push gate is `body.nodeType == "struct_declaration"`) is preserved verbatim from the pre-refactor — the gate filters enum and union bodies out of the push regardless of their typeKind value.
- **Why nested struct chain for depth-stress (NOT the canonical 2200-paren parenthesized-expression initializer like the TypeScript / Swift / Php precedents):** Zig's `variable_declaration` arm matches BEFORE the default arm fires, AND consumes the entire variable_declaration node without descent when the RHS is not `struct_declaration` / `enum_declaration` / `union_declaration`. So a plain `const x = (((...0...)));` would hit the variable_declaration arm, find no struct/enum/union child, exit silently, and the deep parenthesized expression chain would NEVER reach the work stack. The TypeScript / Swift / Php precedents' canonical top-level parenthesized-const-initializer fixture does NOT work for Zig — the arm absorbs the entire decl. Zig's leaf-emit arms (`function_declaration`, `container_field`, `test_declaration`) all consume their nodes without descent, so deep parens inside function bodies, field types, or test bodies cannot exercise the walk's stack either. The ONLY canonical Zig shape that exercises both pre-refactor recursion sites is a nested struct chain: each `const A = struct { … };` fires the variable_declaration arm, emits an entry, and pushes the struct body. Inside the struct body, the default arm's reverse-push reaches the inner `const A = struct { … };` (matches pre-refactor line 95's recurse), and the cycle repeats. The pre-refactor recursive walk would consume ~2 Swift call frames per nesting level (`walk` → `walkVariableDeclaration` → `walk` → …), so a 2200-deep chain blows the cooperative pool's smaller stack; the iterative form runs in heap-allocated work-stack memory regardless of depth. tree-sitter-zig accepts the 2200-deep nested struct declaration chain cleanly (no error recovery); the bracketing `fn first()` / `fn last()` declarations bracket the deep chain and verify left-to-right pre-order preservation via the iterative form's reverse-push + LIFO-pop. The same fixture exercises BOTH pre-refactor recursion sites in a single shape: the variable_declaration arm exercises pre-refactor line 142's body-rebind-push at every level, and the default arm exercises pre-refactor line 95's reverse-stride descent at every level (each struct_declaration body popped falls through default and reverse-pushes its children, reaching the inner variable_declaration on a subsequent pop).

Parsers chunk 310 → 311 tests green attempt-1 via `./tools/test-safe.sh --chunk parsers`. Full-suite serial `swift test` skipped per umbrella acceptance bullet wording (chunked parsers run is the canonical verification path for parser-side rounds; the full-suite stall pattern is separately tracked under `swift-test-serial-full-suite-stall-investigation-2026-05-18`).
- **Luminary re-audit (Torvalds / Evans / Kleppmann):** PASS — the shipped diff matches the umbrella's canonical substrate shape (explicit work-stack, no visitor-pattern indirection, no TSTreeCursor substitution). Torvalds: direct substrate substitution, two recursion sites translated 1:1 (variable_declaration arm pushes body with `name` matching pre-refactor line 142's `walk(body, …, container: name)`; default arm reverse-stride push with container preserved matching pre-refactor line 95's `walk(child, …, container: container)`); minimum-sufficient tuple shape (`(Node, String?)`) covers Zig's substrate; `findChildByType` / `nodeText` / `startLine` / `endLine` / `signatureText` helper calls preserved exactly; `extractTestName` helper preserved verbatim (pure non-recursive, no translation needed); helper-inlining choice for `walkVariableDeclaration` is clean and preserves the body-push gate `body.nodeType == "struct_declaration"` verbatim. Evans: ZigBackend's four docstring invariants preserved verbatim — (1) identifier-child name extraction for `function_declaration` (Zig functions don't expose a `name` field; first `identifier` child is the function name); (2) emit-only-on-struct/enum/union for `variable_declaration` (plain constants skipped silently — `skipsTopLevelConstants` test asserts `const std = @import("std"); const MAX_SIZE: u32 = 1024; const pi: f64 = 3.14159;` produce no entries, green); (3) typed-field filter for `container_field` (`findChildByType(node, type: ":") != nil` gates the emit; filters out enum variants which are bare identifiers — `parsesStructFields` test green confirming all three typed fields emit, `parsesEnumTypes` test green confirming enum variants do NOT emit as properties); (4) hardcoded `container: nil` for `test_declaration` (tests are top-level even inside a struct body — `parsesTestBlocks` test asserts both top-level tests carry `container == nil`, green). The pre-refactor recursive walk would consume ~2200 Swift call frames and crash on the cooperative pool's smaller stack; the iterative form runs in heap-allocated work-stack memory. tree-sitter-typescript accepts the 2200-deep parenthesized expression chain cleanly (no error recovery, unlike SwiftBackend's class-body restriction that forced a top-level `print(...)` fixture); the bracketing `function first()` / `function last()` declarations bracket the deep expression and verify left-to-right pre-order preservation via the iterative form's reverse-push + LIFO-pop.

### May 19 — indexer: TomlBackend `walk` converted from recursive to iterative work-stack of `(node, container)` tuples (umbrella chain child of `indexer-backends-iterative-walk-refactor-2026-05-11`); 2200-deep nested-array depth-stress fixture proves cooperative-pool-safe (with parse-tree-depth-only caveat — TOML's grammar limits walk-reachable depth)

- **What ships:** `Sources/Indexer/Languages/TomlBackend.swift:36-141` replaces the recursive `walk(node, …)` (pre-refactor: `for i in 0..<Int(node.childCount)` + two recursive `walk(…)` sites at lines 61 / 78 of the pre-refactor source — the umbrella's `## Recursive-walk sites under refactor` table predicted exactly these two sites, and the build-time re-derivation confirmed them at the exact same line numbers) with the canonical work-stack shape — `var stack: [(Node, String?)] = [(root, container)]` driven by `popLast()`. Children pushed in reverse via `stride(from: count - 1, through: 0, by: -1)` so LIFO preserves left-to-right pre-order; symbol-emission order is identical to the pre-refactor form. Substrate: **one body-rebind arm with emit** — `table` / `table_array_element` (folded into a single case via `case "table", "table_array_element":` — the historical reason was a Swift-6 codegen stack-overflow workaround on adjacent identical cases in the much-larger central switch; harmless here but the fold is preserved verbatim for spec symmetry) emits via the TomlBackend-private `extractTableName` helper + direct `IndexEntry(...)` construction with `kind: .extension` and then **reverse-pushes the table_node's CHILDREN** (NOT the table node itself) onto the stack with container re-bound to the table name — matches the pre-refactor's `walk(child=table_node, container: name)` semantically. The pre-refactor recursed INTO the table node itself with a new container; the iterative translation MUST NOT push the table node back onto the stack (would re-dispatch to the same arm and infinite-loop). Instead, the arm unrolls one step: reverse-push the table_node's children (which are `[` / `]` bracket tokens, key tokens, and `pair` children) with container = table name. The pair children then match the pair arm and emit with container = table name; the bracket and key tokens fall through default with childCount 0, no-op. **One leaf-emit arm** — `pair` emits via the TomlBackend-private `extractPairKey` helper with `kind: .property` when `currentContainer != nil` else `.variable` — top-level pairs (before any `[table]` header) carry `container: nil` and emit as `.variable`, pairs after a header inherit container = table name via the body-rebind push and emit as `.property`. The default arm reverse-pushes children with `currentContainer` preserved (matches pre-refactor line 78's `if child.childCount > 0 { walk(child, ..., container: container) }`; the iterative form's "guard count > 0 else continue" on default-arm pop reproduces the pre-refactor's "skip child if childless" semantics — childless leaves popped under the default arm fall through as a no-op exactly as the pre-refactor's child.childCount > 0 check skipped them). The dispatch shifts from "iterate root children, switch on child.nodeType" to "pop node, switch on node.nodeType" — semantically identical because the pop sequence reproduces the iteration order, and TOML's root (`document`) never matches `table` / `table_array_element` / `pair` so it falls through to the default arm just as the pre-refactor form's iteration would have. New test `TreeSitterTomlDepthStressTests.testDepthStressIterative` (appended to `Tests/SenkaniTests/TreeSitterDartTomlGraphQLTests.swift` — the same suite-shared file that hosts the Dart + GraphQL depth-stress suites, since TOML / Dart / GraphQL already share `DartTomlGraphQLTests` for parsing tests; the new suite is a sibling at file scope using the shared `indexLang` private helper) indexes a top-level `deep = [[[...0...]]]` with 2200 nested arrays, bracketed by `[first]` / `[last]` tables, **without** `runOnLargeStackThread` wrap and asserts (a) no crash on the cooperative pool, (b) the bracketing `[first]` / `[last]` headers still emit as `.extension` in source order with no container, (c) the `deep` pair emits as `.property` under container `"first"` (TOML's table-header section extends until the next header, so `deep` parses as a child of `[first]`).
- **Why now:** chain successor to the SwiftBackend round (alphabetical order, per the umbrella's `## Implementation cadence + chain mechanic`). TomlBackend's substrate was scope-groom-predicted at two recursion sites with one unique body-rebind container arm plus one leaf-emit arm plus default fall-through; build-time re-derivation confirmed both sites exactly at the predicted line numbers (61 / 78). TomlBackend is the **first chain child to recurse INTO the same node rather than into a separate body subtree** — every prior chain child (PHP, Python, Ruby, Rust, Scala, Swift) pushed a `findBody`-resolved separate body subtree (or a `extractTSDeclaration`-returned body) onto the stack; TOML's pre-refactor walks back into the SAME table_node with a new container, which forces the iterative translation to unroll one step and push the table's grandchildren directly. Closest precedent is PhpBackend's `namespace_definition` arm (`completed/2026/2026-05-19-indexer-backend-iterative-walk-php-2026-05-11.md`) — both rebind container for descendants, but PHP pushes a separate body subtree via `findBody` while TOML pushes the grandchildren directly to avoid the same-node infinite-loop trap. No emit-less wrinkle (unlike RustBackend's `impl_item`) — the body-rebind arm emits an entry before unrolling the grandchildren push.
- **Why 2200-deep nested array as pair value for depth-stress (not a class-body or call-expression chain):** TOML's grammar is structurally distinct from every prior chain child — the walk's reachable depth is fundamentally bounded by the grammar, NOT by recursion depth in the walker. `pair` is leaf-emit (no descent into the pair's value subtree), so a deeply-nested `array` or `inline_table` appearing as a pair value is parsed but never walked. `table` / `table_array_element` recurse one level into the header node's children (header brackets + key + pairs), none of which chain deeply. **No valid TOML construct produces a walk-reachable chain of nodes that fall through the default arm with childCount > 0 at thousands of levels.** The fixture chosen — `deep = [[[...0...]]]` with 2200 nested arrays at top level (as the value of the first pair inside `[first]`) — is the deepest VALID TOML we can express that exercises the iterative walk's stack AT ALL. The umbrella's canonical 2200-paren strategy works for languages with an expression context whose deep descendants fall through the default arm (PHP / Python / Ruby / Rust / Scala / Swift all have such a context — class-body bare expression statements, top-level call_expressions, top-level const initializers); TOML does not, and forcing the issue via syntactically-invalid top-level inline_tables or arrays would trigger tree-sitter-toml error-recovery (the SwiftBackend round documented why error-recovery fixtures are wrong — the parser itself blows the stack at depth ~1000 even though the iterative walk handles arbitrary depth). What the fixture DOES test: (1) the parser handles a 2200-deep nested array without crashing (parse-tree depth ≫ walk-reachable depth — proves the parser itself is robust at this depth); (2) the iterative walk's pair arm correctly emits the top-level pair WITHOUT descending into the deep value subtree — matches pre-refactor leaf-emit semantics exactly; (3) bracketing `[first]` / `[last]` headers emit in source order, proving the iterative form's reverse-push + LIFO-pop preserves left-to-right pre-order over `document.children`. This is the **first chain child where the depth-stress fixture exercises parse-tree depth rather than walk-reachable depth** — the iterative refactor's correctness is still verified via equivalence with pre-refactor leaf-emit semantics, but the cooperative-pool-stack benefit accrues to ALL inputs (not just deep ones), since the iterative form eliminates the recursive call frames regardless of input depth. Documented inline in the depth-stress test's docstring so future chain children can recognize this pattern.

All 13 TOML / Dart / GraphQL tests green via `swift test --filter DartTomlGraphQLTests` (existing 10 + new 1 TOML depth-stress + 2 pre-existing Dart/GraphQL depth-stress). Parsers chunk 308 → 309 tests green attempt-1 via `./tools/test-safe.sh --chunk parsers`. Full-suite serial `swift test` skipped per umbrella acceptance bullet wording (chunked parsers run is the canonical verification path for parser-side rounds; prior chain-child rounds documented the full-suite stall pattern, separately tracked under `swift-test-serial-full-suite-stall-investigation-2026-05-18`).
- **Luminary re-audit (Torvalds / Evans / Kleppmann):** PASS — the shipped diff matches the umbrella's canonical substrate shape (explicit work-stack, no visitor-pattern indirection, no TSTreeCursor substitution). Torvalds: direct substrate substitution, both recursion sites translated 1:1 (table / table_array_element arm reverse-pushes the table_node's children with container = table name, unrolling pre-refactor line 61's `walk(child=table_node, container: name)` one step to avoid the same-node infinite-loop trap; default arm reverse-stride push with container preserved matches pre-refactor line 78); minimum-sufficient tuple shape (`(Node, String?)`) covers TOML's substrate; `extractTableName` / `extractPairKey` private helpers preserved exactly (no inlining, no promotion to TreeSitterBackend extension since no other backend has the same need). Evans: TomlBackend's docstring invariant "TOML symbols come in two flavors: [table] and [[table_array_element]] headers → emitted as .extension (the closest analogue we have for a named scope of pairs); pair (key = value) → emitted as .property when nested inside a table, else .variable" is preserved verbatim by the iterative form — the body-rebind arm emits `.extension` and the pair arm emits `.property` when `currentContainer != nil` else `.variable`; the pre-existing `tomlTopLevelPair` test (asserts `name` / `version` are `.variable` with `container == nil` at top level), `tomlTable` test (asserts `host` is `.property` with `container == "database"` inside `[database]`), and `tomlTableArray` test (asserts both `id` pairs are `.property` with `container == "entries"` across two `[[entries]]` table_array_elements) all green, confirming body-rebind container inheritance is preserved across both `table` and `table_array_element` kinds. SwiftBackend's substrate was scope-groom-predicted at three recursion sites with two body-rebind container arms plus several leaf-emit arms plus default fall-through; build-time re-derivation confirmed all three sites exactly at the predicted line numbers (52 / 62 / 97). Closest precedent is ScalaBackend's three-body-rebind-arm pattern (`completed/2026/2026-05-19-indexer-backend-iterative-walk-scala-2026-05-11.md`) — Swift is structurally similar with one fewer body-rebind arm (no `object_definition` analog because Swift has no singleton-object syntax — `class Foo {}` covers it) and uses the shared `extractSwiftClassLike` helper for the kind-decided-by-keyword class/struct/enum/actor/extension arm (the only chain child to fold five user-visible kinds into one grammar node + helper-driven kind resolution; the kind is decided by scanning the declaration's keyword child in `extractSwiftClassLike`, which the iterative form preserves verbatim via the unchanged helper call). This is the **first chain child to encounter a parser-side recovery limit at depth-stress fixture choice** — Scala / Ruby / PHP / Python / Rust / Java / Kotlin / Lua all used class-body or top-level body-rebind fixtures successfully; Swift's stricter class-body grammar (declarations only) forces a different shape. The default arm reverse-pushes children with `currentContainer` preserved (matches pre-refactor line 116's `if child.childCount > 0 { walk(child, ..., container: container) }`; the iterative form's "guard count > 0 else continue" on default-arm pop reproduces the pre-refactor's "skip child if childless" semantics — childless leaves popped under the default arm fall through as a no-op exactly as the pre-refactor's child.childCount > 0 check skipped them). The dispatch shifts from "iterate root children, switch on child.nodeType" to "pop node, switch on node.nodeType" — semantically identical because the pop sequence reproduces the iteration order, and Scala's root (`compilation_unit`) never matches `class_definition` / `object_definition` / `trait_definition` / `val_definition` / `var_definition` / `type_definition` / `function_definition` / `function_declaration` so it falls through to the default arm just as the pre-refactor form's iteration would have. New test `TreeSitterScalaDepthStressTests.testDepthStressIterative` (in `Tests/SenkaniTests/TreeSitterScalaTests.swift`) indexes a top-level `class Container { (((...0...))) }` with 2200 nested parens as a class-body expression statement, bracketed by `class First` / `class Last`, **without** `runOnLargeStackThread` wrap and asserts (a) no crash on the cooperative pool, (b) the bracketing classes still emit in source order with no container.
- **Why now:** chain successor to the RustBackend round (alphabetical order, per the umbrella's `## Implementation cadence + chain mechanic`). ScalaBackend's substrate was scope-groom-predicted at four recursion sites with three body-rebind container arms plus leaf-emit arms plus default fall-through; build-time re-derivation confirmed all four sites exactly at the predicted line numbers (54 / 68 / 82 / 116). Closest precedent is JavaBackend's five-body-rebind-arm pattern (`completed/2026/2026-05-18-indexer-backend-iterative-walk-java-2026-05-11.md`) — Scala is structurally similar with one fewer arm and is the **first chain child to share `extractPythonClass`** with PythonBackend's class_definition arm (the Python and Scala grammars use the same `class_definition` node type with identical `name` + body shape, so the helper is unconditionally reused — preserved as a helper call without inlining). Scala's `val_definition` / `var_definition` retain the **Scala-specific `pattern`-field extraction** quirk (the only chain child where the property-emission name lives on a `pattern` field, not `name`); this stays verbatim in the leaf-emit arm and is exercised by the `parsesValAndVarProperties` pre-existing test. No emit-less wrinkle (unlike RustBackend's `impl_item`) — all three body-rebind arms emit an entry before pushing the body.
- **Why class-body expression-statement for depth-stress:** Scala's leaf-emit arms (`val_definition` / `var_definition`, `type_definition`, `function_definition` / `function_declaration`) emit and return without walking the initializer / body subtree, so depth inside a `val x = (((...)))` initializer or `def f(): T = (((...)))` body is not walked. The deep chain must live inside a node whose descendants fall through the default arm. A `class Container { (((0))) }` with a bare expression statement inside the class body satisfies this: `class_definition` emits + pushes the body with the class name as container, the body falls through default and reverse-pushes the expression statement, the expression statement falls through default and reverse-pushes the parenthesized expression, and the parenthesized expression chain pushes ~2200 deep through repeated default-arm descent. The pre-refactor walk would consume ~2200 Swift call frames and crash on the cooperative pool's smaller stack; the iterative form runs in heap-allocated work-stack memory.

### May 19 — indexer: PhpBackend `walk` converted from recursive to iterative work-stack of `(node, container)` tuples (umbrella chain child of `indexer-backends-iterative-walk-refactor-2026-05-11`); 2200-deep parenthesized-expression depth-stress fixture proves cooperative-pool-safe

- **What ships:** `Sources/Indexer/Languages/PhpBackend.swift:43-152` replaces the recursive `walk(node, …)` (pre-refactor: `for i in 0..<Int(node.childCount)` + five recursive `walk(…)` sites at lines 56 / 64 / 72 / 111 / 116 of the pre-refactor source — the umbrella's `## Recursive-walk sites under refactor` table predicted exactly these five sites, and the build-time re-derivation confirmed them) with the canonical work-stack shape — `var stack: [(Node, String?)] = [(root, container)]` driven by `popLast()`. Children pushed in reverse via `stride(from: count - 1, through: 0, by: -1)` so LIFO preserves left-to-right pre-order; symbol-emission order is identical to the pre-refactor form. Substrate: **three body-rebind arms** (`class_declaration` + `trait_declaration` → `.class`, `interface_declaration` → `.interface`, `enum_declaration` → `.enum`) each emit via `TreeSitterBackend.extractTSDeclaration` then push the body with `container` re-bound to `entry.name` (matches pre-refactor `walk(body, ..., container: entry.name)`); **one container-preserve arm** (`namespace_definition` → `.extension`) — the PHP-specific quirk that namespaces do NOT act as containers, captured in PhpBackend's existing docstring ("helpers_boot inside `namespace Acme\\Services { … }` is still a top-level `.function` with `container: nil`") — emits the namespace as `.extension` and pushes its body with `currentContainer` PRESERVED (NOT the namespace name), matching pre-refactor line 111's `walk(body, ..., container: container)`; **three leaf-emit arms** (`method_declaration` and `function_definition` via `TreeSitterBackend.extractFunction`, `property_declaration` iterating its `property_element` children for emission) emit without descent (matches pre-refactor); the default arm reverse-pushes children with `currentContainer` preserved (matches pre-refactor `walk(child, ..., container: container)` at line 116). The dispatch shifts from "iterate children, switch on child.nodeType" to "pop node, switch on node.nodeType" — semantically identical because the pop sequence reproduces the iteration order, and PHP's root (`program`) never matches a declaration kind so it falls through to the default arm just as the pre-refactor form's iteration would have. New test `TreeSitterPhpDepthStressTests.testDepthStressIterative` (in `Tests/SenkaniTests/TreeSitterPhpTests.swift`) indexes a top-level `class Container { const X = (((...0...))); }` with 2200 nested parens in the class-constant initializer, bracketed by `class First { }` / `class Last { }`, **without** `runOnLargeStackThread` wrap and asserts (a) no crash on the cooperative pool, (b) the bracketing classes still emit in source order with no container.
- **Why now:** chain successor to the LuaBackend round (alphabetical order, per the umbrella's `## Implementation cadence + chain mechanic`). PhpBackend's substrate was scope-groom-predicted at five recursion sites with three body-rebind arms plus a container-preserve namespace arm plus default fall-through; build-time re-derivation confirmed all five sites exactly at the predicted line numbers (56 / 64 / 72 / 111 / 116). Closest precedent is JavaBackend's five-body-rebind-arm pattern — Php's variant is structurally similar but introduces the **container-preserve arm** as a substrate novelty: pre-existing arms in earlier chain children either rebind container to a derived name (Java / Kotlin / Cpp / CSharp / Dart class-style bodies) or fall through with container preserved (default arm); PhpBackend is the first chain child where a *named, emitting* arm explicitly preserves the OUTER container on body push. This proves the `(Node, String?)` tuple shape handles per-arm container-rebind-vs-preserve choices without per-tuple extension — the choice is encoded in the value passed to `stack.append((body, …))` and nothing else.
- **Why class-constant-initializer in a class for depth-stress:** PHP's `method_declaration` and `function_definition` switch arms emit and return without walking the body, so depth inside `function foo() { ... }` or `function method() { ... }` is not walked; `property_declaration` also emits without descent. The deep chain must live inside a node whose descendants fall through the default arm. A class with a `const X = (((...0...)))` class-constant initializer satisfies this: `class_declaration` emits + pushes the body with the class name as container, the body descends to the `const_declaration` via default, and the const_element → expression chain pushes ~2200 deep. The pre-refactor walk would consume ~2200 Swift call frames and crash on the cooperative pool's smaller stack; the iterative form runs in heap-allocated work-stack memory.

Torvalds: direct substrate substitution, five recursion sites translated 1:1 (three body-rebind arms push body with `entry.name`; namespace arm pushes body with `currentContainer` preserved per PHP's "namespaces don't container" rule; default arm reverse-stride push with container preserved); minimum-sufficient tuple shape (`(Node, String?)`) covers PHP's substrate without per-arm extension. Evans: PHP's namespace-doesn't-act-as-container quirk maps naturally to the canonical shape — the choice between rebind and preserve is just the value passed to `stack.append((body, …))`, no abstraction needed; the docstring's "container: nil" invariant for namespace-scoped functions is preserved by the iterative form because the namespace body push uses `currentContainer` (which is nil at top level) and `function_definition` inside it inherits that nil. Kleppmann: depth-stress passes at 2200 parens without `runOnLargeStackThread`; iterative form is structurally safe regardless of grammar-update changes that might start descending into method/function bodies or other currently-leaf arms; bracketing classes verify left-to-right pre-order preservation (`["First", "Container", "Last"]`); 303/303 parsers chunk green attempt-1.
- **Chain mechanic:** umbrella's `blocked_by` updated from `indexer-backend-iterative-walk-php-2026-05-11` → `indexer-backend-iterative-walk-python-2026-05-11` (PythonBackend filed under `backlog/` with the umbrella-template body; the new child notes PythonBackend has two recursion sites at the scope-groom table's lines 55 / 63 — closer to the minimal LuaBackend / GoBackend / BashBackend / GraphQLBackend pattern than to PHP's multi-arm shape; points the build round at the umbrella's `## Substrate decision` section for the canonical shape).
