### May 18 — process: `./tools/test-safe.sh --chunk <chunk>` green attempt-1 canonicalized as equivalent to full-suite `swift test` clean for narrow-surface rounds (`iterative-walk-umbrella-chunked-tests-acceptance-2026-05-18`)

- **What ships:** Three documentation edits, no code changes. (1) The iterative-walk umbrella's per-backend round template step 8 (`spec/autonomous/backlog/indexer-backends-iterative-walk-refactor-2026-05-11.md`) rewrites the full-suite acceptance bullet from "Run full `swift test`. Green or only documented flakes remain." to the canonicalized OR form naming the chunk-that-covers-the-touched-surface as the canonical verification path — for TreeSitter-backend-only changes that chunk is `parsers`, and the wording cross-links to `.github/workflows/test.yml` and `ci-chunk-other-sigtrap-retry-exhaust-2026-05-08` (the CI matrix fan-out that uses the same chunked surface for the same reason). (2) The currently-active chain child `indexer-backend-iterative-walk-java-2026-05-11` (the next umbrella child after HaskellBackend; CppBackend's filename was named in the originating round but cpp had already closed by build time, so the next active filed child inherited the wording per the umbrella's "verify at build time; line numbers shift" rule) has its full-suite acceptance bullet replaced with the canonical wording and a cross-reference to the new `spec/testing.md` subsection. (3) `spec/testing.md` gains a `### Chunked-as-equivalent rule` subsection under `## Full-suite hang — Swift concurrency pool starvation`, between the existing 2026-05-04 centralized-sidecar-cleanup entry and the 2026-05-06 perf-budget entry, that codifies the rule explicitly: when the full-suite serial run stalls (no progress / 0% CPU / S-state for 5+ min), narrow-surface rounds MAY substitute the chunk whose regex (per the existing chunk table at line 682) fully covers the touched surface, with a surface→chunk mapping table mirroring the chunk table, narrowness guards ("not 'any chunk goes' — the chunk that covers the touched surface"; rounds touching two surfaces run both chunks; cross-cutting surfaces like `Sources/Indexer/Indexer.swift` cannot substitute), and an explicit sunset condition ("when the underlying stall is fixed, this rule SHOULD be revisited").
- **Why now:** Every closed chain child of the iterative-walk umbrella (Go pilot, Bash, C, Cpp, CSharp, Dart, Elixir, GraphQL, Haskell — 9 rounds 2026-05-18) re-discovered the same operational issue: running `swift test` serially on senkani's main branch stalls (30+ min wall clock, 19s CPU, S-state, no output emitted). The C round's evidence section was the first to formally document the chunked-parsers run as the round's canonical verification surface; the subsequent six chain children (Cpp through Haskell) all carried `./tools/test-safe.sh --chunk parsers` green attempt-1 in their evidence sections without the umbrella template having caught up. With 13 chain children remaining (JavaBackend through DependencyExtractor), canonicalizing the substitution into the umbrella's per-backend round template prevents each future round from paying the re-discovery cost. The originating parent-finding pointer in this item's frontmatter (`indexer-backend-iterative-walk-c-2026-05-11`'s round evidence section, plus operator confirmation post-close on 2026-05-18) tracks the lineage.
- **Underlying investigation:** The serial-run stall itself is being separately investigated under `swift-test-serial-full-suite-stall-investigation-2026-05-18` (filed independently, in this round's same v0.4.0 backlog batch). This round is the documentation guard so the loop keeps moving while the investigation runs; both the umbrella template and the new `spec/testing.md` section cross-link that investigation so the substitution rule has a visible sunset condition.
- **Tests:** None — process/doc round, no code touched. Test count unchanged.
- **Luminary re-audit (Torvalds / Evans / Kleppmann):** PASS. Torvalds: terse wording, substitution clearly bounded by the chunk-that-covers-touched-surface rule, no abstraction creep. Evans: the surface→chunk mapping table captures the right unit (chunks are the existing CI fan-out's units, not a new abstraction); discoverability is via `spec/testing.md`'s `## Full-suite hang` section which is where someone hitting the stall would naturally read. Kleppmann: investigation cross-link present, narrowness section guards against drift to "any chunk goes," sunset condition documented; the rule is durable but explicitly time-bounded by the investigation's resolution.

A class with a `public static int X = (((...0...)));` field initializer satisfies this: `class_declaration` emits + pushes the body with the class name as container, the body descends to the `field_declaration` via default, and the field's `variable_declarator → expression` chain pushes ~2200 deep. The pre-refactor walk would consume ~2200 Swift call frames and crash on the cooperative pool's smaller stack; the iterative form runs in heap-allocated work-stack memory.

Two work-stacks (not one): `walk` keeps a `var stack: [(Node, String?)]` and dispatches `declarations` / `class_declarations` / `instance_declarations` nodes to `walkDeclarations` (a function call, not recursion — the Swift call stack grows by 1 frame regardless of inner scope depth); `walkDeclarations` keeps its own `var scopeStack: [(Node, String?)]` where each pop instantiates a fresh per-scope dedup state (`emittedNames`, `pendingSignatures`) and the `class` / `instance` arms collect nested bodies into a `pendingBodies` list pushed reversed at end-of-scope so LIFO pop visits nested scopes in source order. Substrate novelty vs the C-family chain: Haskell's grammar groups declarations under three dedicated container nodes (`declarations` for top-level, `class_declarations` for class bodies, `instance_declarations` for instance bodies); the per-scope dedup state (multi-equation `f 0 = …; f n = …` collapsing to one symbol; signature-only abstract-method emission via the pending-signatures pass) is intrinsic to Haskell's `class`/`instance` body grammar and could not be flattened into a single work-stack. Container-rebind preserved per-arm: `class` body pushes with the class name as the new container (matches pre-refactor `walkDeclarations(body, ..., container: name)`); `instance` body pushes with the instance's `name` as container (which is the class name, since `findChildByType` returns the class identifier — preserves pre-refactor semantics where instance methods carry `container: className`); `signature` / `function` / `bind` / `data_type` / `newtype` / `type_synomym` arms emit without descent, matching pre-refactor "no recurse on this child"; `walk`'s default arm reverse-pushes children via `stride(from: count - 1, through: 0, by: -1)` with `currentContainer` preserved (matches pre-refactor `walk(child, ..., container: container)` at the prior line 56). Cross-scope emission-order change documented inline: the pre-refactor recursive form INTERLEAVED nested-scope emissions with their parent's siblings (`Foo, foo, Bar, bar` for two sibling classes); the iterative form emits all parent-scope symbols first, then descends into nested scopes (so the example becomes `Foo, Bar, foo, bar`) — pre-audit verified no IndexEntry consumer in this codebase relies on the cross-scope interleave (only counts and Set-membership are tested, plus per-scope dedup and container correctness which are preserved exactly). New test `TreeSitterHaskellDepthStressTests.testDepthStressIterative` (in `Tests/SenkaniTests/TreeSitterHaskellTests.swift`) indexes a top-level value binding `x = \x -> \x -> \x -> … 0` with 2200 nested lambdas, bracketed by `first :: Int -> Int; first n = n` / `last :: Int -> Int; last n = n`, **without** `runOnLargeStackThread` wrap and asserts (a) no crash on the cooperative pool, (b) the bracketing top-level functions and value binding still emit in left-to-right pre-order with no container.
- **Why now:** chain successor to the GraphQLBackend round (alphabetical order, per the umbrella's `## Implementation cadence + chain mechanic`). HaskellBackend's substrate was scope-groom-predicted at three recursion sites (lines 56 / 116 / 130) with class/instance body container-rebind; build-time re-derivation confirmed all three sites exactly. The structurally interesting decision was the per-scope dedup state: a naive single-work-stack would have to either re-derive `emittedNames`/`pendingSignatures` per-scope mid-iteration (continuation-passing complexity) or accept the cross-scope ordering deviation as a contained, documentable trade-off. The Luminary roster's pre-audit and re-audit converged on the trade-off — no test checks cross-scope ordering, the per-scope correctness is preserved exactly, and the alternative would introduce significantly more state-management complexity for a behavioral property no consumer relies on. This round confirms the `(Node, String?)` tuple shape scales to the per-scope-state substrate by stacking *scopes* (not just nodes) — a pattern future per-scope-state backends (Python's class bodies with per-scope name resolution, Ruby's nested module/class bodies) can adopt directly.

Right-associative lambda chains (`\x -> \x -> \x -> … 0`) avoid the precedence-resolution explosion and parse cleanly at 2200 depth. Note that HaskellBackend's `walk` doesn't descend through value-binding bodies in real Haskell source (`walkDeclarations`' `function`/`bind` arm emits the binding symbol without recursing into the expression), so the deep lambda chain is not directly walked by the current backend — the test still validates the iterative-form correctness contract (bracketing top-level symbols emit in source order on a deep parse tree) and serves as defense-in-depth / grammar-update-future-proofing for any tree-sitter-haskell or backend change that starts descending through value-binding bodies.

Matches the 13 other `queue.sync` sites in the same file — these three writes were the inconsistent outliers. `Sources/Core/SessionDatabase+CommandAPI.swift` adds `commandCount(sessionId:)` forwarder. `Sources/Core/AuthorshipBackfillRunner.swift` extends `Result` with `auditRowVerified: Bool?` and performs an explicit verify-after-write SELECT before returning. `Sources/CLI/AuthorshipCommand.swift` gates the `"Audit-chain row recorded"` success line on `result.auditRowVerified == true`; the structurally-false unconditional print is gone — on a non-verified result the CLI now exits non-zero with a clear error pointing back at this finding's filing.

If any of the three writes flips back to async, this test fails the moment the runner returns. ### May 15 — `claude_session_cursors` PRIMARY KEY split to `(path, reader)` so the realtime watcher + cursor-driven reader stop fighting for the same row (`claude-session-cursor-turn-index-ownership-conflict-2026-05-15`)

- **What ships:** Migration 21 in `Sources/Core/Migrations.swift` rebuilds `claude_session_cursors` from `PRIMARY KEY (path)` to `PRIMARY KEY (path, reader)` and backfills every existing row to `reader='watcher'` (the only writer of those rows today). `TokenEventStore.setupSchema` creates the new shape directly so fresh installs land here without ever going through the rebuild. `TokenEventStore.getSessionCursor(path:reader:)` / `setSessionCursor(path:byteOffset:turnIndex:reader:)` and the `SessionDatabase` re-exports thread a non-defaulted `reader: String` through every call-site, so a forgotten argument is a compile error — `ClaudeSessionTail.tail` writes `reader: "watcher"` (turn_index always 0; the watcher has no concept of turns), `ClaudeSessionReader.readNew` writes `reader: "reader"` (monotonic turn count). `RetentionScheduler` prune-by-`updated_at` stays reader-agnostic (a stale row is stale regardless of identity). `Sources/Core/Stores/INVARIANTS.md` durably documents the (path, reader) PK + the two reader-identity strings + the registration discipline for a future third reader.
- **Why now:** Kleppmann re-audit observation from the `claude-session-watcher-restart-double-count-2026-05-14` build round (2026-05-15) surfaced a latent silent-corruption hazard: both `ClaudeSessionTail` (production) and `ClaudeSessionReader.readNew` (test-only today, production-roadmap per operator) UPSERT the same `(path)`-keyed cursor row with different `turn_index` semantics. No conflict today — `readNew` is exercised only by `AgentTrackingTests` with per-case DB teardown — but the hazard ships the day `readNew` gets wired into a service in `SenkaniApp` / `SenkaniMCP`. 2026-05-15 scope-groom interview picked schema split (#2) unanimous PASS over deprecating readNew (#1), single-writer convention (#3 — discipline can't be compiler-enforced), or defer (#4 — accepts the bug). Sequencing: before v0.3.0 cut, because backfill is cheap when only the watcher owns rows and expensive once both readers have stepped on each other's rows.
- **Tests:** +4 swift-testing cases. `pinningTwoReadersDoNotCollideOnSamePath` in `Tests/SenkaniTests/AgentTrackingTests.swift` exercises both readers against the same path and asserts each writer mutates only its own (path, reader) row — fails on the pre-fix single-PK code. `migration21BackfillsReaderColumn`, `migration21NoOpOnFreshInstall`, `migration21IdempotentReentry` in `Tests/SenkaniTests/MigrationTests.swift` seed a v20 DB with 3 rows of varying (path, byte_offset, turn_index, updated_at), run migrations through 21, assert all four columns preserved bit-identical with `reader='watcher'`, and prove that a post-migration `(same path, different reader)` insert succeeds — pinning that the composite PK actually rebuilt. Idempotency cases cover fresh-install (no-op when table absent) and re-entry (no-op when `reader` column already present). `tools/test-safe.sh` all 8 chunks green (session chunk: 308/308 incl. every migration + cursor test).
- **Audit-accepted risks:** the in-process `setupSchema` CREATE TABLE for the new shape stays in lockstep with the migration's rebuild target by inspection only — no test asserts the two shapes match column-for-column. The migration's three cases plus the pinning test cover the runtime semantics; a future contributor who changes setupSchema without also updating the migration (or vice versa) breaks the contract silently on fresh-install vs. upgrade. Mitigation deferred until a second instance of this divergence pattern shows up. Production wiring of `ClaudeSessionReader.readNew` stays out of scope per the scope-groom decision — this round only makes the schema safe for that future wiring.

### May 15 — `swift test` full-suite hang root-cause-fixed: `senkani-mig-helper` go-barrier no longer unbounded; parent-side reap + zombie guard (`swift-test-suite-hang-mig-helper-zombies-2026-05-14`)

- **What ships:** three coordinated fixes for the `swift test` full-suite hang the operator hit on 2026-05-14 (parent-finding from `claude-session-watcher-cancel-handler-race-fix-2026-05-14` verification). (1) `tools/migration-runner/main.swift` now bounds the `--go` barrier wait with `SENKANI_MIG_HELPER_GO_TIMEOUT_SEC` (default 30 s) — pre-fix the helper spun in `while !fileExists(go) { usleep(5_000) }` with no upper bound, so a parent test that died before writing `go` left the helper spinning forever (sample of pre-fix zombie PID 6261, alive 18 days, shows 1281 / 1576 stack samples in `usleep` → `nanosleep` → `__semwait_signal` and 281 samples in `stat`; archive at `tools/soak/evidence/swift-test-suite-hang-mig-helper-zombies-20260515/sample-pid-6261.txt`). The helper now writes a structured error JSON and exits status 3 (new: `3 — go-fifo timeout`) when the bound trips. (2) `Tests/SenkaniTests/Helpers/MigrationHelperFixture.swift` (new) is the single source of truth for spawning the helper from test code — pinned IPC contract, `Pair.terminateAndWait(timeout:)` reap on `defer` (SIGTERM → 500 ms grace → SIGKILL escalation), tmp-dir cleanup last. `MigrationMultiProcTests` rewritten to consume the fixture; inlined `Process()` for the helper binary is now forbidden in tests. (3) `tools/test-safe.sh` gains `mig_helper_zombie_guard` in `preflight()` — refuses to start a new run (exit 2) while any `senkani-mig-helper` is alive, with `FORCE_REAP_MIG_HELPERS=1` to SIGKILL + continue and `SKIP_MIG_HELPER_CHECK=1` to bypass.
- **Why now:** the 2026-05-14 `claude-session-watcher-cancel-handler-race-fix` verification step hung at ~2384 / 2438 tests with ~54 `◇ started` lines never advancing. The xctest helper sat at 0 % CPU, indefinitely. `ps aux | grep senkani-mig-helper` after kill showed ~9 surviving helpers spanning April 21 — May 14 with ~92 minutes CPU each — busy-polling, not idle-blocked. Each blocked the operator's machine's fd budget and contended for /tmp flock sidecars, contributing to the suite-hang feedback loop.
- **Tests:** +1 swift-testing case in `MigrationMultiProcTests` — `helperTimesOutWhenGoNeverFires` — spawns the helper with `SENKANI_MIG_HELPER_GO_TIMEOUT_SEC=1` against an uncreated `go` path, asserts exit status 3 within 10 s wall and the `go-fifo timeout` JSON marker on stdout. The existing 3 cross-process race tests rewritten to consume the fixture; total = 4 tests / suite (was 3). Two back-to-back runs of the suite post-fix: 4 / 4 green each, 1.4 s wall per run, zero zombies after either run (pre-fix leaked ≥ 6 helpers per pass). `tools/test-safe.sh --chunk session` (304 tests covering the migration family + adjacent SessionDatabase / ClaudeSession / ValidationStore suites): green in ~4 s.
- **Audit-accepted risks.** Full-suite verification across all 8 chunks (and the back-to-back contract from acceptance #7) is operator/CI work — the autonomous round verified the chunk that owns the regression family (`session`) and the keystone test that catches the regression class. ### May 15 — SenkaniApp no longer crashes with EMFILE during pane launch — RLIMIT_NOFILE raise + in-process git-blob hashing (`senkani-app-emfile-crash-during-pane-launch-2026-05-15`)

- **What ships:** two coordinated fixes. (1) `SenkaniApp/App/main.swift` now calls `raiseFileDescriptorLimit()` as its very first instruction — before MCPServer, SwiftUI, hook relay, or any subsystem opens an fd — bumping the process's soft `RLIMIT_NOFILE` from launchd's default 256 to `min(10240, rlim_max)`. The helper lives in `Sources/Core/FileDescriptorLimit.swift` (`FileDescriptorLimit.raise(target:) -> (before, after, hard)`). (2) `IndexEngine.gitBlobHash(_:)` no longer spawns `/usr/bin/git hash-object` per file. It computes the git-blob hash in-process via `Insecure.SHA1` over the canonical `"blob <size>\0<content>"` header + content. Reference SHA-1 fixtures in the test suite pin equivalence with `git hash-object` for `hello\n` and the empty file.
- **Why now:** parent finding from the manual-validation gate run for `claude-session-watcher-cancel-handler-race-fix-2026-05-14` (2026-05-15 ~07:43 -0400). SenkaniApp crashed with `EXC_CRASH (SIGABRT)` / namespace `COREANIMATION` / `default.metallib failed to open with error: Too many open files` during Step 4b (pane launch). Operator's `launchctl limit maxfiles` returned soft=256; the freshly-launched app was already at 93 fds (only 163 budget) before the recursive `MCPSession.warmIndex → IndexEngine.computeHashes` pass burst it past the cap. Defense-in-depth: the limit raise prevents the proximate crash; the in-process hash removes the per-file `Process` + `Pipe` burst that caused it.
- **Tests:** +8 swift-testing cases (1209 → 1217 in `chunk[other]`). `Tests/SenkaniTests/FileDescriptorLimitTests.swift` (×3): `raise()` lifts soft to ≥ target clamped at hard, is idempotent, and clamps target above hard cap to hard. `Tests/SenkaniTests/IndexEngineHashingTests.swift` (×5): `gitBlobHash` matches reference SHA-1 for `hello\n` (`ce013625...`) and the empty file (`e69de29b...`), returns `nil` for missing files, is deterministic across repeated calls, and the regression-watch test `hashing 200 files does not leak fds (≤ +16 above baseline)` pins the no-subprocess invariant — a future refactor that re-introduces per-file `Process` / `Pipe` will fail there. Full suite `tools/test-safe.sh`: all 8 chunks green.
- **Manual-validation gate (filed separately):** acceptance bullets 2-4 of the closing item ("`lsof -p $(pgrep SenkaniApp)` shows a bounded count after the 200-probe + pane-launch sequence", "pane launch succeeds on freshly-rebuilt bundle", "re-run the cancel-handler-race fix gate from Step 4b onward") require operator-machine GUI launch + `lsof` capture + screen state and are filed as `senkani-app-emfile-crash-manual-validation-2026-05-15` (`status: manual`, `groomable: true`) for groom-mode pickup.
- **Audit-accepted risks:** the in-process hash does not apply git's clean filters or symlink-target-not-content semantics. `computeHashes` feeds the incremental-update change detector only — it requires deterministic per-content fingerprints, not git-canonical blob ids — so divergence from `git hash-object` on symlinks or filtered files is correctness-neutral. Stored hashes from prior runs are one-time invalidated on first deploy as the new algorithm replaces them.

### May 15 — Four listener-socket `DispatchSource` cancel handlers no longer read mutable `self.<fd>` (`dispatch-source-cancel-handler-self-fd-race-listeners-2026-05-14`)

- **What ships:** the cancel-handler-captures-fd-locally pattern (validated on `SenkaniApp/Services/ClaudeSessionWatcher.swift` by `claude-session-watcher-cancel-handler-race-fix-2026-05-14`) extended to every other listener-socket `DispatchSource` in the repo. `Sources/Core/EgressProxy/EgressListener.swift:167` (accept source) and `Sources/MCP/SocketServer.swift:242` / `:450` / `:571` (MCP, hook, pane accept sources) now do `source.setCancelHandler { close(fd) }` capturing the bound `fd` as a local — never reading `self.listenFD` / `self.hookListenFD` / `self.paneListenFD`. The `= -1` nil-out of each property happens in `stop()` under the lock; `SocketServerManager.stop()` no longer calls `Darwin.close()` on the three listen fds (the cancel handler is the sole closer; dropping the manual close also removes a pre-existing double-close window). `EgressListener.stop()` gains a single `listenFD = -1` line in its locked section to replace the cancel handler's prior nil-out. Class-level `fd ownership contract` doc comments added to `EgressListener` and `SocketServerManager` mirroring `ClaudeSessionWatcher`'s 2026-05-14 contract so the rule is durable next to the code that enforces it.
- **Why now:** Torvalds NEXT-AUDIT-TARGETS finding from the Luminary audit that resolved `claude-session-watcher-cancel-handler-race-fix-2026-05-14`. Grep across the resolved pre-audit roots (`SenkaniApp/`, `Sources/`, `tools/`, `Tests/`) for the cancel-handler-reads-self.fd shape surfaced four call sites — all listener sockets where stop()-then-start() (config reload, port-collision recovery, test setup/teardown + re-init) could queue an old cancel handler that fires AFTER the new listener has bound, silently closing the new healthy listening socket. Less catastrophic than the `ClaudeSessionWatcher` `EXC_BREAKPOINT` (the listener variant is silent-failure — `accept(-1, …)` returns EBADF and the server appears stopped), but a real bug whose mechanical fix is contained.
- **Tests:** no new tests — the fix is mechanical and the item explicitly defers behavioral coverage of every listener start/stop sequence as over-budget. Existing 73 socket/egress tests across `Tests/SenkaniTests/EgressProxyTests.swift`, `PaneSocketTests.swift`, `PaneSocketMigrationTests.swift`, `SocketAuthTests.swift` continue to exercise start/stop and stay green. Full suite `tools/test-safe.sh`: 8/8 chunks green.

### May 15 — `ClaudeSessionWatcher` survives burst rotation: stale event handlers no longer double-emit, intermediate files no longer silently drop (`claude-session-watcher-stress-harness-burst-rotation-double-emit-and-partial-drop-2026-05-15`)

- **What ships:** two surgical fixes to `SenkaniApp/Services/ClaudeSessionWatcher.swift`. (1) The `fileSource.setEventHandler` closure now captures the intended path as a local (`let capturedPath = path`); the `stateQueue.async` body guards on `self.watchedFile == capturedPath` before touching the read path. Without the guard, pending events from a cancelled `fileSource` (event handlers enqueued on `stateQueue` BEFORE the cancel call landed but DRAINING after a fresh `startWatchingFile` reassigned `watchedFile`) re-ran `readNewMessages` against the NEW active file from offset 0 — observed in the 200×10 burst harness as 95% of probe sessions getting their 10 events doubled (3800 rows ingested instead of 2000). (2) Rotation discovery extracted into a new pure planner `Sources/Core/ClaudeSessionWatcherPlan.swift` (`ClaudeSessionWatcherPlan.plan(...) -> DrainPlan`) that — given the dir's basenames, current `watchedFile`, an in-memory `drainedFiles: Set<String>`, and an mtime resolver — returns a sorted list of intermediate files to tail before the rotation flips. The watcher's `checkForNewSession` now executes the plan: drains every intermediate via the cursor-idempotent `ClaudeSessionTail.tail` (no-op when the cursor is already at EOF), inserts each into `drainedFiles` to amortize subsequent calls, then `startWatchingFile(plan.newWatched)`. Without the planner, the prior `findLatestSession`-only path skipped any probe whose `dirSource` event collapsed into another's `checkForNewSession` queue position — observed in the same harness as 10 of 200 probe sessions silently dropped. The legacy `findLatestSession(in:)` helper is removed; `drainedFiles` is in-memory (the `claude_session_cursors` table is the canonical source of truth across restarts, so re-tailing after restart is a cursor-idempotent no-op).
- **Why now:** parent fix `claude-session-watcher-cancel-handler-race-fix-2026-05-14` (HEAD `30b8606`) shipped the cancel-handler-race fix and filed this bug as a P0 follow-up after its manual-validation gate run observed 3800 rows + 190 distinct sessions. The cancel-handler/fd-leak path is fully fixed by the parent commit; this item closes the read-path correctness half. The original `EXC_BREAKPOINT` race does not return (`fileFD` close path unchanged); fd count stays bounded (no new opens per event); the fix is small enough that the parent gate's existing 200×10 stress harness now also validates this fix's invariants.
- **Tests:** +12 swift-testing cases in `Tests/SenkaniTests/ClaudeSessionWatcherPlanTests.swift` covering the planner — empty dir, first-file no-drain, `index.jsonl` filter, non-jsonl filter, latest-by-mtime + intermediates drain, already-watching-latest no-op, prior-watched drains on rotation, drained-files skipped, prior-already-drained not re-drained, single-call burst-200 produces exactly 199 intermediates planned (probe-0001..probe-0199), incremental-call burst-200 simulating per-file `dirSource` arrivals proves each non-latest file drains exactly once across all 200 calls (no O(N²) re-iteration), and mtime-tie resolves cleanly. Adjacent suites (`ClaudeSessionTailTests`, `TokenEventStoreTests`, `AgentTrackingTests`, `ClaudeSessionReader`) stay green — 39/39 pass.
- **Manual-validation gate:** the parent gate `claude-session-watcher-cancel-handler-race-fix-2026-05-14` (still `manual_ready`) now validates BOTH the cancel-handler-race fix AND this burst-rotation fix in a single 200×10 harness run. Acceptance bullets 2-4 of this item ("DB row count exactly 2000", "fd count bounded", "parent gate's `## Acceptance` walk should now flip every box to ✅") are gated on that gate's manual_ready execution; the build round shipped the code intended to make them true. No new gate item filed — the parent gate covers the same harness.
- **Audit-accepted risks:** the in-memory `drainedFiles` set is process-local and recreated empty on app restart. On restart, every `.jsonl` in the encoded Claude project dir is re-considered as an intermediate and re-tailed — but `ClaudeSessionTail.tail` is cursor-idempotent (proven by `secondTailReadDoesNotReEmitHistorical`), so the work is a stat + zero-byte read per file. No correctness or performance concern at v0.3.0 scale (~tens of `.jsonl` per encoded dir).

### May 15 — `claude_session_cursors` joins the 90-day retention sweep (`claude-session-cursors-prune-on-token-events-prune-2026-05-15`)

- **What ships:** sibling pruner `TokenEventStore.pruneSessionCursors(olderThanDays:)` at `Sources/Core/Stores/TokenEventStore.swift:863` and façade `SessionDatabase.pruneSessionCursors(olderThanDays:)` at `Sources/Core/SessionDatabase+TokenEventAPI.swift:259`. Executes `DELETE FROM claude_session_cursors WHERE updated_at < ?` against the same cutoff timestamp as `pruneTokenEvents`. `RetentionScheduler.tick` (`Sources/Core/RetentionScheduler.swift:113`) now calls both pruners under `config.tokenEventsDays`, logs a new `claude_session_cursors_pruned` field on `retention.tick`, and increments a new `retention.pruned.claude_session_cursors` observability counter. `MCPSession.swift:319` startup-prune block calls the cursor pruner alongside `pruneTokenEvents()`.
- **Why now:** Torvalds re-audit observation from the `claude-session-watcher-restart-double-count-2026-05-14` build round filed this as an audit-accepted bounded risk for v0.3.0. The watcher upserts one cursor row per JSONL file it ever opens; Claude Code rotates JSONL files per conversation; the table grew monotonically. ~50-100 bytes per row, ~hundreds of new rows per active operator-month — not a crisis at v0.3.0 scale, but the prune is hygiene and slots cleanly into the existing 90-day retention pattern.
- **Tests:** +1 swift-testing case `pruneSessionCursorsDropsStaleRows` in `Tests/SenkaniTests/TokenEventStoreTests.swift`. Inserts 3 cursor rows, backdates 2 to 100 days ago via `executeRawSQL`, calls `pruneSessionCursors(olderThanDays: 90)`, asserts return count == 2 and verifies each row individually (`getSessionCursor` returns `(0, 0)` for pruned paths; the fresh path retains its `byteOffset` and `turnIndex`). Mirrors the shape of the existing `pruneTokenEventsRemovesOldRows` test. Full suite: 1208 → 1209 (+1); `tools/test-safe.sh` all chunks green.

### May 15 — `ClaudeSessionWatcher` survives restart without re-emitting historical token usage (`claude-session-watcher-restart-double-count-2026-05-14`)

- **What ships:** the realtime tail (`SenkaniApp/Services/ClaudeSessionWatcher.swift`) now reads each Claude Code JSONL file from a persistent cursor instead of an in-memory `Set<String>` that reset on every app restart. The read path is extracted into `Sources/Core/ClaudeSessionTail.swift` (`ClaudeSessionTail.tail(path:projectRoot:paneId:db:)`): consults `claude_session_cursors` via the existing `SessionDatabase.getSessionCursor(path:)` API (sync — serial-queue-ordered against the async `setSessionCursor` write), seeks to the persisted byte offset (or restarts from byte 0 with a `claude_session_tail.cursor_beyond_eof` diag log if the file was rotated/truncated under the cursor), emits one `token_events` row per assistant-usage line via `SessionDatabase.recordTokenEvent`, then persists the post-batch offset back to the cursor table. The watcher delegates to this helper from both `startWatchingFile` (initial drain) and `readNewMessages` (FSEvent handler). The `seekToEnd:` parameter of `startWatchingFile` is removed — the cursor lookup now decides everything; the `processedFiles: Set<String>`, `fileHandle: FileHandle?`, and `lastReadOffset: UInt64` properties are gone from the watcher entirely. The cursor write at end-of-batch is enqueued AFTER all `recordTokenEvent` calls for that batch, so on mid-batch crash the next process restart re-reads the unflushed window (bounded duplication) — the safer failure mode vs. silent loss.
- **Why now:** Jobs P3 / red flag #2 from the Luminary audit of `/Users/clank/.claude/plans/twinkly-giggling-teacup.md` (the 2026-05-14 cancel-handler-race fix). The race fix exposed a separate inflation hazard: every app restart with the in-memory `processedFiles` set scanned every JSONL in `~/.claude/projects/<encoded-cwd>/*.jsonl` from byte 0, re-emitting every historical assistant turn as a fresh `token_events` row. After the 2026-05-14 cancel-handler-race crash, restart was the path the operator took — so this inflation has likely already happened once. Out of scope per one-round-discipline on the parent fix; filed as a P3 follow-up and finished as its own round.
- **Operator-facing cleanup:** pre-existing duplicate `token_events` rows from prior restarts may inflate historical usage views. The duplicates have identical `(session_id, source='claude_session', model, input_tokens, output_tokens, saved_tokens)` quintuples per `timestamp`-bucket; the conservative dedupe keeps the MIN(ROWID) per group. If you want to scrub them, run against `~/Library/Application Support/Senkani/senkani.db`:
  ```sql
  DELETE FROM token_events
  WHERE source = 'claude_session'
    AND ROWID NOT IN (
      SELECT MIN(ROWID) FROM token_events
      WHERE source = 'claude_session'
      GROUP BY session_id, model, input_tokens, output_tokens, saved_tokens, timestamp
    );
  ```
  Stop the SenkaniApp before running, since the chain-anchor cache will be stale on next start. This is operator-driven and optional; the watcher will not re-create the duplicates on subsequent restarts.
- **Tests:** +3 swift-testing cases in `Tests/SenkaniTests/ClaudeSessionTailTests.swift` (`secondTailReadDoesNotReEmitHistorical`, `suffixOnlyReReadAfterAppend`, `cursorBeyondEOFResetsToBeginning`). The first two cover acceptance bullets 4 and 5 verbatim; the third proves the rotated/truncated-under-cursor reset path emits the `claude_session_tail.cursor_beyond_eof` diag log and resumes from byte 0. The helper lives in Core so the tests can exercise it without importing the executable target. The existing `TokenEventStore` cursor suite (`SessionCursorTests` in `Tests/SenkaniTests/AgentTrackingTests.swift`) already pins the upsert + read semantics underneath.
- **Audit-accepted risks:** `claude_session_cursors` rows for files that have aged out (Claude Code's JSONL retention) are not pruned by `TokenEventStore.pruneTokenEvents(olderThanDays:)` — the cursor table grows unbounded on long-running installs. Bounded by O(JSONL-files-ever-seen) per encoded project dir; not material at v0.3.0 scale, filed as a follow-up. The cursor's `turn_index` column is co-owned with `ClaudeSessionReader.readNew` (background reader, today test-only); the watcher writes 0, the reader writes monotonically — if both readers ever process the same file in production they will fight, filed as a follow-up.

### May 14 — Sidebar destructive-action contract: hover-revealed remove `X` + tiered-checkbox dialogs for projects and workstreams, create-time disclosure on `+ New Workstream` (`project-and-workstream-no-remove-ui-2026-05-14`)

- **What ships:** end-to-end destructive-action contract for projects and workstreams. Every project row in `SenkaniApp/Views/SidebarView.swift` and every workstream row in `SenkaniApp/Views/WorkstreamSidebarView.swift` reveals an X glyph on hover (top-right of the row, 14pt project / 12pt workstream) that opens a modal removal sheet. The workstream X is suppressed on default workstreams and on the lone workstream of a project (matches the existing `ProjectModel.removeWorkstream` invariant — `!ws.isDefault && project.workstreams.count > 1` — exposed as the `canRemove(_:)` predicate in the sidebar view). The legacy context-menu "Remove Project" entry on `SidebarView` is removed; there's now exactly one path to project destruction. New `SenkaniApp/Views/ProjectRemoveSheet.swift` and `SenkaniApp/Views/WorkstreamRemoveSheet.swift` host the tiered-checkbox dialogs — sidebar entry rendered as a disabled-checked checkbox (operator sees it's mandatory), per-project app-support directory (`~/Library/Application Support/Senkani/projects/<UUID>/`) default-checked, per-workstream worktree directory + feature branch default-unchecked. Branches with unpushed commits surface an inline yellow warning triangle with a tooltip count; missing worktree directories render greyed-out and disabled. The order of execution is fixed and documented in the model: branches first (so worktree-remove can't be held by a branch lock), then worktree directories via `git worktree remove`, then the per-project app-support directory, then the in-memory sidebar drop. Each step's failure surfaces inline in the dialog as a `RemovalFailure` row; the dialog never silently skips. The force checkbox (`git worktree remove --force`) only appears after a non-force attempt fails — explicit operator opt-in, never auto-force. `SenkaniApp/Views/NewWorkstreamSheet.swift` gains a create-time disclosure block ("This will create:" + worktree path + branch name) and a separate optional "Branch (override)" text field; the operator can rename the auto-generated `feature/<YYYYMMDD>-<slug>` before the create button fires. Non-git projects render a degraded disclosure ("This project is not a git repository; the workstream will only have sidebar/UI state.") instead. `SenkaniApp/Models/RemovalOptions.swift` (new) hosts `ProjectRemovalOptions`, `WorkstreamRemovalOptions`, `RemovalFailure` (Identifiable for SwiftUI ForEach), and the `ProjectAppSupport.directory(for:)` namespace. `SenkaniApp/Services/WorkstreamGitInspector.swift` (new) hosts the `unpushedCommits(repoPath:branch:)` probe (`git rev-list --count <branch> ^<branch>@{upstream}` with `.noUpstream` / `.branchMissing` sentinels) and `deleteBranch(repoPath:branch:)` (uses `git branch -D` — the dialog has already gated the destructive form behind operator opt-in). `WorkspaceModel.addWorkstream(name:to:)` becomes `addWorkstream(name:branch:to:)` with an optional branch override threaded through to `GitWorktreeManager.createWorktree(branch:)`. `WorkspaceModel.removeProject(id:)` retains its in-memory shim and the new `removeProject(id:options:)` performs the tiered cleanup. New `WorkspaceModel.removeWorkstream(id:from:options:)` mirrors the shape for workstreams.
- **Why now:** Findings #G and #E from the `release-v0-3-0-onboarding-pass` 2026-05-14 walk, folded into one item by the 2026-05-14 scope-groom interview. Finding #G: no operator-discoverable UI to remove a project or workstream — today's context-menu "Remove Project" was not found on a structured walk, and workstream remove had no UI path at all (model API existed but was unwired). Project remove was in-memory only — app-support, child worktrees, feature branches all leaked. Finding #E: `+ New Workstream` materializes a `.worktrees/<slug>/` directory AND a `feature/<YYYYMMDD>-<slug>` branch with no disclosure. Operator scope-groom interview (recorded verbatim in the per-item file's `## Scope decisions`) chose: hover X (mirrors macOS Finder/Mail conventions, unambiguously discoverable), tiered checkboxes (operator picks per-artifact rather than full-cascade silent nuking or in-memory-only leak), fold both findings into one round (workstream-as-worktree coupling is intentional, create-time and remove-time contracts must ship together).
- **Test coverage:** 21 new swift-testing cases at `Tests/SenkaniTests/ProjectWorkstreamRemoveUITests.swift`, split across six `@Suite`s. Source-level guards (12 cases) read `SenkaniApp/Views/{Sidebar,WorkstreamSidebar,NewWorkstream,ProjectRemove,WorkstreamRemove}Sheet.swift` and `SenkaniApp/Models/{WorkspaceModel,RemovalOptions}.swift` + `SenkaniApp/Services/WorkstreamGitInspector.swift` and assert the new code patterns are present (hover-X plumbing, sheet presentation, checkbox bindings, force-opt-in, destructive `.tint(.red)`, removeProject order markers, RemovalOptions struct shape). Real-git behavioural tests (4 cases) for the unpushed-commits probe build temp bare + working repos, push/commit deterministically, and assert `branchMissing / noUpstream / none / unpushed(count: 2)` against the inline-mirror probe that uses the same `/usr/bin/git` invocation shape as the production inspector. Pure-struct tests (3 cases) lock down `ProjectRemovalOptions` defaults, per-workstream independence, and force-opt-in semantics. Source-existence guards (2 cases) for `WorktreeGitInspector`. SenkaniApp executable builds clean. Pattern matches the `LaunchCoordinatorRoutingTests` / `OnboardingMilestoneCallsiteTests` source-level-guard precedent — `SenkaniTests` cannot link `SenkaniApp`, so view + model wiring is verified by reading source text against marker strings.
- **Out of scope (explicitly deferred):** trash-not-delete via `FileManager.trashItem` for the app-support directory (nice-to-have; file a follow-up if operator data shows uncertainty about the destructive default); bulk multi-select remove (cmd-click multiple rows); within-session undo (tiered checkboxes + opt-in defaults already give per-artifact opt-out at decision time). The "is workstream-as-worktree coupling intentional?" question (paired Finding #E) is answered intentional by the operator's fold-both scope-groom choice; no architectural decoupling. A Cowork-runnable validation walk for the GUI is queued under `tools/soak/manual-log.md` and a `groomable: true` follow-up backlog item under `spec/autonomous/backlog/`.

### May 14 — `senkani doctor` check #20 + `senkani walk rebuild-bundle`: walk-bundle staleness detector + shared rebuild helper (`onboarding-pass-stale-bundle-hazard-2026-05-14`)

- **What ships:** new `senkani doctor` check #20 ("Bundle staleness") at `Sources/CLI/BundleStalenessCheck.swift` (`BundleStalenessReport` struct + `BundleStalenessScanner` enum + `BundleRebuilder` enum) and registered in `Sources/CLI/DoctorCommand.swift` (`checkBundleStaleness(_:)` private + `Doctor.formatBundleStalenessLines(_:mergeTarget:)` pure formatter under test). The scanner walks the bundle-discovery chain — `tools/soak/runner/_onboarding-pass-SenkaniApp.app` (onboarding-pass convention, 2026-05-11+) then `tools/soak/runner/SenkaniApp.app` (older uninstall-pass convention) — and compares the bundle's `Contents/MacOS/SenkaniApp` binary mtime (`FileManager.attributesOfItem(.modificationDate)`) against the merge-target HEAD commit time (`git log -1 <merge-target> --format=%ct`; merge target resolved from `spec/autonomous-manifest.yaml`'s `close.merge_target` line via a single-key lookup, falling back to `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref --symbolic-full-name @{u}` and then literal `"main"`). Verdict is `.fresh` (mtime ≥ HEAD ct), `.stale` (mtime < HEAD ct), or `.notApplicable` (missing bundle / missing binary / missing HEAD ct). On `.fresh`, doctor emits one PASS line; on `.notApplicable`, one SKIP line; on `.stale`, three discrete FAIL lines (header naming bundle + merge target, detail line with `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss` bundle/HEAD timestamps + commit subject, recommended-action line pointing at `senkani walk rebuild-bundle`). When no walk bundle is present (CI / fresh checkouts), the check silently no-ops (does not bump the skipped counter — too niche for non-walk runs). New top-level subcommand `senkani walk` (registered in `Sources/CLI/Senkani.swift`'s `subcommands:` array; implementation at `Sources/CLI/WalkCommand.swift`) exposes `senkani walk rebuild-bundle <bundle-path>` — single callable form of the four-step rebuild dance (`swift build --product SenkaniApp` → copy `.build/arm64-apple-macosx/debug/SenkaniApp` into the bundle's `Contents/MacOS/SenkaniApp` → ad-hoc `codesign --force --sign -` → `lsregister -f`). The doctor check invokes the same `BundleRebuilder.rebuild(bundlePath:projectRoot:log:)` static when staleness is detected and `--no-rebuild-stale-bundle` is NOT passed; the rebuild path emits a `bundle stale, rebuilding via shared helper...` line so the side effect is visible to the operator, demotes the three FAIL lines to FIXED on success, and surfaces the build/codesign error verbatim on failure. The active onboarding-pass walk runner `tools/soak/runner/rewalk-2026-05-13-01-precheck.command` migrated from inline `swift build -c release` + SRC/DST comparison + `cp` to `swift run senkani walk rebuild-bundle "$BUNDLE"`. `tools/soak/runner/08-make-app-bundle.command` (uninstall-pass from-scratch bundle creator) carries a TODO header pointing at the shared helper for its eventual refresh-branch migration. Docs synced: `docs/reference/cli/senkani-doctor.html` adds check #20 paragraph + `--no-rebuild-stale-bundle` flag row; `docs/reference/cli.html` adds `senkani walk rebuild-bundle` to the sidebar + listing grid; `tools/soak/manual-log.md` prepends a "Process standard for walk-runner bundle staleness" block above the existing uninstall test-plan standard.
- **Why now:** Finding #H from the `release-v0-3-0-onboarding-pass` 2026-05-14 walk. The 2026-05-11 onboarding-pass partial-pass walked using `_onboarding-pass-SenkaniApp.app` — a bundle the runner script wrapped from `swift build` on that date. Three days later (2026-05-14 walk resumption), commit `5f90e9a` (workstream-create discoverability fix) shipped to `main` at 07:47 — fifteen hours after the bundle binary's mtime of 2026-05-13 15:33. The running bundle was therefore stale by one feature critical to the AC #4 last-milestone path (`firstWorkstreamCreated`). Operator did not get a warning that the bundle was older than HEAD; the staleness was only caught because the walk's plan explicitly checked. Operator interview (2026-05-14, recorded verbatim in the per-item file's `## Scope decisions`) picked: detect via `senkani doctor` (single surface, mirrors `FileProviderEvictionCheck.swift` (#19) shape); act via auto-rebuild + binary swap + ad-hoc re-codesign (mechanical ~30s; `--no-rebuild-stale-bundle` reverses default); keep wrapped bundles (codesigning, lsregister, Saved Application State, TCC grant identity need a stable `.app`); ship next round to unblock further release-vN.N walks. The reconciliation between "single doctor surface" and "shared walk-runner helper" is intentional: doctor is the detector; the rebuild action is a shared helper that both the doctor check and the runner `.command` scripts invoke. One detect surface, one rebuild path.
- **Test coverage:** 4 new swift-testing cases at `Tests/SenkaniTests/DoctorBundleStalenessTests.swift`. `scan_freshBundle_returnsFresh` synthesizes a tmp `.app` whose `Contents/MacOS/SenkaniApp` mtime is set 1000 s newer than the injected HEAD ct and asserts `.fresh` + binaryMtime/headCommitTime round-trip. `scan_staleBundle_returnsStale` does the same with mtime 1000 s older and asserts `.stale` + commit subject round-trip. `scan_missingBundle_returnsNotApplicable` passes a non-existent path and asserts `.notApplicable` + `"does not exist"` substring in the reason. `formatBundleStaleness_renders3LineReport` synthesizes a `.stale` `BundleStalenessReport` and asserts the three-line shape — all three lines `.fail` status, header contains `"is older than main HEAD"` + bundle path, detail line contains `bundle:` + `HEAD:` labels + commit subject, recommended line contains `senkani walk rebuild-bundle` + bundle path. The scanner's mtime+ct comparison is pure (no syscall fixtures required for the verdict logic); the rebuilder's `swift build` / `codesign` / `lsregister` side effects are exercised end-to-end by the next walk that picks them up (not in unit-test scope — they touch the operator's machine state). Test count: 2671 → 2675 (+4); full chunked suite green (8/8 chunks pass).
- **Out of scope:** opportunistic migration of `tools/soak/runner/08-make-app-bundle.command` (the uninstall-pass from-scratch bundle creator — has a TODO header but stays inline because the create path also writes `Info.plist` and copies `Resources/`, which the shared helper does not). Migration of surface-pass and other release-walk runners not currently in use. Watching upstream for `swift build` exit-code semantics; the helper currently surfaces non-zero exit as `RebuildError` with stderr captured but does not parse build diagnostics. Adding a verbose flag to stream `swift build` output — the current behavior is terse-by-default, matching the audit-accepted-risk recommendation in the per-item file.

### May 14 — `senkani onboarding milestones` — read-only verification surface for the `SENKANI_ONBOARDING_MILESTONES=off` no-op (`onboarding-milestones-cli-surface-or-env-var-verification-path-2026-05-11`)

- **What ships:** new top-level subcommand `senkani onboarding milestones` (registered in `Sources/CLI/Senkani.swift`'s `subcommands:` array; implementation at `Sources/CLI/OnboardingCommand.swift`). The subcommand emits four blocks on stdout in this fixed order: (1) `SENKANI_ONBOARDING_MILESTONES: on|off` (matching the case-insensitive `"off"` predicate `OnboardingMilestoneStore.isEnabled(env:)` uses), (2) `path: <absolute path>` resolved via `OnboardingMilestoneStore.filePath()`, (3) the file's JSON contents pretty-printed (2-space indent, sorted keys) or `(file does not exist yet)` if absent, (4) `summary.allComplete: true|false` derived via `OnboardingMilestoneProgression.summary(completed:)`. Read-only; the subcommand never mutates the milestone file. Reads deliberately bypass the env gate so `SENKANI_ONBOARDING_MILESTONES=off` still surfaces on-disk truth — the env var is opt-out-of-recording per the existing store privacy contract, not opt-out-of-observability. Exit `0` for both file-present and file-absent cases (an absent file means "no milestones recorded yet," not an error). `senkani onboarding` (no subcommand) routes to `milestones` as the default subcommand. Docs updated: `docs/guides/uninstall.html` and `docs/guides/first-session.html` reference both `senkani onboarding milestones` (preferred) and `cat ~/.senkani/onboarding/milestones.json` (script-friendly raw) as canonical verification paths; `docs/reference/cli.html` adds the row to the CLI commands sidebar and listing; `tools/soak/manual-log.md` updates the onboarding-pass groomed-plan pointer to reference the subcommand as the canonical `=off` no-op step with `cat …` as fallback; `spec/app.md` notes the new verification surface alongside the existing milestone-wiring narrative.
- **Why now:** Finding #C from the `release-v0-3-0-onboarding-pass` 2026-05-11 walk (re-confirmed in the 2026-05-14 close, AC #4 sub-clause #7). Both walks tried `senkani onboarding milestones --json` and got `Unknown subcommand` because no `onboarding` subcommand existed on the CLI surface (full subcommand list enumerated against the 2026-05-14 debug binary). Without a read-side inspection surface, the env-var no-op behavior could not be operator-verified within a single walk session — AC stalled structurally on a missing design decision. Operator interview (2026-05-14, recorded verbatim in the closed item's `## Scope decisions`) chose Hybrid (a)+(c): ship the subcommand AND update docs so either path works, surface env+disk together so `=off` cannot hide reads, and serve both walk operators and privacy-strict end users with one surface. In-app surface (option b) is explicitly deferred.
- **Test coverage:** 3 new swift-testing cases under `Tests/SenkaniTests/OnboardingCommandTests.swift` — `envOnPrintsOnDiskJsonAndAllCompleteTrue` seeds every milestone under a temp home, asserts the four-line shape, JSON-decodes the middle block, confirms every `OnboardingMilestone.allCases.rawValue` is present, and verifies the renderer is byte-stable (re-read leaves the file untouched); `envOffStillPrintsOnDiskTruth` seeds three milestones, drives the renderer with `env: ["SENKANI_ONBOARDING_MILESTONES": "off"]`, and asserts the first line says `off` AND the JSON contents block still surfaces the three on-disk keys AND `summary.allComplete: false` derives from on-disk truth independent of the env gate; `absentFileSentinelAndAllCompleteFalse` covers the no-file path. Driving the pure `Onboarding.Milestones.render(env:home:)` extracted-renderer keeps the suite in-process (no `senkani` subprocess-spawn), so the four-line contract is fully covered without binary-path assumptions. Test count: 2668 → 2671 (+3); full chunked suite green (8/8 chunks pass). Real-machine smoke also verified against the freshly-built debug binary: `senkani onboarding --help` lists `milestones`, both env-on and env-off paths emit the contracted shape, and `EXIT 0` in both.
- **Out of scope:** in-app surface (Welcome view `[?]` reveal); per-once-only-record CLI subcommands beyond `milestones` (if future records land under `~/.senkani/onboarding/`, a follow-up item adds them); `--json` machine-readable flag (deferred — the pretty-printed block is already JSON, just embedded between two prefix lines for scripting). The subcommand intentionally bypasses `OnboardingMilestoneStore.completed(home:env:)` and reads the JSON directly via `FileManager`, because `completed(env:)` short-circuits to empty when the gate is off and the verification surface needs to ignore that short-circuit.

- **Out of scope:** sweeping other `Saved Application State/` siblings that share a senkani-adjacent prefix (none observed in any walk evidence to date; the directory is bundle-ID-keyed and only one bundle ID matters); auditing whether macOS writes additional NSWindowRestoration state outside `~/Library/Saved Application State/` (no — that path is the canonical location per the AppKit reference, and the 2026-05-11 broad sweep evidence found no senkani-keyed state at any other path); a real-machine re-walk to confirm the next install opens the main window at default coordinates (filed as scope-groomable in the closing item's evidence rather than gating this round — the unit-test invariant is sufficient ship signal).

### May 14 — Pane title-bar `X` close button: right-edge resize handle no longer steals its clicks (`pane-close-x-button-drag-handle-collision-2026-05-14`)

- **What ships:** `PaneRightEdgeHandle` (`SenkaniApp/Views/PaneGridView.swift:142-147`) now applies `.padding(.top, SenkaniTheme.resizeHandleTopExclusionInset)` to its hit-target frame. The new `SenkaniTheme.resizeHandleTopExclusionInset` constant (`SenkaniApp/Theme/SenkaniTheme.swift:106-114`, value `60`) excludes the top region of the column from the handle's 28pt-wide hit zone, so clicks on the pane-close `X` in the 24pt header AND the settings-panel `X` (top-trailing of the body when the FCSIT panel is open) reach the buttons instead of being intercepted by the resize handle. The pane-close `X` itself already had a 44pt-class hit target via `.frame(14×14).padding(15).contentShape(Rectangle())` (`SenkaniApp/Views/PaneContainerView.swift:244-256`) — that wasn't the bug. The bug was that the resize handle's hit region ran the full column height and sat directly on top of the close button.
- **Why now:** Finding #F from the `release-v0-3-0-onboarding-pass` 2026-05-14 walk. Operator quote during the AC #4 closeout: *"(btw — clicking the x was hard because of the right-side drag bar, but after finangling I was able to close it)"*. The walk completed by sidestepping the collision (`+ Add Project` to surface a fresh Welcome view from a no-panes project), but the close-pane UX is the only operator-side path to reach the Welcome view from inside a workstream — workstreams auto-provision a Terminal at create-time, so the no-panes state is unreachable without closing the auto-spawn. Sharp edge had to land in v0.3.0.
- **Test coverage:** 3 new swift-testing cases in `Tests/SenkaniTests/PaneRightEdgeHandleGeometryTests.swift` — source-level guards because `SenkaniTests` cannot link the `SenkaniApp` target. `topExclusionInsetClearsCloseButtons` parses `SenkaniTheme.swift` and asserts the inset is ≥ `activeAccentLineHeight + headerHeight + 0.5 (separator) + 8 (settings-panel-X top padding) + 14 (settings-panel-X icon height)` — i.e. ≥ 49pt today, with the constant set to 60pt for safety margin. `handleViewReferencesNamedConstant` asserts `PaneGridView.swift` applies the inset via the named constant rather than a magic numeric literal — a future refactor that hard-codes `60` will fail this test. `paneCloseButtonHitTargetIsLargeEnough` regex-asserts the `Image("xmark").frame(14×14).padding(15).contentShape(Rectangle())` chain remains intact on the close button so the 44pt hit shape doesn't shrink. Test count: 2662 → 2665 (+3); full chunked suite green (8/8 chunks pass).
- **Out of scope:** AppKit-level NSEvent hit-test diagnostics — the named-constant + invariant test is sufficient guard for the geometry. Real interactive verification belongs in a future Cowork-runnable walk (operator clicks the `X` at min-column (180pt) and max-column (900pt) widths and confirms it closes the pane on the first click). Filing this as a follow-up walk item is not warranted today — the geometry invariant covers every column width because the close button is anchored to the right edge of the header strip and the exclusion inset is anchored to the column's top.

- **What ships:** 2 new swift-testing cases under `Tests/SenkaniTests/OnboardingMilestoneTests.swift`. `canonicalRawValueSpellingIsPinned` maps every `OnboardingMilestone` case to its expected literal `String` rawValue (`projectSelected`, `agentLaunched`, `firstTrackedEvent`, **`firstNonzeroSavings` — lowercase `z`**, `firstBudgetSet`, `firstWorkstreamCreated`, `firstStagedProposalReviewed`); a future case rename now must come through this explicit per-case pin instead of a silent edit to the `enumOrderIsStable` array. `storeIgnoresUnknownOnDiskKeys` hand-writes a `~/.senkani/onboarding/milestones.json` that mixes one canonical key, one hypothetical legacy capital-`Z` key, and one totally-unknown key, then asserts only the canonical key surfaces through `OnboardingMilestoneStore.completed(...)` — pinning the `OnboardingMilestone(rawValue: key)` graceful-drop guard at `Sources/Core/OnboardingMilestoneStore.swift:167` as durable behavior.
- **Why now:** Finding #D from the `release-v0-3-0-onboarding-pass` 2026-05-14 walk surfaced a casing discrepancy between operator-written AC text (`firstNonZeroSavings`, capital `Z`) and the actual recorder output (`firstNonzeroSavings`, lowercase `z`). Pre-audit grep across all four source roots (`Sources/`, `SenkaniApp/`, `Tests/`, `tools/`) confirmed canonical is **`firstNonzeroSavings`** (lowercase `z`) — declared at `Sources/Core/OnboardingMilestone.swift:25`, used by every call site (`SessionDatabase+TokenEventAPI.swift:119`, `BudgetConfig.swift:303`, `LaunchCoordinator.swift:66`, `SprintReviewViewModel.swift:242,261`, `SprintReviewSeedFixture.swift:65`), and present in every existing on-disk evidence file under `tools/soak/evidence/onboarding-pass-milestones-4-7/`. The drift was purely a typo in operator-written AC text in the closed luminary-walk file; recorder and on-disk reality have always been canonical. ### May 14 — Onboarding milestone recorder: lost-update race serialized; predecessor-chain ownership documented (`onboarding-milestone-recorder-gap-projectSelected-agentLaunched-2026-05-14`)

- **What ships:** `OnboardingMilestoneStore.record(_:at:home:env:)` (`Sources/Core/OnboardingMilestoneStore.swift`) now runs its entire read-modify-write under a new file-private `NSRecursiveLock` (`recordLock`). Before this round, the `completed(home:)` read and the subsequent `write(_:home:)` were not serialized — two concurrent records on different milestones from the same process could each read the same baseline, mutate their own snapshot, and write back, with last-write-wins silently dropping one of the updates (classic TOCTOU). The lock closes that hole within a process; the on-disk side was already atomic via temp-file + `replaceItemAt`. Type-level docstring grew an "Atomicity contract" section that pins (a) in-process serialization, (b) on-disk rename-atomicity, (c) once-only semantics enforced inside the lock, (d) the accepted cross-process limitation, and (e) the explicit separation between Store (passive observer) and `OnboardingMilestoneProgression` (chain-reasoning owner).
- **Why now:** Finding #I from the `release-v0-3-0-onboarding-pass` 2026-05-14 walk surfaced that `milestones.json` had lost `projectSelected` and `agentLaunched` between 2026-05-11 (when both were recorded) and 2026-05-14 (walk-resume), while `firstTrackedEvent` (recorded at roughly the same time as the missing two) survived. The most consequential read of the finding is data-integrity in the very system AC #4 validates. Even if the specific 2026-05-11→2026-05-14 disappearance turns out to have been an operator `rm -f` or partial-uninstall (rather than a lost-update race), the recorder's TOCTOU is a live latent bug independent of that incident. Fixing it pre-emptively unblocks any future onboarding-pass walk that fires the SwiftUI-side and Core-side milestone callsites concurrently (the common path on a fresh install: `WorkspaceModel.addProject` + `LaunchCoordinator.launchPane` + `SessionDatabase.recordTokenEvent` can all fire within milliseconds of each other once the operator clicks the first task starter).
- **Predecessor-chain decision:** the recorder is now explicitly documented as a passive observer that does NOT enforce ordering. AC #3 of the closing item proposed either (a) backfill predecessors or (b) refuse out-of-order records — both rejected because the chain logic already lives in `OnboardingMilestoneProgression.next(after:)`, which surfaces the lowest-order missing milestone to the UI regardless of which keys are present on disk. Backfill would fabricate timestamps; refusal would silently drop legitimate observations the operator deliberately triggered. The chosen approach is the third option: lock the read-modify-write so concurrent records cannot lose each other's update, then trust Progression to drive the UI's "next" cue when the operator's on-disk state is out of order (e.g. after an `rm -f` reset).
- **Test coverage:** 2 new swift-testing cases under `Tests/SenkaniTests/OnboardingMilestoneTests.swift`. `recordIsSerializedAcrossConcurrentMilestones` fires 16 concurrent records per milestone (112 tasks total) via `withTaskGroup` and asserts all 7 keys land on disk — exercises the race that the lock closes. `recordDoesNotEnforcePredecessorChain` records `firstTrackedEvent` against a fresh home, asserts only that key persists (no backfill, no refusal), and asserts `OnboardingMilestoneProgression.summary(...)` still surfaces `projectSelected` as `next` — pins the Store-vs-Progression separation as the durable contract. Test count: 2658 → 2660 (+2); full chunked suite green (8/8 chunks pass).
- **Out of scope:** the diagnostic bisect that AC #1 nominally asked for (replay the operator's 2026-05-11 → 2026-05-13 timeline to identify the exact event that wiped `projectSelected` / `agentLaunched`) — the evidence trail doesn't carry enough state to do a deterministic bisect, and the fix (lock + documentation) closes the data-integrity hole regardless of which past event triggered the loss. Cross-process serialization is documented as an accepted limitation; the senkani CLI and SenkaniApp GUI fire disjoint milestone sets in practice, so the race is theoretical, and the right fix if it ever surfaces is `flock(2)` on the parent dir or single-owner-process routing (not a within-this-round change).

### May 13 — `budget.json` partial-schema decode resilience (`onboarding-milestone-5-budget-decoder-partial-schema-2026-05-13`)

- **What ships:** `BudgetConfig` (`Sources/Core/BudgetConfig.swift`) replaces auto-synthesized `Codable` with an explicit `init(from:)` + `encode(to:)` that uses `decodeIfPresent(...) ?? <default>` for every non-Optional property. A `~/.senkani/budget.json` that sets a real limit but omits `softLimitPercent` (or any future-added non-Optional field) now decodes cleanly with the property's Swift-side default — Swift's auto-synthesized decoder treats every non-Optional stored property as a required JSON key regardless of `= <default>`, which silently dropped partial-schema files into the `loadFromEnv()` fallback path.
- **Why now:** the 2026-05-13 re-walk of `release-v0-3-0-onboarding-pass-milestones-4-7-walk-2026-05-11` exposed two compounding harms: (1) onboarding-milestone false-negative — a user writing `{"perSessionLimitCents":500}` and expecting `firstBudgetSet` to fire was blocked by `keyNotFound(softLimitPercent, …)`, `loadFromEnv()` returned all-nil limits, `isNonDefault` was false, the Welcome banner stalled at "Set a budget" against the user's actual on-disk state; (2) silent budget bypass — the user believed their $5/session cap was enforced when in reality no limits were active because env vars weren't set either. Security/billing posture issue, not just UX.
- **Test coverage:** 6 new swift-testing cases under `Tests/SenkaniTests/BudgetConfigTests.swift` — partial-schema decode with default fill, partial-schema `isNonDefault`, empty-object decode, encode→decode round-trip preservation, encoder emits `softLimitPercent` always and omits nil limits, `loadFromDisk` end-to-end fires `.firstBudgetSet` on a partial-schema file. The existing `OnboardingMilestoneCallsiteTests.loadFromDiskFiresFirstBudgetSet` "default file" fixture switched from `{"softLimitPercent":0.8}` to `{}` to exercise the resilience path directly. Test count: 2570 → 2576 (+6); full suite green.
- **Scope of fallback path unchanged:** the corrupt-JSON `logWarning` + `loadFromEnv()` fallback at `Sources/Core/BudgetConfig.swift:277-280` stays in place for genuinely-malformed files; only partial-schema-but-valid-JSON files now decode successfully. The post-decode validation block (`perSessionLimitCents < 0`, `softLimitPercent out of [0,1]`, etc.) still runs after the explicit init. Encoded shape is byte-stable for fully-specified configs — existing on-disk files keep decoding through the explicit path.

### May 13 — Sprint Review seeder for deterministic onboarding walks (`onboarding-milestone-7-sprint-review-seeder-2026-05-13`)

When the operator opens SenkaniApp's Sprint Review pane and clicks Accept or Reject on the seeded row, `SprintReviewViewModel.accept`/`.reject` fires `OnboardingMilestoneStore.record(.firstStagedProposalReviewed)` through the **unchanged** call site at `Sources/Core/SprintReviewViewModel.swift:242,261` — the seeder pre-populates the store, it does not bypass the milestone code path.

Without a deterministic seeder, step 6 (Accept/Reject) was unreachable on demand and the walk had to pause indefinitely. This subcommand is the canonical step-5 unblocker so future re-walks don't depend on accumulated real Claude session activity to test the milestone path. - **Test coverage:** 3 new swift-testing cases under `Tests/SenkaniTests/SprintReviewSeedFixtureTests.swift` — seed→accept fires the milestone through the unchanged dispatch (acceptance criterion), `--force` overrides the already-completed guard, synthetic-id collision skip.

### May 13 — Savings-pipeline two-part instrumentation lands (Fix path 5) (`savings-pipeline-two-part-instrumentation-2026-05-12`)

- **What ships:** the P0 follow-up to the May-12 walk's Fix path 5
  routing. Two coordinated edits restore `OnboardingMilestone.firstNonzeroSavings`
  fire eligibility on the `claude_session` writer path and surface the
  `mcp_tool` compression-delta failure mode as a structured log event.
- **Part A — `ClaudeSessionWatcher` derives `savedTokens` from JSONL
  `cache_read_input_tokens`.** The realtime tail in
  `SenkaniApp/Services/ClaudeSessionWatcher.swift:147` previously had
  its own copy of the JSONL parser that hardcoded `savedTokens: 0`
  (line 181 in the pre-fix shape). That parser is now extracted as
  `ClaudeSessionReader.parseAssistantUsageLine(_:)` in
  `Sources/Core/ClaudeSessionReader.swift:68`, consumed by both the
  watcher and the existing `ClaudeSessionReader.readNew` cursor-driven
  path so the `cache_read_input_tokens → savedTokens` mapping has a
  single source of truth that future contributors can't accidentally
  reintroduce a divergent copy of.
- **Part B — `MCPSession.recordMetrics` emits compression-delta
  diagnostics.** Two-tier emission added at
  `Sources/MCP/Session/MCPSession.swift:982`:
  - `mcp.metrics.compression_negative` fires UNCONDITIONALLY when
    `savedBytes <= 0` (raw_bytes / compressed_bytes / saved_bytes /
    tool_name / feature / command), so the cases where compression
    underperforms surface in operator stderr without configuration.
  - `mcp.metrics.recorded` fires per-call when
    `SENKANI_SAVINGS_DEBUG=1` (env-cached via `MCPSession.savingsDebugEnabled`,
    matching the `Logger.isJSON` cache pattern), for diagnostic
    deep-dives where every recordMetrics entry needs inspection.
- **Tests delta:** +8 (4 in `Tests/SenkaniTests/AgentTrackingTests.swift`
  pin the parser contract incl. `parseAssistantUsageExtractsCacheReadTokens`
  with a fixture `cache_read_input_tokens: 1234`; 4 in
  `Tests/SenkaniTests/MCPSessionTests.swift` under
  `@Suite("MCP Session recordMetrics diagnostics", .serialized, .loggerSinkGate)`
  pin the negative-delta diagnostic + env-gated verbose paths). Full

  `swift build -c debug` exit 0 in 141.42 s (zero errors);
  `swift test` exit 0 in 228 s with **2559 tests passed in
  12.978 s** of execution. No Package.swift / Package.resolved
  mutations; pin-rationale block at `Package.swift:23-69` preserved
  verbatim. Hypothesis #4 (FileProvider eviction) confirmed; #1
  (debug-vs-release conditional) ruled out by direct discriminator
  evidence.
- **Downstream:** unblocks `test-suite-flake-reverification-2026-05-07`

### May 11 — `TreeSitterCppTests` C++ parse-time perf gate widened 10 ms → 20 ms (`treesitter-cpp-parse-perf-gate-flake-2026-05-11`)

  parent-finding round close on 2026-05-11 hit `median 0.013278708 s >
  0.01 s` on the operator's Mac. On-hardware bench (30 samples) showed
  per-sample p50 ~1.5 ms, p95 ~4.5 ms, p99 ~6.8 ms under full-suite

  path — `TreeSitterBackend.index` is called synchronously without
  the wrap, so wrap-spawn-cost was never a factor for this gate).
- Validation: 5 consecutive full-suite runs (2551 tests each) on
  operator hardware, all green. C++ perf test passed in 3.16-3.77 s
  wall-clock (test-method wall, including the 3 internal samples and
  framework overhead) every run.
- Suite: 2551 → 2551 (gate widened, no test added/removed).

### May 11 — `tools/soak/runner/08-make-app-bundle.command` always rebuilds (`soak-bundle-script-stale-binary-rebuild-2026-05-11`)

- **Why:** The bundle script gated its build on `[ ! -x .build/debug/SenkaniApp ]` —
  so an iterative debug cycle that edited `SenkaniApp/App/*.swift` and re-ran
  the script silently re-bundled the pre-edit binary. The operator believed
  they bundled the fix; they actually bundled the bug. The `.app` then
  "reproduced" the bug they thought they fixed, burning ~20 minutes per
  ghost-bug debug loop (this was the parent finding from
  `app-bundle-launchservices-isatty-fallback-2026-05-10`'s fix-verification
  cycle on 2026-05-11). The redundant-build cost of unconditional rebuild is
  ~seconds (SwiftPM's incremental build is correct on no-changes); the
  ghost-bug cost is minutes. Bad trade — gate removed.
- `tools/soak/runner/08-make-app-bundle.command` now invokes
  `swift build --product SenkaniApp` unconditionally, aborts with non-zero
  exit if the build fails to produce `$APP_BIN`, and echoes the bundled
  binary's mtime (`Bundled binary built at <ISO>`) so the operator can
  confirm at a glance which version got bundled.
- Audited companion soak-runner scripts for the same gate-on-existence
  shape: `06-launch-binary.command` has a similar `if [ ! -x $APP_BIN ]`
  but its contract is explicitly "launch pre-built binary" — different
  semantic class (it falls back to release when debug is missing, never
  rebuilds), so no defect filed. `13-step7-and-tarball.command` only
  verifies state — no build path.
- Validation: injected `SENKANI_BUNDLE_REBUILD_MARKER_8c2f4a1e` into
  `SenkaniApp/App/main.swift`, ran `swift build --product SenkaniApp`,
  confirmed marker present in `.build/debug/SenkaniApp` (count=1). Reverted
  the marker, rebuilt, confirmed marker absent (count=0). SwiftPM picks
  up source edits in both directions.
- Suite: operator-tooling shell script only — no test-count change.

### May 11 — Indexer CLI entry points run on a large-stack background Thread (`indexer-cli-entry-points-large-stack-thread-2026-05-11`)

- **Why:** Closes the stack-guard asymmetry filed off the
  `mcp-warmindex-treesitter-walk-stack-overflow-2026-05-10` ship.
  `MCPSession.ensureIndex` already wrapped `IndexStore.buildOrUpdate`
  in `runOnLargeStackThread` (16 MB) so AST walks can't smash the
  cooperative pool's 544 KB stack — but the CLI entry points
  (`senkani index`, `senkani bundle`, `senkani bundle --rebuild-index`,
  cold-bundle fallback) were still running on the main thread's 8 MB
  stack. Comfortable for any realistic AST, but not infinite — a
  pathological TS/Swift AST against an external repo via `senkani
  index /path/to/big-monorepo` could still trap. Symmetry restored.
- Hoisted `Senkani` root command and `Index` / `BundleCommand`
  subcommands from `ParsableCommand` to `AsyncParsableCommand`.
  ArgumentParser's mixed-roster dispatcher (`AsyncParsableCommand.main()`
  in swift-argument-parser 1.3.0+) calls async `run()` for the two
  converted subcommands, sync `run()` for the other 28 — no change to
  the rest of the CLI surface.
- Each of the four `IndexStore.buildOrUpdate` call sites in
  `Sources/CLI/{IndexCommand,BundleCommand}.swift` now wraps the
  build in `await runOnLargeStackThread { ... }`. Removed the
  semaphore-trick `runAsync` helper in `BundleCommand` (used only by
  the remote-fetch path) — `try await BundleComposer.fetchRemote(...)`
  is called directly now that `run()` is async, removing one of the
  deadlock surfaces flagged in the warmindex round.
- `IndexStore.buildOrUpdate` itself stays synchronous — wrapping
  happens at the four entry sites, not inside the utility. Contract
  documented in `RunOnLargeStackThread.swift`'s doc-comment so future
  CLI commands that build the index can't reintroduce the gap.
- Suite: thread-routing refactor with no test-count change; existing
  CLISmokeTests + Bundle* coverage applies. Full `./tools/test-safe.sh`
  green across all 8 chunks (1186 tests in chunk[other] alone).
- Out of scope (filed separately):
  `indexer-backends-iterative-walk-refactor-2026-05-11` is the proper
  long-term fix — iterative AST walks with depth caps. This round
  only adds the thread-level guard.

### May 11 — `senkani doctor` FileProvider eviction scanner emits relative paths consistently (`doctor-fileprovider-eviction-star2-path-mismatch-2026-05-11`)

- **Why:** `DoctorFileProviderEvictionTests.swift:163` was failing
  because `FileProviderEvictionScanner.scan(root:)` emitted absolute
  paths under temp roots — `URL(fileURLWithPath:).path` canonicalizes
  `/var/folders/.../T/...` to `/private/var/folders/.../T/...` during
  enumeration, but the prefix-trim used the unresolved `root` string
  passed in. The `hasPrefix(root + "/")` check fell through, hit the
  silent `else { star2Siblings.append(path) }` fallback, and the
  contract ("paths relative to project root") quietly broke. Test
  caught it; operator-facing behavior on real project paths was
  unaffected (no `/var` ↔ `/private/var` divergence on `~/Desktop/…`).
- Fix in `Sources/CLI/FileProviderEvictionCheck.swift`: resolve `root`

### May 11 — Two-bug fix: SenkaniApp first-launch crash (`mcp-warmindex-treesitter-walk-stack-overflow-2026-05-10`, `app-bundle-launchservices-isatty-fallback-2026-05-10`)

- **Bug 1 — Stack-guard crash in `MCPSession.warmIndex`.** Tree-sitter
  language backends and `DependencyExtractor` recurse on AST depth.
  Real Go/TS/Swift files routinely produce ASTs ~200+ levels deep,
  past Swift Concurrency's cooperative-pool ~544 KB stack. Symptom on
  fresh install: `EXC_BAD_ACCESS (SIGILL)` 286 frames into
  `GoBackend.walk`, app dies before the welcome screen.
- Fixed at the entry points (single-point structural fix, no per-
  backend rewrite required): new
  `Sources/Indexer/RunOnLargeStackThread.swift` helper spawns a fresh
  `Thread` with a 16 MB stack and runs the AST work on it. Applied
  to all four cooperative-pool call sites in `MCPSession.swift`
  (`warmIndex` incremental, `warmIndex` full, `ensureIndex`,
  `handleFileChanges`). The 23 indexer backends + 2
  `DependencyExtractor` sites remain unchanged; the wrapped entry
  points are now the only paths AST work reaches them through.
  Deep-analysis punch list (every site checked + verdict) lives in
  the backlog item's `## Execution evidence`.
- **Bug 2 — LaunchServices launches misrouted to MCP mode.**
  `SenkaniApp/App/main.swift:11` used `isatty(STDIN_FILENO) == 0` as a
  fallback to detect MCP-server mode. Every `open SenkaniApp.app` /
  Spotlight / dock launch hands stdin=`/dev/null` to the child, so
  the heuristic fired and the binary entered `MCPServerRunner.run()`
  instead of `SenkaniGUI.main()`. The recursion crash masked this:
  post-fix, LS launches "open and exit cleanly" instead of crashing,
  because the MCP gate denied on missing `pane_id`.
- Dropped the `isatty` fallback; MCP mode now requires an explicit
  `--mcp-server` flag. The dedicated `senkani-mcp` binary (registered
  by `MCPInstallCommand.swift`) is what Claude Code uses, so the
  fallback was never needed for production.
- Process learning: SKILL.md gains a mandatory "similar-issue scan"
  step in the build-mode close phase. The GoBackend crash was one of
  23 sibling sites; shipping only the Go fix would have left every
  other language vulnerable. The new step requires an `Explore`-agent
  deep scan before doc-sync, with results recorded in the item's
  evidence.
- Defects-outside-criteria filed:
  `fcsit-pane-toggles-ux-redesign-2026-05-11` (UX rethink — operator
  observation),
  `uninstall-scanner-userdefaults-preferences-gap-2026-05-11`
  (10th-category gap: `~/Library/Preferences/dev.senkani.app.plist`
  not wiped by `senkani uninstall --yes`).
